item.name: sonPolicyId

item.desc: This parameter sets the service type, 21 for PnP, 26 for SH, 43 for CS, 46 for ANR, 47 for PCI, 48 for X2, 49 for MRO, 50 for CCO, 51 for RO, 52 for MLB, 57 for ES, and 58 for MAGICRADIO.
item.name: sonFuncId

item.desc: Run Mode
item.name: sonRunMode

item.desc: This parameter is the DTX energy saving switch. When it is set to Open, the DTX function is enabled. When it is set to Close, the DTX function is disabled.
item.name: esDTXSwitch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables symbol shutdown based on MBSFN subframes.
item.name: esEDTXSwch

item.desc: This parameter indicates the mode of RRU self-checking. If an RRU supports self-checking, the RRU can perform symbol power judgment by baseband dispatch when this parameter is set to Enhanced RRU Self-Check. Otherwise, it means RRU perform symbol judgment by itself. If RRU does not support self-checking, this parameter is invalid.
item.name: notifyBBFlag

item.desc: The 24 hours starting from 00:00 in a day are divided into 96 periods, each of which is 15 minutes. This parameter is an array consisting of 96 elements. From the first element, the array indicates whether symbol shutdown for energy saving is allowed during a period of 15 minutes starting from 00:00 on a weekday (Monday to Friday). If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that symbol shutdown for energy saving is not allowed during the corresponding period. If this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that symbol shutdown for energy saving is allowed during the corresponding period.
item.name: weekdayDTXEsTime

item.desc: The 24 hours starting from 00:00 in a day are divided into 96 periods, each of which is 15 minutes. This parameter is an array consisting of 96 elements. From the first element, the array indicates whether symbol shutdown for energy saving is allowed during a period of 15 minutes starting from 00:00 on a Saturday or Sunday. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that symbol shutdown for energy saving is not allowed during the corresponding period. If this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that symbol shutdown for energy saving is allowed during the corresponding period.
item.name: weekendDTXEsTime

item.desc: The 24 hours starting from 00:00 in a day are divided into 96 periods, each of which is 15 minutes. This parameter is an array consisting of 96 elements. From the first element, the array indicates whether symbol shutdown for energy saving is allowed during a period of 15 minutes starting from 00:00 on a special day. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that symbol shutdown for energy saving is not allowed during the corresponding period. If this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that symbol shutdown for energy saving is allowed during the corresponding period.
item.name: specialDTXEsTime

item.desc: MAC Statistic Interval
item.name: rbInterval

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of RB usage for closing subframes. When the RB usage is lower than the threshold, subframes can be closed; otherwise, subframes cannot be closed.
item.name: thrClose

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of RB usage for opening subframes. When the RB usage is higher than the threshold, subframes can be opened; otherwise, subframes cannot be opened.
item.name: thrOpen

item.desc: If the load meets the cycle requirement specified by this parameter for consecutive times, the subframes are shut down.
item.name: dtxOffDetectNumber

item.desc: If the load meets the cycle requirement specified by this parameter for consecutive times, the subframes are switched on.
item.name: dtxOnDetectNumber

item.desc: This parameter indicates whether to consider QCI5 users or not. If the switch is open, the subframe should not be closed and the closed subframe need to be opened while the QCI5 users exist; otherwise, it has no effect on the closed subframe.
item.name: qci5Swch

item.desc: This parameter indicates the maximum number of subframes that can be closed when the subframe is to be closed. If the number of subframe that can be closed is greater than this prameter value, the closing subframes number is equal to this parameter value; otherwise, the closed subframes number is equal to the number of sunframe which can be closed.
item.name: maxCloseFrameNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the time at which the energy saving period policies are changed. It is configured based on hours. For example, the parameter value 20 indicates 20:00 p. M. If the energy saving period involves different day types (weekdays, weekends, and special days), different energy saving period policies are applied before and after this parameter is set. For example, if Friday is a boundary day between the weekday energy saving period policy and the weekend energy saving period policy, the weekday energy saving period policy takes effect from 0:00 on Friday to the time specified by this parameter, and the weekend energy saving period policy takes effect from the time specified by this parameter to 0:00 next day.
item.name: esPolicySwchTime

item.desc: If this parameter is set to Open, the conversion of PRBs occupied by the NGBR service is implemented; otherwise, the conversion is not implemented.
item.name: ngbrPrbConvSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the RF shutdown function for energy saving.
item.name: rfShutdownSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the channel shutdown time for energy saving from Monday through Friday every week. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a day (from Monday through Friday) and indicates whether channel shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, channel shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, channel shutdown for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: weekdayChannelEsTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the channel shutdown time for energy saving on Saturday and Sunday every week. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a day (Saturday or Sunday) and indicates whether channel shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, channel shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, channel shutdown for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: weekendChannelEsTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the channel shutdown time for energy saving on special days. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a special day and indicates whether channel shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The start time of a special day is specified by the specialStarTimeES (Special Date Start Time of Energy Saving) parameter and the end time of a special day is specified by the specialEndTimeES (Special Date End Time of Energy Saving) parameter. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, channel shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, channel shutdown for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: specialChannelEsTime

item.desc: The parameter sets the time window of switching off for channel off.
item.name: rfShutdownDelayTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink load threshold for triggering channel shutdown for energy saving. It is one of the conditions for triggering channel shutdown for energy saving. If the downlink load on the cell is lower than this threshold, channel shutdown can be triggered for the cell.
item.name: trdLoadOffChanESDown

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink load percentage threshold in the case of channel shutdown deactivation. When the downlink load on the cell is higher than or equal to the threshold, channel shutdown is deactivated and services in the cell are recovered.
item.name: trdLoadOnChanESDown

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink load threshold for triggering channel shutdown for energy saving. It is one of the conditions for triggering channel shutdown for energy saving. If the uplink load on the cell is lower than this threshold, channel shutdown can be triggered for the cell.
item.name: trdLoadOffChanESUp

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink load threshold for deactivating channel shutdown. When the uplink load on the cell is higher than the threshold, channel shutdown for energy saving is deactivated and services in the cell are recovered.
item.name: trdLoadOnChanESUp

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum tolerable number of UEs in RRC_CONNECTED status when the channel is shut down. When the number of UEs in RRC_CONNECTED status is lower than the threshold, the channel is allowed to be shut down; otherwise, the channel is not allowed to be shut down.
item.name: trdNumUEOffChanES

item.desc: This parameter indicates the number of UEs in RRC_CONNECTED status when a channel is shut down. If the number of UEs in RRC_CONNECTED status is larger than or equal to this threshold, channel shutdown is not allowed; otherwise, carrier shutdown is allowed.
item.name: trdNumUEOnChanES

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of voice users allowed when the channel is shut down. When the number of voice service users is lower than the threshold, the channel is allowed to be shut down; otherwise, the carrier is not allowed to be shut down.
item.name: volteUeNumThrdChanneloff

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of voice users allowed when the channel is awakened. If the number of voice users is larger than or equal to the threshold, the channel is awakened immediately; otherwise, the channel is not wakened.
item.name: volteUeNumThrdChannelon

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration of the timer for load detection after a channel is shut down. When the system starts a periodic detection on system load and the number of UEs, this timer is started. Before the timer times out, the system calculates the system load and counts the number of UEs. After the timer times out, the system checks whether the number of times that the channel is woken up is larger than or equal to the threshold. If yes, the system shuts down the channel. If not, the system continues the detection.
item.name: rfsdWakeupTimerLen

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval of channel shutdown. It is used to control the time when another channel shutdown occurs after the previous channel shutdown occurred. When another channel shutdown occurs after the previous channel shutdown occurred, this timer is started. Before the timer times out, channel energy-saving detection is not performed. After the timer times out, channel energy-saving detection starts.
item.name: allowedTimeChanES

item.desc: This parameter indicates the number of detected PRBs in the case of channel-on. If the number of detected PRBs in the case of channel-off is larger than or equal to this configured value, the channel is woken up.
item.name: rfWakeupTimeWinNumPrb

item.desc: This parameter indicates the number of detected UEs in RRC_CONNECTED state in the case of channel-on. If the number of detected UEs in RRC_CONNECTED state in the case of channel-off is larger than or equal to this configured value, the channel is woken up.
item.name: rfWakeupTimeWinNumRrc

item.desc: This parameter sets a channel shutdown method. If this parameter is set to 0 (Shutdown Port), channels are shut down by port. If this parameter is set to 1 (Shutdown Half of Ants of One Port), the channels corresponding to Port1 and Port2 are shut down in a 4Port configuration scenario and half of the antennas of each port are shut down in a 2Port configuration scenario.
item.name: channeloffMethods

item.desc: This parameter is used to select the method for the shutdown of eight antennas and two ports. If it is set to 0, method 1 for antenna shutdown is selected. If it is set to 1, method 2 for antenna shutdown is selected.
item.name: antennaoffMethods8

item.desc: This parameter is used to select the method for the shutdown of four antennas and two ports. If it is set to 0, method 1 for antenna shutdown is selected. If it is set to 1, method 2 for antenna shutdown is selected.
item.name: antennaoffMethods4

item.desc: This parameter sets the pattern of 8-antenna FDD channel shutdown. If it is set to 0, it indicates that channel shutdown pattern 1 is used. If it is set to 1, it indicates that channel shutdown pattern 2 is used. By querying the mapping relationship carried by the anttoport field in the baseband resource, you can determine the information about CRS port shutdown corresponding to the selected channel shutdown pattern.
item.name: rruChShutdownPattern

item.desc: The parameter is used to determine the adjust power offset of CRS.
item.name: crsPowerAdjust

item.desc: This parameter indicates the mode of MM cell channel off. The value of the parameter is set to Close DL. When channel shutdown, only the downlink transmit power is turned off. If the parameter value is set to Close DL and UL, the uplink and downlink transmit powers are turned off when channel shutdown.
item.name: chOffMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the proportion of the antennas that are shut down when the channel of an MM cell is shut down.
item.name: chOffRatio

item.desc: This parameter sets an energy-saving function. Compared with the effect of carrier shutdown (this parameter is set to 0), the effect of enhanced carrier shutdown (this parameter is set to 1) is better. However, in the latter case, it takes a longer time for a cell to resume operation after it exits the energy-saving status.
item.name: carrierShutdownMode

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the energy saving function.
item.name: esSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the load evaluation mode for carrier shutdown. If it is set to Non Load Evaluation, carrier shutdown is triggered at the specified time. If it is set to Evaluation ES Cell, carrier shutdown is triggered as long as the load of the energy-saving cell meets the load condition. If it is set to Evaluation ES Cell and Coverage Cell, carrier shutdown can be triggered only when both the load of the energy-saving cell and the cell providing coverage meets the load condition.
item.name: carrierESLBEvaluateMod

item.desc: This parameter sets the carrier shutdown time for energy saving from Monday through Friday every week. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a day (from Monday through Friday) and indicates whether carrier shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, carrier shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, carrier shutdown for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: weekdayCarrierEsTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the carrier shutdown time for energy saving on Saturday and Sunday every week. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a day (Saturday or Sunday) and indicates whether carrier shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, carrier shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, carrier shutdown for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: weekendCarrierEsTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the carrier shutdown time for energy saving on special days. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a special day and indicates whether carrier shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The start time of a special day is specified by the specialStarTimeES (Special Date Start Time of Energy Saving) parameter and the end time of a special day is specified by the specialEndTimeES (Special Date End Time of Energy Saving) parameter. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, carrier shutdown for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, carrier shutdown for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: specialCarrierEsTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink load threshold for the cell to enter energy-saving state. It is one of the conditions for checking whether the cell enters energy-saving state. When the uplink load of the cell is smaller than this threshold, the current cell can enter energy-saving state.
item.name: trdLoadESUp

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink load threshold for the cell to enter energy-saving state. It is one of the conditions for checking whether the cell enters energy-saving state. When the downlink load of the cell is smaller than this threshold, the cell can enter energy-saving state.
item.name: trdLoadESDown

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink load threshold of compensation cells after energy-saving cells enter energy-saving state. When the sum of the uplink load of a compensation cell and that of an energy-saving cell is smaller than this threshold, the eNodeB triggers the energy-saving cell to enter energy-saving state.
item.name: resPRBUp

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink load threshold of compensation cells after energy-saving cells enter energy-saving state. When the sum of the downlink load of a compensation cell and that of an energy-saving cell is smaller than this threshold, the eNodeB triggers the energy-saving cell to enter energy-saving state.
item.name: resPRBDown

item.desc: This parameter set the maximum number of UEs with data services in the case of intra-RAT carrier shutdown of energy saving cells. If the number of UEs with data services in an energy saving cell is smaller than this threshold, carrier shutdown is allowed for the energy saving cell.
item.name: numTrdTotalUE

item.desc: This parameter indicates the threshold tolerance of the number of VoLTE UEs when a carrier is shut down in an energy saving cell. If the number of UEs with VoLTE services is less than this threshold, carrier shutdown is allowed; otherwise, carrier shutdown is not allowed.
item.name: volteUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter indicates the time window for observing the load on a cell after the cell is switched off.
item.name: switchoffTimeWindow

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval of LTE carrier shutdown. It is used to control the time when another carrier shutdown occurs after the previous carrier shutdown occurred. When another carrier shutdown occurs after the previous carrier shutdown occurred, this timer is started. Before the timer times out, carrier shutdown detection for energy-saving is not performed. After the timer times out, carrier shutdown detection for energy-saving starts.
item.name: intervalESTimerLen

item.desc: This parameter sets the load conversion factor of carrier shutdown for energy saving. In the case of channel shutdown for energy saving, cell load needs to be converted for load check in carrier shutdown for energy saving. In this case, this conversion factor is used for load conversion.
item.name: loadConversionFactor

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables carrier shutdown of cells in a high-speed railway scenario for energy saving.
item.name: highWayESSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the period during which no train travels in the coverage of carriers in a high-speed railway scenario where carrier shutdown for energy saving is enabled. During the configured period, carriers are shut down by default for energy saving.
item.name: highWayIdleStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the period during which no train travels in the coverage of carriers in a high-speed railway scenario where carrier shutdown for energy saving is enabled. During the configured period, carriers are shut down by default for energy saving.
item.name: highWayIdleEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the delay in carrier shutdown after a high-speed train leaves the high-speed railway cell. It is used to shut down carriers after a period when a notification indicating that a high-speed train leaves the high-speed railway cell is received to ensure user experience in the cell. When a carrier is shut down with a period of delay after a high-speed train leaves the high-speed railway cell, this timer is started. After the timer times out, carrier shutdown starts.
item.name: carrierShutDownDelayTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the period for forced wakeup of the shutdown carriers in a high-speed railway scenario. After the carriers are shut down, they are forced to wake up if no train travels in the coverage of the carriers within this period.
item.name: carrierForcedWakeUpTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration of the penalty timer after a high-speed railway cell is forcibly woken up from carrier shutdown. When a high-speed railway cell is forcibly woken up, the timer is started. During the operation of the timer, if the cell receives a vehicle arrival and departure message, the cell can enter the carrier shutdown state for energy saving again. Otherwise, the cell cannot enter carrier shutdown state. After the timer expires, the system determines whether to start carrier shutdown in accordance with the vehicle status of the serving cell and neighbor cells. If neither the serving cell nor neighbor cells have vehicles, the serving cell can start carrier shutdown. Otherwise, the serving cell cannot enter carrier shutdown state.
item.name: penaltyTime

item.desc: This parameter sets an energy-saving function. Compared with the effect of deep sleep (this parameter is set to 0), the effect of enhanced deep sleep (this parameter is set to 1) is better. However, in the latter case, it takes a longer time for a sleeping cell to resume operation after it exits the energy-saving status.
item.name: deepSleepMode

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables deep sleep in a cell for energy saving.
item.name: sleepEsSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the load evaluation mode for deep sleeping. If it is set to Non Load Evaluation, deep sleeping is triggered at the specified time. If it is set to Evaluation ES Cell, deep sleeping is triggered as long as the load of the energy-saving cell meets the load condition. If it is set to Evaluation ES Cell and Coverage Cell, deep sleeping can be triggered only when both the load of the energy-saving cell and the cell providing coverage meets the load condition.
item.name: deepSleepLBEvaluateMod

item.desc: This parameter sets the deep sleep time for energy saving from Monday through Friday every week. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a day (from Monday through Friday) and indicates whether deep sleep for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, deep sleep for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, deep sleep for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: weekdaySleepEsTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the deep sleep time for energy saving on Saturday and Sunday every week. It is an array parameter consisting of 96 elements, each of which represents a 15-minute time period in a day (Saturday or Sunday) and indicates whether deep sleep for energy saving is allowed in this time period. The first element represents 00:00-00:15, the second element represents 00:16-00:30, the third element represents 00:31-00:45, and so on. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, deep sleep for energy saving is allowed in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, deep sleep for energy saving is not allowed in this time period.
item.name: weekendSleepEsTime

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the automatic configuration of the energy-saving coverage relation of cells.
item.name: eSSelfConfigSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the auto-configuration period of the energy-saving coverage relation between a cell and its neighbor cells. It is used to configure the auto-configuration frequency of the energy-saving coverage relation.
item.name: eSSelfConfigPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum overlapping coverage degree threshold between a cell and its neighbor cells. An energy-saving coverage relation can be configured between a cell and its neighbor cells only when the overlapping coverage degree is greater than or equal to this threshold.
item.name: eSSelfConfigOverlapThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the time window for observing the load of a basic-coverage cell to wake up energy-saving cells. After an energy-saving cell enters energy-saving status, the coverage cell detects the cell load every 30 seconds. If the period during which the load of the coverage cell meets the wakeup conditions is longer than or equal to the parameter value, the energy-saving cell can be woken up. Otherwise, the system continues to detect the load of the coverage cell.
item.name: wakeupTimeWindow

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum percentage of the uplink load on a compensation cell when an intra-RAT energy-saving cell is awoken. The energy-saving cell can be awoken if the percentage of the uplink load on the compensation cell is higher than this threshold.
item.name: intraWakeupUlPRBThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum percentage of the downlink load on a compensation cell when an intra-RAT energy-saving cell is awoken. The energy-saving cell can be awoken if the percentage of the downlink load on the compensation cell is higher than this threshold.
item.name: intraWakeupDlPRBThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of RRC connections in a compensation cell when an intra-RAT energy-saving cell is awoken. The energy-saving cell can be awoken if the number of RRC connections in the compensation cell is larger than this threshold.
item.name: intraWakeupRRCNumThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum uplink PRB usage threshold for the LTE cells that provide basic coverage to wake up energy-saving NR cells. If the uplink PRB usage of a covering cell is higher than or equal to this threshold, the condition for waking energy saving cells up is satisfied. This is one of the conditions for a basic covering cell to wake up energy saving cells.
item.name: prbThrCellOnUl

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink PRB usage threshold for the LTE cells that provide basic coverage to wake up energy-saving NR cells. If the downlink PRB usage of a basic covering cell is higher than or equal to this threshold, the condition for waking energy saving cells up is satisfied. This is one of the conditions for a basic covering cell to wake up energy saving cells.
item.name: prbThrCellOnDl

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of UEs that are in a basic covering cell and support the NR capability. It is used to determine whether the cell that provides basic coverage can wake energy-saving NR cells up. In a basic covering cell, if the number of UEs that support the NR capability is larger than or equal to this threshold, the condition for waking energy-saving NR cells up is satisfied. This is one of the conditions for a basic covering cell to wake up energy-saving NR cells.
item.name: cellOnUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter is the voltage dynamic adjust function for energy saving. When it is set to Open, the voltage dynamic adjustment function is enabled. When it is set to Close, the voltage dynamic adjust function is disabled.
item.name: esVDASwitch

item.desc: The 24 hours starting from 00:00 in a day are divided into 96 periods, each of which is 15 minutes. This parameter is an array consisting of 96 elements. From the first element, the array indicates whether dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is allowed during a period of 15 minutes starting from 00:00 on a weekday (Monday to Friday). If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is not allowed during the corresponding period. If this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is allowed during the corresponding period.
item.name: weekdayVDAEsTime

item.desc: The 24 hours starting from 00:00 in a day are divided into 96 periods, each of which is 15 minutes. This parameter is an array consisting of 96 elements. From the first element, the array indicates whether dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is allowed during a period of 15 minutes starting from 00:00 on a Saturday or Sunday. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is not allowed during the corresponding period. If this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is allowed during the corresponding period.
item.name: weekendVDAEsTime

item.desc: The 24 hours starting from 00:00 in a day are divided into 96 periods, each of which is 15 minutes. This parameter is an array consisting of 96 elements. From the first element, the array indicates whether dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is allowed during a period of 15 minutes starting from 00:00 on a special day. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is not allowed during the corresponding period. If this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that dynamic-PA-bias-voltage shutdown for energy saving is allowed during the corresponding period.
item.name: specialVDAEsTime

item.desc: Voltage Dynamic Adjust Energy Saveing is divided into dynamic and semi dynamic.
item.name: esVDAType

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables dynamic voltage adjustment for the PA on the main control board of the BBU on the LTE side. If it is set to Open, the dynamic voltage adjustment for the PA on the main control board of the BBU on the LTE side takes effect in the scenario where 4G and 5G carriers share an AAU. If this parameter is set to Close, the dynamic voltage adjustment for the PA on the main control board of the BBU on the LTE side does not take effect.
item.name: paVoltAdjustEsSwitch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables auto-negotiation of energy-saving coverage relations. If it is set to Open, the relation from a coverage cell to an energy-saving cell is determined through the negotiation initiated by the energy-saving cell. If it is set to Close, the relation from a coverage cell to an energy-saving cell is determined through manual configuration.
item.name: eSSelfNegoSwch

item.desc: This parameter is an array parameter consisting of three elements, which respectively set the priority of the following three energy-saving modes: intelligent power-on/power-off, deep sleep, and carrier shutdown. The priorities of the elements decrease in turn. The element value 0 indicates intelligent power-on/power-off, 1 indicates deep sleep, and 2 indicates carrier shutdown. If the conditions of at least two of the three energy-saving modes are satisfied, the energy-saving mode with the highest priority takes effect.
item.name: esPriority

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the function of automatically starting and stopping energy saving. When this parameter is set to Open, energy saving is automatically started and stopped for the corresponding cell to reduce energy consumption of the eNodeB.
item.name: autoStartStopSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the load evaluation method for intelligent power-on/power-off for energy saving. If it is set to 0 (Non Evaluation Load), intelligent power-on/power-off for energy saving is enabled or disabled only within configured periods. If it is set to 1 (Evaluate the load of energy-saving cell), intelligent power-on/power-off for energy saving is enabled or disabled in a cell based on both the configured periods and the load of energy-saving cells. If it is set to 2 (Evaluation ES Cell and Coverage Cell), intelligent power-on/power-off for energy saving is enabled or disabled in a cell based on both the configured periods and the load of energy-saving cells and basic-coverage cells.
item.name: autoRunLoadEvaMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the automatic startup/stop time for energy saving from Monday to Friday every week. This parameter is an array with 96 elements, each of which corresponds to a 15-minute time range in a day (in one day there are 96 time segments in 24 hours) from Monday to Friday. The first element represents 00: 00-00: 15, and so on. If a time range is set to 0, it indicates that the time range is non-energy-saving, that is, cells cannot be in energy-saving status in the time range. If a time range is set to 1, it indicates that the time range is energy-saving, that is, cells can enter energy-saving status in the time range.
item.name: autoRunWeekdayTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the automatic startup/stop time for energy saving from Saturday to Sunday every week. This parameter is an array with 96 elements, each of which corresponds to a 15-minute time range in a day (in one day there are 96 time segments in 24 hours) from Saturday to Sunday. The first element represents 00: 00-00: 15, and so on. If a time range is set to 0, it indicates that the time range is non-energy-saving, that is, cells cannot be in energy-saving status in the time range. If a time range is set to 1, it indicates that the time range is energy-saving, that is, cells can enter energy-saving status in the time range.
item.name: autoRunWeekendTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum duration for which intelligent power-on/power-off for energy saving takes effect once. The energy-saving periods for intelligent power-on/power-off are configured by the autoRunWeekdayTime (Automatic Startup/Stop Time for Energy Saving on Weekdays) and autoRunWeekendTime (Automatic Startup/Stop Time for Energy Saving on Weekends) parameters. One or more consecutive energy-saving periods form one energy-saving period and the duration of one energy-saving period cannot exceed the duration specified by this parameter. Otherwise, intelligent power-on/power-off for energy saving does not take effect.
item.name: maxAutoStartStopEsTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the time shift duration for starting and exiting energy saving. For carrier shutdown or deep sleep without load evaluation, the time when energy saving is started is delayed by this duration compared with the configured start time of energy saving, and the time when energy saving is exited is advanced by this duration compared with the configured end time of energy saving.
item.name: esShiftTimeLen

item.desc: This parameter controls which energy-saving cells enter and exit energy-saving mode. If this parameter is set to All, the energy-saving cells that meet the specified conditions enter energy-saving mode. To exit energy-saving mode, all the energy-saving cells are woken up. If this parameter is set to Frequency-based, the eNodeB selects the cells with higher energy-saving priorities to start energy saving. To end energy saving, the eNodeB wakes up the energy-saving cells with lower priorities.
item.name: esCellControlMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the absolute SRS threshold for the UEs in a pRRU. It is used to determine whether a UE belongs to the current pRRU. If the SRS strength value of a UE is larger than this threshold, the UE may belong to this pRRU. A pRRU cannot be shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way as long as there is a UE in the pRRU.
item.name: ueAbsoluteSignalThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the load evaluation period when a cell exits energy-saving state after it is shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. If the load of a cell always meets the condition for awakening the pRRUs that are shut down for energy saving within the period specified by this parameter, the cell exits energy-saving state and the pRRUs that are in the cell and shut down for energy saving can be waken up.
item.name: precisionOnEvaluPrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the load evaluation period for shutting down pRRUs in a precisely controlled way. It is used to detect whether a cell can be shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. If the load of a cell always meets the condition for shutting down pRRUs in a precisely controlled way within the period specified by this parameter, the pRRUs that are in the cell and allowed to be shut down can be shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way.
item.name: precisionOffEvaluPrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the relative SRS threshold for the UEs in a pRRU. It is used to determine whether a UE belongs to the current pRRU. If the SRS strength value of a UE is larger than the difference between the maximum signal strength of the UE and this threshold, the UE may belong to this pRRU. A pRRU cannot be shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way as long as there is a UE in the pRRU.
item.name: ueRelativeSignalThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of VoLTE UEs in a cell. It is used to wake up the pRRUs that are in the cell and shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. When the number of VoLTE UEs in the cell is larger than this threshold, the cell exits energy-saving state and the shutdown pRRUs in the cell are woken up.
item.name: precisionOnVolteUeNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink PRB usage threshold of a cell. It is used to wake up the pRRUs that are in the cell and shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. When the uplink PRB usage threshold of the cell is higher than this threshold, the cell exits energy-saving state and the shutdown pRRUs in the cell are woken up.
item.name: precisionOnUlPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of RRC-connected UEs in a cell. It is used to wake up the pRRUs that are in the cell and shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. When the number of RRC-connected UEs in the cell is larger than this threshold, the cell exits energy-saving state and the shutdown pRRUs in the cell are woken up.
item.name: precisionOnUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of UEs in sentinel pRRUs. It is used to wake up the pRRUs that are shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. If precisely controlled shutdown for energy saving is enabled for a QCell, some pRRUs in the QCell are used as sentinel pRRUs to monitor the cell load and cannot be shut down in a precisely controlled way while some pRRUs can be shut down for energy saving only when the specified energy-saving condition is met. When the number of UEs in the sentinel pRRUs in the cell is larger than or equal to this threshold, it indicates that the cell meets the condition for awakening the pRRUs that are shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. In this case, the cell exits energy-saving state and the shutdown pRRUs in the cell are woken up.
item.name: precisionOnSentinelUeNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink PRB usage threshold of a cell. It is used to wake up the pRRUs that are in the cell and shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. When the downlink PRB usage threshold of the cell is higher than this threshold, the cell exits energy-saving state and the shutdown pRRUs in the cell are woken up.
item.name: precisionOnDlPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of UEs in sentinel pRRUs. It is used to shut down the pRRUs that can be shut down for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. If precisely controlled shutdown for energy saving is enabled for a QCell, some pRRUs in the QCell are used as sentinel pRRUs to monitor the cell load and cannot be shut down in a precisely controlled way while some pRRUs can be shut down for energy saving only when the specified power-off condition is met. When the number of UEs in the sentinel pRRUs in the cell is smaller than this threshold, it indicates that the cell meets the condition for shutting down pRRUs for energy saving in a precisely controlled way. In this case, the pRRUs that are in the cell and can be shut down for energy saving may be shut down and enter energy-saving state.
item.name: precisionOffSentinelUeNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of UEs for enabling envelope tracking. It is used to determine whether a cell enters or exits energy-saving status. During the time period for which energy can be saved through envelope tracking, if the number of UEs in a cell is smaller than this parameter value, the eNodeB performs envelope tracking (reduces the power voltage of the RF module) so that the cell enters energy-saving status. During energy saving, if the number of UEs in a cell is larger than or equal to the sum of this parameter and the envTrackUeNumOffset (Offset of the Number of UEs in a Cell for Exiting Envelope Tracking) parameter, the eNodeB adjusts the power voltage of the RF module to the maximum voltage level and the cell exits energy-saving status.
item.name: envTrackUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the offset of the number of UEs in a cell for exiting envelope tracking after energy saving. During envelope tracking for energy saving, if the number of UEs in a cell is larger than or equal to the sum of this parameter and the envTrackUeNumThrd (Threshold Number of UEs for Enabling Envelope Tracking) parameter, the eNodeB adjusts the power voltage of the RF module to the maximum voltage level and the cell exits energy-saving status.
item.name: envTrackUeNumOffset

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables envelope tracking for energy saving. If it is set to Open, the eNodeB decreases the power voltage of the RF module to save energy when the number of UEs in a cell is smaller than the envTrackUeNumThrd (Threshold Number of UEs for Enabling Envelope Tracking) parameter during the energy-saving period specified by the weekendEnvTrackTime (Envelope Tracking Time for Energy Saving on Weekends) and weekdayEnvTrackTime (Envelope Tracking Time for Energy Saving on Working Days) parameters. During energy saving, if the cell load is high and the number of UEs in the cell is larger than or equal to the sum of the envTrackUeNumThrd (Threshold Number of UEs for Enabling Envelope Tracking) parameter and the envTrackUeNumOffset (Offset of the Number of UEs in a Cell for Exiting Envelope Tracking) parameter, the eNodeB adjusts the power voltage of the RF module to the maximum voltage level and the cell exits energy-saving status. During energy saving, if the number of subframes with limited power in a radio frame is larger than or equal to the value of the envTrackRcvSubframeThr (Threshold Number of Subframes for Rapid Voltage Recovery During Envelope Tracking for Energy Saving) parameter, the eNodeB adjusts the power voltage of the RF module to the maximum voltage level and the cell exits energy-saving status.
item.name: envTrackSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of subframes for rapid voltage recovery during envelope tracking for energy saving. During envelope tracking for energy saving in a cell, if the number of subframes with limited power in a radio frame is larger than or equal to this parameter value, the eNodeB adjusts the power voltage of the RF module to the maximum voltage level and the cell exits envelope tracking-based energy saving.
item.name: envTrackRcvSubframeThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum power coefficient of a cell in envelope tracking. It is used to control the minimum power reserved for the cell during voltage decrease caused by envelope tracking for energy saving. The minimum power reserved for the cell is the initial power multiplied by this coefficient and then by 0.1.
item.name: envTrackPwrMinFactor

item.desc: This parameter sets the envelope tracking time for energy saving from Saturday to Sunday every week. It is an array with 96 elements, each of which corresponds to a 15-minute time period in a day (a day or 24 hours consists of 96 time periods) and indicates whether energy saving is allowed. The first element indicates whether energy saving is allowed during the period from 00:00 to 00:15. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, energy saving is not allowed for carriers in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, energy saving is allowed for carriers in this time period.
item.name: weekendEnvTrackTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the envelope tracking time for energy saving from Monday to Friday every week. It is an array with 96 elements, each of which corresponds to a 15-minute time period in a day (a day or 24 hours consists of 96 time periods) and indicates whether energy saving is allowed. The first element indicates whether energy saving is allowed during the period from 00:00 to 00:15. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 0, energy saving is not allowed for carriers in this time period. If the element corresponding to a time period is set to 1, energy saving is allowed for carriers in this time period.
item.name: weekdayEnvTrackTime

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the performance evaluation function. If this parameter is set to Open, the eNodeB determines whether an energy-saving cell enters or exits energy-saving status based on performance evaluation.
item.name: performanceEvalSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the detection interval (in minutes) for waking up energy-saving cells. With energy saving based on frequency priorities, a coverage cell covers energy-saving cells on multiple frequency layers. After the coverage cell wakes up energy-saving cells on a low-priority frequency layer, the coverage cell waits for the interval set by this parameter before performing load detection again. After the next detection, if the coverage cell determines that the conditions for waking up energy-saving cells are satisfied, the coverage cell wakes up energy-saving cells on the next frequency layer.
item.name: wakeupDetectInterval

item.desc: This parameter sets the shutdown pattern of 4-antenna FDD channels. If this parameter is set to 0 (Channel Shutdown Pattern1), it indicates that channel shutdown pattern 1 is used. If this parameter is set to 1 (Channel Shutdown Pattern2), it indicates that channel shutdown pattern 2 is used. In FDD 4T4Port configuration scenarios, pattern 1 indicates that the channels corresponding to Port2 and Port3 are shut down, and pattern 2 indicates that the channels corresponding to Port3 and Port4 are shut down.
item.name: rruChShutdownPattern4T

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable DRX for precisely-controlled sleeping cells in low-load hours. If DRX is enabled, the energy-saving effect of UEs can enhance but the precisely-controlled sleeping cells may fail to accurately identify and locate UEs. If DRX is disabled, the precisely-controlled sleeping cells can accurately identify and locate UEs.
item.name: precisionLowLBDrxMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for the total number of UEs for a basic-coverage cell to wake up an energy-saving NR cell. If the total number of UEs in the basic-coverage cell is larger than or equal to this threshold, the energy-saving NR cell is woken up. This is one of the conditions for a basic-coverage cell to wake up energy-saving NR cells.
item.name: cellOnAllUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of a special day, such as a holiday or anniversary. It is an array parameter consisting of four elements that indicate a month, date, hour, and minute in turn. For example, if this parameter is set to [3,10,8,20], it indicates that the start time is 08:20 on March 10.
item.name: specialStarTimeES

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of a special day, such as a holiday or anniversary. It is an array parameter consisting of four elements that indicate a month, date, hour, and minute in turn. For example, if this parameter is set to [3,10,8,20], it indicates that the end time is 08:20 on March 10.
item.name: specialEndTimeES

item.desc: This parameter indicates the ID of the special energy saving policy and is generated automatically by the UME.
item.name: specialEsPolicyID

item.desc: This parameter sets the indication of the period on festivals and holidays during which the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect. It is an array with 96 elements. The 24 hours of a day are divided into 96 periods of 15 minutes. Starting from the first element, each element of this array parameter indicates whether the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods from 00:00 on festivals and holidays. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on festivals and holidays. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving policy does not take effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on festivals or holidays.
item.name: esParaSpcTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the indication of the period on weekdays during which the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect. It is an array with 96 elements. The 24 hours of a day are divided into 96 periods of 15 minutes. Starting from the first element, each element of this array parameter indicates whether the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods from 00:00 on weekdays. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on weekdays. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving policy does not take effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on weekdays.
item.name: esParaWeekdayTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the indication of the periods at weekends (Saturday and Sunday) during which the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect. It is an array with 96 elements. The 24 hours of a day are divided into 96 periods of 15 minutes. Starting from the first element, each element of this array parameter indicates whether the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods from 00:00 on Saturday and Sunday. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on Saturday and Sunday. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving policy does not take effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on Saturday or Sunday.
item.name: esParaWeekendTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum uplink load of a cell when the cell enters energy saving state. It is one of the conditions for determining whether a cell enters energy saving state. The current cell can enter energy saving state only when the uplink load of the cell is lower than or equal to this threshold.
item.name: esOffUlLoadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum downlink load of a cell when the cell enters energy saving state. It is one of the conditions for determining whether a cell enters energy saving state. The current cell can enter energy saving state only when the downlink load of the cell is lower than or equal to this threshold.
item.name: esOffDlLoadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum uplink load of a compensation cell when the current cell enters energy saving state. It is one of the conditions for determining whether a cell enters energy saving state. The current cell can enter energy saving state only when the uplink load sum of the current cell and the compensation cell is smaller than this threshold.
item.name: esOffUlLoadReserveThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum downlink load of a compensation cell when the current cell enters energy saving state. It is one of the conditions for determining whether a cell enters energy saving state. The current cell can enter energy saving state only when the downlink load sum of the current cell and the compensation cell is smaller than this threshold.
item.name: esOffDlLoadReserveThrd

item.desc: This parameter set the maximum number of UEs with data services in an energy saving cell. If the number of UEs with data services in an energy saving cell is smaller than this threshold, the cell can enter energy saving state.
item.name: dataUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of VoLTE UEs in a cell when the cell enters energy saving state. It is one of the conditions for determining whether a cell enters energy saving state. The current cell can enter energy saving state only when the number of VoLTE UEs in the cell is smaller than this threshold.
item.name: volteUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the indication of the period on festivals and holidays during which the corresponding energy saving wakeup policy takes effect. It is an array with 96 elements. The 24 hours of a day are divided into 96 periods of 15 minutes. Starting from the first element, each element of this array parameter indicates whether the corresponding energy saving wakeup policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods from 00:00 on festivals and holidays. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving wakeup policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on festivals and holidays. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding energy saving wakeup policy does not take effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on festivals and holidays.
item.name: wakeEsParaSpcTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the indication of the period on weekdays during which the corresponding wake-up policy takes effect. It is an array with 96 elements. The 24 hours of a day are divided into 96 periods of 15 minutes. Starting from the first element, each element of this array parameter indicates whether the corresponding wake-up policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods from 00:00 on Monday to Friday. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding wake-up policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on Monday to Friday. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding wake-up policy does not take effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on Monday to Friday.
item.name: wakeEsParaWeekdayTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the indication of the periods at weekends (Saturday and Sunday) during which the corresponding wake-up policy takes effect. It is an array with 96 elements. The 24 hours of a day are divided into 96 periods of 15 minutes. Starting from the first element, each element of this array parameter indicates whether the corresponding wake-up policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods from 00:00 on Saturday and Sunday. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding wake-up policy takes effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on Saturday and Sunday. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding wake-up policy does not take effect in the corresponding 15-minute periods on Saturday or Sunday.
item.name: wakeEsParaWeekendTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink load threshold for an intra-RAT compensation cell to wake up energy-saving cells. After an energy-saving cell enters energy-saving state, the compensation cell detects its own uplink load. If the uplink load of the compensation cell is larger than or equal to the threshold, the eNodeB wakes up the energy-saving cells to ensure sufficient resources for UEs and guarantee service quality.
item.name: intraWakeupUlPRBThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink load threshold for an intra-RAT compensation cell to wake up energy-saving cells. After an energy-saving cell enters energy-saving state, the compensation cell detects its own downlink load. If the downlink load of the compensation cell is larger than or equal to the threshold, the eNodeB wakes up the energy-saving cells to ensure sufficient resources for UEs and guarantee service quality.
item.name: intraWakeupDlPRBThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of RRC-Connected UEs for an intra-RAT compensation cell to wake up energy-saving cells. After an energy-saving cell enters energy-saving state, the compensation cell detects the number of RRC-Connected UEs in it. If the number of RRC-Connected UEs in the compensation cell is larger than or equal to the threshold, the eNodeB wakes up the energy-saving cells to ensure sufficient resources for UEs and guarantee service quality.
item.name: intraWakeupRRCNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum uplink PRB usage of the LTE cells that provide basic coverage to wake up energy saving NR cells. If the uplink PRB usage of a basic-coverage LTE cell is higher than or equal to this threshold, the condition for waking up energy saving cells is satisfied. This is one of the conditions for a basic-coverage LTE cell to wake up energy saving cells.
item.name: nRWakeupUlPRBThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink PRB usage threshold for the LTE cells that provide basic coverage to wake up energy saving NR cells. This is one of the conditions for a basic-coverage LTE cell to wake up an energy saving cell. An energy saving NR cell can be waken up only when the downlink PRB usage of a basic-coverage LTE cell is higher than or equal to this threshold.
item.name: nRWakeupDlPRBThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of UEs that are in a basic-coverage LTE cell and support the NR capability. It is used to determine whether the cell that provides basic coverage can wake up energy saving NR cells. In a basic-coverage LTE cell, if the number of UEs that support the NR capability is larger than or equal to this threshold, the condition for waking up energy saving NR cells is satisfied. This is one of the conditions for a basic-coverage cell to wake up energy saving NR cells.
item.name: nRWakeupUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter is reserved for special energy saving policies.
item.name: reserve2

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for the total number of UEs for a basic-coverage LTE cell to wake up an energy-saving NR cell. In a basic-coverage LTE cell, if the number of UEs is larger than or equal to this threshold, one of the conditions for waking up energy-saving NR cells is satisfied.
item.name: nRWakeupAllUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the load prediction-based energy-saving function set. A maximum of four energy-saving functions can be selected. If an energy-saving function is selected, the eNodeB adaptively adjusts the energy-saving period of this function based on load prediction, thus improving the energy-saving efficiency. The energy-saving functions include carrier shutdown, deep sleep, intelligent power-on/power-off, and channel shutdown.
item.name: esBasedOnLoadPredList

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of 96 elements. It sets whether the eNodeB allows to determine the 15-minute periods to be carrier shutdown periods based on load prediction results on workdays (from Monday to Friday). The 24 hours (starting from 00:00 a. M. ) of a day are divided into 96 periods of 15 minutes. Starting from element 0, each element of this array parameter indicates whether the eNodeB allows to determine the corresponding 15-minute period to be a carrier shutdown period for energy saving based on the load prediction result. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the eNodeB allows to check whether a 15-minute period is a carrier shutdown period for energy saving based on the load prediction result. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the eNodeB does not allow to check whether a 15-minute period is a carrier shutdown period for energy saving based on the load prediction result.
item.name: allowEsTimeWeekDay

item.name: allowEsTimeWeekEnd

item.desc: This parameter sets a list of energy-saving self-optimization functions. A maximum of two energy-saving functions can be configured. If an energy-saving function is added to this list, the system enables the optimization for the corresponding function by day, evaluates related KPIs, and then adjusts the threshold parameters of the function. For example, if this parameter is set to 1 (Carrier ES Threshold Self-Optimization), the system collects and evaluates the KPIs related to carrier shutdown, deep sleep, and intelligent AAU power-on/power-off, and adjusts the threshold parameters of the corresponding carrier-level energy-saving policy based on the KPIs to balance energy conservation and consumption reduction with the system performance.

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables board reset if the board is reset because a fault is detected in the current cell while there are other normal cells related to the board. If this parameter is set to Close, the board is directly reset without being related to the status of other cells. If this parameter is set to Open, whether to trigger board reset depends on the status of other cells.
item.name: selHealResetRelaCellStateSwch

item.desc: This parameter is the switch of judging whether the CPU load is too high. If it is set to Open, self-healing detection is not performed when the CPU load is too high. Self-healing detection includes sleeping cell self-healing and poor-performance cell self-healing.

item.desc: The parameter shows the maximum number of self-healing recovering action. That is, before the self-healing fault recover, the maximum number of recovering action permitted by the system.
item.name: shMaxRevActionNum

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the self-healing detection function for sleeping cells.
item.name: sonEnableSlpCellHeal

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables sleeping-cell recovery. If it is set to Open and a sleeping cell is detected, the eNodeB performs the corresponding recovery operations, including the recovery of the sleeping cell and the corresponding RRU and baseband board. If it is set to Close, no recovery operation is performed by the eNodeB.
item.name: switchRecoSleepCell

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables sleeping-cell compensation by the eNodeB. If a sleeping cell cannot be recovered and this parameter is set to Open, the eNodeB takes some measures, for example, sleeping-cell shutdown, for compensation. If this parameter is set to Close, no compensation measure is taken by the eNodeB on sleeping cells.
item.name: switchComSleepCell

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the sleeping-cell detection period. It is configured in hour:minute format.
item.name: startTimeSCH

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the sleeping-cell detection period. It is configured in hour:minute format.
item.name: endTimeSCH

item.desc: This parameter indicates the detection period for self-healing of sleeping cells. If the cell satisfies the decision condition of sleeping cells during the detection period, this cell is a sleeping cell.
item.name: detectDura

item.desc: When the switch is on, the PDCH throughput of the cell will be considered to judge whether the cell is sleeping cell.
item.name: sleepCellThrouSwch

item.desc: This parameter is used to control whether to detect PDCP throughput for Sleeping Cell.When this parameter is configured as Not detect, PDCP throughput is not detected. When this parameter is configured as Detect, PDCP throughput is detected.
item.name: sleepCellPDCPSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the PDCP throughput threshold for sleeping cell detection. It is one of the conditions for determining whether the serving cell is a sleeping cell. It is possible for the serving cell to be identified as a sleeping cell based on PDCP throughput only if the PDCP throughput in the serving cell is not larger than the parameter value. It is impossible for the serving cell to be identified as a sleeping cell based on PDCP throughput if the PDCP throughput in the serving cell is larger than the parameter value.
item.name: sleepCellPDCPThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to reference the number of times that UEs attempt to access a cell in the determination of a sleeping cell. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the serving cell can be determined as a sleeping cell only when the number of online UEs in the cell is 0 and the number of times that UEs attempt to access the cell is larger than the value of the sleepCellHoInNumThrd (Threshold of the Number of UE Access Attempts for Sleeping Cell Detection) parameter. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the number of times that UEs attempt to access a cell is not considered in the determination of a sleeping cell.
item.name: sleepCellHoInDetectSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of times that UEs attempt to access a cell. It is one of the conditions for determining whether the serving cell is a sleeping cell. The serving cell can be determined as a sleeping cell only if the sleepCellHoInDetectSwch (Switch for Sleeping Cell Detection Based on Incoming Handover) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the number of online UEs in the cell is 0, and the number of times that UEs attempt to access the cell is larger than this threshold.
item.name: sleepCellHoInNumThrd

item.desc: The unit of the sleeping cell referred history period.

item.name: upInterfNIFaultThr

item.desc: When the number of cell satisfied fault recovery condition is equals to the threshold, the interference cell become normal.
item.name: upInterfRecoStatNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of Msg1 messages and is used to determine whether a cell can receive Msg1 messages. When the sleeping cell detection algorithm is being executed after the sleeping cell detection period expires, if the number of Msg1 messages that the cell has received is larger than the threshold, it is determined that the cell can receive Msg1 messages.
item.name: msg1NumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of RRC connections. At the end of a sleeping cell detection period, if the maximum number of RRC-connected UEs equals 0, the number of times that E-RABs are successfully established, and the number of times that RRC-connected UEs are successfully connected, the cell is determined as a sleeping cell.
item.name: rrcConnectNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of non-sleeping periods of the referenced historical data. When the sleeping cell detection period expires, historical data is required for determining whether the cell is a sleeping cell, and the minimum number of non-sleeping periods of the selected historical data must be reached in decision making. For example, if this parameter is set to 3, it can be determined that the cell is a sleeping cell only if there are at least three non-sleeping periods in the periods of the selected historical data.
item.name: sleepRefHisDataPrdThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of historical normal-load granularities. normal-load evaluation is implemented for each hour of the historical period corresponding to the period for sleeping cell detection. If the number of normal-load granularities (hours) is larger than or equal to this threshold, the entire historical period is considered as a normal-load period.
item.name: hisDataNormalLoadRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time of the period during which the sleeping cell performs recovery actions. If the start time at which the sleeping cell starts to perform recovery actions is later than this time, no recovery action is performed by the sleeping cell.
item.name: recoveryEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time of the period during which the sleeping cell performs recovery actions. If the switchRecoSleepCell parameter is set to 1 (Open), the sleeping cell starts to recover from this time point.
item.name: recoveryStartTime

item.desc: In a scenario where a new cell is established and the number of CA collaboration relationships is 0, if this parameter is set to Open, fast CA self-configuration with the same coverage is executed in the cell. If this parameter is set to Close, fast CA self-configuration with the same coverage is not executed in the cell. Location-based fast CA self-configuration is to execute in the neighbor cells with the same coverage when the two cells share the same RRU or the physical distance of the two cells is less than the threshold. If location-based fast CA self-configuration cannot meet CA configuration requirements, this parameter is set to Open for measurement-based fast CA self-configuration. Fast CA self-configuration is executed in the temporary neighbor cells based on the UE measurement result.
item.name: fastCAConfigSwch

item.desc: In a scenario where a new cell is established and the number of CA collaboration relationships is 0, if this parameter is set to Open, fast CA self-configuration with different coverage is executed in the cell. If this parameter is set to Close, fast CA self-configuration with different coverage is not executed in the cell. If location-based fast CA self-configuration cannot meet CA configuration requirements, this parameter is set to Open for measurement-based fast CA self-configuration. Fast CA self-configuration is executed in the temporary neighbor cells based on the UE measurement result.
item.name: fastCAConfigSwchForMeas

item.desc: This parameter indicates the maximum distance for fast CA self-configuration to decide the cells with the same coverage. The distance between two cell is the actual distance calculated based on the longitude and latitude of the cells.

item.desc: This parameter sets the period during which fast CA self-configuration takes effect. When fast CA self-configuration is enabled, this timer is started. When the timer times out, fast CA self-configuration is disabled and no more CA relation is added after neighbor cells are added to the serving cell.

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables deep sleep of the BBU. If it is set to Open, deep sleep of the BBU for energy saving is triggered when the deep-sleep conditions are satisfied. If it is set to Close, deep sleep of the BBU is disabled.

item.desc: This parameter sets the deep-sleep duration of BBUs for energy saving on weekdays. It is an array consisting of 96 elements each of which indicates a granularity of 15 minutes. The first element indicates the period from 00:00 to 00:15, the second element indicates the period from 00:15 to 00:30, the third element indicates the period from 00:30 to 00:45, and so on. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that deep sleep of the BBU is triggered for energy saving in the period corresponding to the element when the deep-sleep conditions are satisfied. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that deep sleep of the BBU for energy saving is not triggered in the period corresponding to the element.
item.name: bbuDeepShutDownWorkdayPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the deep-sleep duration of BBUs for energy saving on weekends. It is an array consisting of 96 elements each of which indicates a granularity of 15 minutes. The first element indicates the period from 00:00 to 00:15, the second element indicates the period from 00:15 to 00:30, the third element indicates the period from 00:30 to 00:45, and so on. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that deep sleep of the BBU is triggered for energy saving in the period corresponding to the element when the deep-sleep conditions are satisfied. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that deep sleep of the BBU for energy saving is not triggered in the period corresponding to the element.
item.name: bbuDeepShutDownWeekdayPeriod

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables CSS collaboration self-configuration. If it is set to Open, CSS collaboration self-configuration is enabled. If it is set to Close, CSS collaboration self-configuration is disabled.
item.name: cSSSelfConfigSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the SINR threshold for determining whether the reported GERAN cells can be configured with CSS collaboration. If the measured SINR is less than or equal to this threshold, it indicates that there is strong interference in the neighbor cell. If the measured SINR is larger than this threshold, it indicates that there is weak interference in the neighbor cell.
item.name: cSSJudgeSINRThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of GERAN neighbor cells for which CSS collaboration is allowed to be configured. If the number of GERAN neighbor cells to be configured with CSS collaboration is less than or equal to this threshold, all the GERAN neighbor cells are reported to the EMS for configuration; otherwise, only the GERAN neighbor cells within this threshold are reported to the EMS for configuration.
item.name: cSSGERANCellNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of UEs for periodical CSS collaboration self-configuration measurement. If the current number of UEs is less than or equal to this threshold, all the UEs perform the measurement; otherwise, only the UEs within this threshold perform the measurement.
item.name: cSSMeasUENumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the ratio of the number of MR samples that meet the SINR condition before CSS collaboration self-configuration to the total number of MR samples. If the measured value is larger than or equal to this threshold, CSS collaboration is performed on the neighbor cell. If the measured value is less than this threshold, CSS collaboration is not performed on the neighbor cell.
item.name: cSSJudgeMRRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of samples of periodical measurement reports before CSS collaboration auto-configuration. If the number of samples is larger than or equal to this threshold, CSS collaboration is performed on the LTE cell. If the number of samples is smaller than this threshold, CSS collaboration is not performed on the LTE cell.
item.name: cSSMRSampleThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of GERAN frequencies for which CSS collaboration is allowed to be configured. If the number of GERAN frequencies to be configured with CSS collaboration is less than or equal to this threshold, all the GERAN frequencies are reported to the EMS for configuration. If the number of GERAN frequencies to be configured with CSS collaboration is larger this threshold, only the GERAN frequencies within this threshold are reported to the EMS for configuration.
item.name: cSSGERANArfcnNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the period to select UEs for CSS collaboration self-configuration. In each period, the selected UEs perform MR measurement for CSS collaboration self-configuration.
item.name: cSSSelfCfgSelectUePeriod

item.desc: This parameter indicates the start time of CSS collaboration self-configuration detection. Every day, the detection starts at this time.
item.name: cSSCooperDeteStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration of the timer for detecting CSS self-configuration. When CSS is enabled, this timer is started and the system starts to collect statistics on the number of times that the measurement results of CSS collaboration self-configuration are reported. When the timer times out, the data collection stops. If the number of times that the measurement results of CSS collaboration self-configuration are reported reaches the detection threshold, the system load is sorted based on the measurement results and the CSS Supported Update Switch parameter is modified. If the number of times that the measurement results of CSS collaboration self-configuration are reported does not reach the detection threshold, the next detection is started.
item.name: cSSSelfCfgSingDeteTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of CSS collaboration self-configuration detections in a single period.
item.name: cSSSelfCfgDetectNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval for executing CSS collaboration self-configuration. The unit of this parameter depends on the statistical granularity for CSS collaboration sfle-configuration.
item.name: cSSConfigExeInterPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the granularity at which statistics are collected for CSS collaboration self-configuration.
item.name: cSSStatisticInterGrade

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables appointed reporting for CSS collaboration self-configuration. If it is set to Open, CSS collaboration attributes are updated at the specified reporting appointed of time. If it is set to Close, CSS collaboration attributes are updated immediately after the number of CSS self-configuration detections reaches the threshold.
item.name: cSSAppointRptSwch

item.desc: This parameter indicates the start time of CSS collaboration self-configuration. When CSS collaboration self-configuration is enabled, CSS collaboration attribute update is implemented at the time specified by this parameter.
item.name: cSSAppointRptStartTime

item.desc: This parameter indicates the end time of CSS collaboration self-configuration. When CSS collaboration self-configuration is enabled, CSS collaboration attribute update is implemented before the time specified by this parameter.
item.name: cSSAppointRptStopTime
