item.desc: This parameter sets the spectrum sharing strategy between 4G and 5G systems. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), it indicates that no spectrum resource is shared between 4G and 5G systems. If this parameter is set to 1 (Semi-static), it indicates that semi-static spectrum resources are shared between 4G and 5G systems, and cell spectrum resources can be adjusted between 4G and 5G systems every second based on traffic load. If this parameter is set to 2 (Dynamic), it indicates that dynamic spectrum resources are shared between 4G and 5G systems, and cell spectrum resources can be adjusted between 4G and 5G systems every millisecond based on traffic load.
item.name: specShareBaseNrSwch

item.desc: This parameter is the threshold that the uplink PRB usage of service cell and basic coverage cell should meet when spectrum sharing is started. Only when the uplink PRB usage of service cell and basic coverage cell is less than the threshold, Spectrum Sharing can be started.
item.name: ulPrbEnterThr

item.desc: This parameter is the threshold that the downlink prb usage of service cell and basic coverage cell should meet when spectrum sharing is started. Only when the downlink prb usage of service cell and basic coverage cell is less than the threshold, Spectrum Sharing can be started.
item.name: dlPrbEnterThr

item.desc: The parameter is the threshold that serving cell meet the user number threshold when the NR spectrum sharing is started.
item.name: uENumberEnterThr

item.desc: This parameter is the threshold that the uplink prb usage of basic coverage cell should reach when spectrum sharing is stopped. When the uplink prb usage of the basic coverage cell exceeds the threshold, spectrum sharing is stopped.
item.name: ulPrbExitThr

item.desc: This parameter is the threshold that the downlink prb usage of basic coverage cell should reach when spectrum sharing is stopped. When the downlink prb usage of the basic coverage cell exceeds the threshold, spectrum sharing is stopped.
item.name: dlPrbExitThr

item.desc: This parameter indicates that when the number of users in service cell is larger than the threshold, the spectrum sharing will be exit.
item.name: uENumberExitThr

item.desc: This parameter indicates the mode of load evaluation in NR spectrum sharing.
item.name: loadJudgmentType

item.desc: The parameter is the load evaluation period that the NR spectrum sharing is started or exited.
item.name: loadEvaluatePeriod

item.desc: This parameter represents the continuous request number of Shared Spectrum on the LTE side.
item.name: reqNumOfShare

item.desc: This parameter indicates spectrum sharing request punished period.
item.name: punishPeriod

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables spectrum sharing for an anchor cell. If it is set to Open, it indicates that the current cell is an anchor cell and spectrum sharing is disabled.
item.name: anchorSwitch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables active silence for semi-static spectrum sharing on the LTE side. If it is set to Open, LTE cells send spectrum resource release notifications to NR cells and the NR cells directly request spectrum resources from the LTE cells to start the spectrum sharing procedure. If this parameter is set to Close, this function does not take effect.

item.desc: This parameter sets the policy ID of an intelligent beam adjustment function of an FMM cell. It is used to distinguish the policies of different functions and is unique within the eNodeB.
item.name: sonPolicyId

item.desc: This parameter sets the service type, 26 for SH, 43 for CS, 46 for ANR, 47 for PCI, 48 for X2, 49 for MRO, 51 for RO, 52 for MLB, 57 for ES, 58 for MAGICRADIO, 59 for SpecShare, 64 for FmmAapc.
item.name: sonFuncId

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables intelligent beam optimization. It is used to adjust the azimuth and coverage of beams in a sector.To enable the beam overall-adjustment sub-function, set this parameter to Overall Beam Opt. In this case, the eNodeB adjusts the azimuth and coverage of the beams of each space-division cell group on the whole in accordance with the UE distribution in the sector, so that the beams can match the UE distribution of the current sector on the whole.To enable the beam-level adjustment function, set this parameter to Single Beam Opt. In this case, the eNodeB adjusts the beamwidth and azimuth of each beam within each space-division cell based on the distribution of UEs in the corresponding cell of the sector. This ensures that each beam aligns properly with the distribution of UEs within in it.
item.name: fmmAapcOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of intelligent beam optimization. If it is set to Maximum SINR, the system adjusts the coverage angle of the cell to better match the UE distribution to improve user experience. If it is set to Self Adaptive, the system adjusts the coverage angle and coverage of the cell to better match the UE distribution to improve user experience.
item.name: fmmAapcOptMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the operating mode of intelligent beams. It takes effect when the Switch of Intelligent Beam Optimization (SonFMMAAPCFDDLTE.fmmAapcOptSwch) parameter is set to Open. If it is set to Weight Self-Optimization Adjustment, the system periodically optimizes and evaluates weights, and outputs and applies the evaluation results. If it is set to Weight Self-Handover, the system uses the separate fixed weights on weekdays and weekends alternatively.
item.name: optWeightValueValiMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the time range of the operator's local weekdays and weekends. If it is set to 0, it indicates that the local weekdays are from Monday to Friday and the weekends are Saturday and Sunday. If it is set to 1, it indicates that the local weekdays are from Sunday to Thursday and the weekends are Friday and Saturday.
item.name: weekType

item.desc: This parameter sets the time at which the weights of intelligent beam optimization can be modified.
item.name: fmmAapcChangeTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration for detecting intelligent beam optimization. If the Switch of Intelligent Beam Optimization parameter is set to Open, the eNodeB starts the procedure for detecting intelligent beam optimization. If this parameter is set to a larger value, the calculated beam weights of the space-division cell groups are more accurate. If this parameter is set to a smaller value, the detection duration is shorter and the calculated beam weights of the space-division cell groups are less accurate.
item.name: optDetectTimerLen

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration for evaluating intelligent beam optimization. If the Switch of Intelligent Beam Optimization parameter is set to Open, the eNodeB starts the procedure for evaluating intelligent beam optimization after performing a procedure for detecting intelligent beam optimization. The procedure for evaluating intelligent beam optimization is used to evaluate the system impact after the optimal weight calculated through intelligent beam optimization is applied. A larger parameter value indicates more-accurate evaluation results.
item.name: optEvaluationTimerLen

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for determining the handover success rate of the fast-evaluation process when intelligent beam optimization is enabled. It is used to determine whether intelligent beam optimization passes the fast-evaluation process. Fast evaluation is to evaluate the system impact in one day after the result of intelligent beam optimization is applied. One of the conditions for determining that intelligent beam optimization passes the fast-evaluation process is as follows: The difference between the handover success rate in the collection period and the handover success rate in the fast evaluation period must be smaller than this parameter value.
item.name: fastEvalHoSuccessThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for determining the link establishment success rate of the fast-evaluation process when intelligent beam optimization is enabled. It is used to determine whether intelligent beam optimization passes the fast-evaluation process. Fast evaluation is to evaluate the system impact one day after the result of intelligent beam optimization is applied. One of the conditions for determining that intelligent beam optimization passes the fast-evaluation process is as follows: The difference between the link establishment success rate in the optimization collection period and the link establishment success rate in the fast evaluation period must be smaller than this parameter value.
item.name: fastEvalErabSetupThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for determining the dropped-call rate of the fast-evaluation process when intelligent beam optimization is enabled. It is used to determine whether intelligent beam optimization passes the fast-evaluation process. One of the conditions for determining that intelligent beam optimization passes the fast-evaluation process is as follows: The difference between the dropped-call rate in the fast-evaluation period and the dropped-call rate in the optimization collection period is smaller than this parameter value.
item.name: fastEvalErabDropThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage threshold for determining busy or idle hours. If the PRB usage of a cell in the current period is higher than this threshold, the current period is a busy-hour period of the cell. If the PRB usage of a cell in the current period is lower than or equal to this threshold, the current period is a busy-hour period of the cell.
item.name: prbUsageThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the payload gain threshold for optimization performance evaluation of the beam-level {H,A} adjustment result. It is used to determine whether the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment passes the performance evaluation process. Within the period specified by the beamHAAdjustPeriod (Period for Beam-Level {H,A} Adjustment) parameter after the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the performance evaluation process is met if the optimized FMM-sector-level payload gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: perfEvalIPayloadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage threshold at the start time of fast evaluation of beam-level {H,A} adjustment. After the beam-level {H,A} adjustment result takes effect, the time at which the cell-level PRB usage is larger than or equal to the parameter value for the first time is the start time of fast evaluation. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that the fast-evaluation process is implemented immediately after the beam-level {H,A} adjustment result takes effect.
item.name: fastEvalStartPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the IP throughput gain threshold for optimization performance evaluation of the beam-level {H,A} adjustment result. It is used to determine whether the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment passes the performance evaluation process. Within the period specified by the beamHAAdjustPeriod (Period for Beam-Level {H,A} Adjustment) parameter after the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the performance evaluation process is met if the optimized FMM-sector-level IP throughput gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: perfEvalIPthpThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the IP throughput gain threshold for fast evaluating the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment. It is used to determine whether the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment passes the fast-evaluation process. Within the period specified by the beamHAAdjustPeriod (Period for Beam-Level {H,A} Adjustment) parameter after the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the fast-evaluation process is met if the optimized FMM-sector-level IP throughput gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: fastEvalIPthpThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the payload gain threshold for fast evaluating the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment. It is used to determine whether the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment passes the fast-evaluation process. Within the period specified by the beamHAAdjustPeriod (Period for Beam-Level {H,A} Adjustment) parameter after the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the fast-evaluation process is met if the optimized FMM-sector-level payload gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: fastEvalPayloadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the period for fast evaluating the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment. It is valid if the fmmAapcOptSwch (Switch of Intelligent Beam Optimization) parameter is set to 2 (Single Beam Opt). Fast evaluation is to evaluate whether the related indicators meet the specified conditions within the period specified by this parameter after the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect. If the optimization result passes the evaluation process, the optimization result still takes effect. If the optimization result fails to pass the evaluation process, the configurations roll back to those before the optimization.
item.name: fastEvalPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the azimuth spacing between neighbor cells if beam-level {H,A} adjustment is enabled. It is used to adjust the beam width (H). During beam-level {H,A} adjustment, if the minimum azimuth angle between a cell and its neighbor cells is larger than or equal to the parameter value, set the beam width (H) corresponding the cell to a larger value. If the minimum azimuth angle between a cell and its neighbor cells is smaller than the parameter value, set the beam width (H) corresponding the cell to a smaller value.
item.name: beamWidthThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the upper limit of the beam azimuth spacing between neighbor cells if beam-level {H,A} adjustment is enabled. It is used to determine whether the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect. If beam-level {H,A} adjustment is enabled and the beam azimuth spacing between neighbor cells is smaller than or equal to the parameter value, one of the conditions for the optimization result to take effect is met. Otherwise, the optimization result does not take effect.
item.name: azimDisHighThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the lower limit of the beam azimuth spacing between neighbor cells if beam-level {H,A} adjustment is enabled. It is used to determine whether the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect. If beam-level {H,A} adjustment is enabled and the beam azimuth spacing between neighbor cells is larger than or equal to the parameter value, one of the conditions for the optimization result to take effect is met. Otherwise, the optimization result does not take effect.
item.name: azimDisLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the beam-level {H,A} adjustment period and the optimization performance evaluation period. It is valid if the fmmAapcOptSwch (Switch of Intelligent Beam Optimization) parameter is set to 2 (Single Beam Opt). During a period specified by this parameter, the system performs the beam-level {H,A} adjustment procedure. During another period specified by this parameter, the system performs the optimization performance evaluation procedure. Performance evaluation is to evaluate whether the related indicators meet the specified conditions after the optimization result of beam-level {H,A} adjustment takes effect. If the optimization result passes the evaluation process, the optimization result still takes effect in the next period. If the optimization result fails to pass the evaluation process, in the next period, the configurations roll back to those before the optimization.
item.name: beamHAAdjustPeriod

item.name: FDN

item.desc: Collection period of measurement task.

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the string type and can be configured as planned.
item.name: id

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the string type and can be configured as planned.
item.name: moId

item.desc: This parameter sets the ID of a policy for adjusting the number of FMM intelligent beams. It is used to identify a policy. This parameter must be unique within an eNodeB.
item.name: sonPolicyId

item.desc: This parameter sets the service type, 26 for SH, 43 for CS, 46 for ANR, 47 for PCI, 48 for X2, 49 for MRO, 51 for RO, 52 for MLB, 57 for ES, 58 for MAGICRADIO, 59 for SpecShare, 61 for BeamNumAdjust, 64 for FmmAapc.
item.name: sonFuncId

item.desc: Run Mode
item.name: sonRunMode

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the intelligent beam quantity adjustment and beam power adjustment functions. It is used for intelligent beam combination and intra-sector beam power adjustment.If this parameter is set to Beam Comb, the eNodeB determines whether to combine or split the current smart space-division cell group based on the PRB usage and IP throughput of the cells in the group, that is, whether to adjust the number of beams. If the sector load is low, the number of cells in the space-division group can be decreased to improve the signal coverage of the overlapped areas and reduce CRS interference between the cells. If the sector load is high, the number of cells in the space-division cell group can be increased to increase the number of UEs scheduled through space-division multiplexing. Combination and splitting are supported only between the beams in a fixed combination.If this parameter is set to Beam Comb Enhanced, the function principle is the same as that of the beam combination sub-function, but combination and splitting are supported for any beams.If this parameter is set to Beam Power Opt, beam power optimization can be implemented based on a single frequency or multiple frequencies in the same sector. By collecting statistics on and identifying the service load of each space-division cell in a sector, the eNodeB shuts down some ultra-idle cells to increase the spectrum efficiency of busy cells, so that power allocation in the sector can be suitable for service distribution, and downlink performance can be improved.If this parameter is set to Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt, both the enhanced beam combination sub-function and sector-based beam power optimization sub-function are enabled.
item.name: beamNumAdjustSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the mode in which a beam weight value is generated for a smart space-division cell group. To use a weight value in the weight database as an optimized weight value, set this parameter to Weight Database. Because the weight values in the weight database are saved in advance, calculation complexity is low, the beam construction granularity is fine, and the configuration flexibility is poor. To use the weight value generated online by the HAVT as the optimized weight value, set this parameter to HAVT Online Generate. In this case, the calculation complexity is high, the beam construction granularity is coarse, and the configuration flexibility is high.
item.name: wgtGenerateMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the lower PRB usage threshold for cell combination in the SSCG beam quantity adjustment function. It determines whether cells are combined during intelligent beam quantity adjustment. One of the conditions for combining two cells is as follow: The PRB usage of either of the two cells is consecutively smaller than or equal to this threshold for a number of times specified by the KPI Collection Times for Beam Number Adjustment parameter. The larger this parameter value is, the higher the probability of cell combination is. The smaller this parameter value is, the lower the probability of cell combination is.
item.name: cellCombPrbLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the higher threshold of the PRB usage for cell combination in the case that the function of intelligent beam quantity adjustment in FDD massive MIMO is enabled. This threshold determines whether two cells can be combined in the phase for optimizing the number of beams. If the sum of the PRB usage of two cells is smaller than or equal to this threshold consecutively for the number of times specified by the ucKpiCollectTimes parameter, the condition for combining the two cells is satisfied. The larger the parameter value, the more likely that two cells are combined.
item.name: cellCombPrbHighThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the medium threshold of the PRB usage for cell combination in the case that the function of intelligent beam quantity adjustment in FDD massive MIMO is enabled. This threshold determines whether two cells can be combined in the phase for optimizing the number of beams. If the PRB usage of either one of two cells is smaller than or equal to this threshold consecutively for the number of times specified by the ucKpiCollectTimes parameter, the condition for combining the two cells is satisfied. The larger the parameter value, the more likely that two cells are combined.
item.name: cellCombPrbMidThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the higher threshold of the PRB usage for cell splitting in the case that the function of intelligent beam quantity adjustment in FDD massive MIMO is enabled. This threshold determines whether a cell can be split in the phase for optimizing the number of beams. If the PRB usage of a cell is larger than or equal to this threshold consecutively for the number of times specified by the ucKpiCollectTimes parameter, the condition for splitting the cell is satisfied. The smaller the parameter value, the more likely that a cell is split.
item.name: cellSplitPrbHighThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the lower threshold of IP throughput for cell splitting in the case that the function of intelligent beam quantity adjustment in FDD massive MIMO is enabled. This threshold determines whether a cell can be split in the phase for optimizing the number of beams. If the IP throughput of a cell is smaller than or equal to this threshold for the number of times specified by the ucKpiCollectTimes parameter, the condition for splitting the cell is satisfied. The larger the parameter value, the more likely that a cell is split.
item.name: cellSplitIpLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the UE distribution proportion for determining cell splitting in the case that the intelligent-beam quantity adjustment function in FDD massive MIMO is enabled. In the 32 beams of a cell, if the proportion of the number of UEs in the first 16 beams and the proportion of the number of UEs in the last 16 beams are both larger than or equal to this parameter value, one of the conditions for cell splitting is satisfied. A smaller parameter value indicates that it is more likely to split a cell.
item.name: cellSplitUEDistrThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage hysteresis for beam recovery in the scenarios where there is no FMM signal coverage after FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect. After the period for evaluating the effect of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization ends, the system attempts to temporarily recover the disabled FMM beams and collects statistics on the total PRB usage in this area within the period specified by the beamRecoveryPeriod (Period to Determine Whether to Recover Disabled FMM Beams) parameter. If the increase in the total PRB usage relative to the value of the closeCellPrbThrd (PRB Usage Threshold for Disabling FMM Beams) parameter is larger than the value of this parameter, the disabled FMM beams can be recovered.
item.name: beamRecoveryPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage threshold at the start time of fast evaluation of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization. After the FMM-sector-level beam power optimization result takes effect, the time at which the cell-level PRB usage is larger than or equal to the parameter value for the first time is the start time of fast evaluation. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that the fast-evaluation process is implemented immediately after the FMM-sector-level beam power optimization result takes effect.
item.name: fastEvalStartPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold ratio of the valid busy-hour duration to the current period if FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). If the PRB usage of a cell in an FMM sector is larger than or equal to the value of the powLiftPrbLowThrd (Low PRB Usage Threshold of Cells with Power Increase) parameter, the system determines that the traffic of the FMM sector is high. In the first period that is specified by the powAdjustPeriod (Period for Sector Beam Power Optimization) parameter and during which FMM-sector-level beam power optimization starts to be performed, if the ratio of the busy-hour duration of the current FMM sector to this period is larger than or equal to the parameter value, this period is valid and FMM-sector-level beam power optimization continues to be performed. Otherwise, this period is invalid and FMM-sector-level beam power optimization starts to be performed again in the next period.
item.name: busyTimeLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the period for FMM-sector-level beam power optimization and optimization performance evaluation. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). During a period specified by this parameter, the system performs the beam power optimization procedure. During another period specified by this parameter, the system performs the optimization performance evaluation procedure. Performance evaluation is to evaluate whether the related indicators meet the specified conditions after the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect. If the optimization result passes the evaluation process, the optimization result still takes effect in the next period. If the optimization result fails to pass the evaluation process, in the next period, the configurations roll back to those before the optimization.
item.name: powAdjustPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage hysteresis for beam recovery in the scenarios where FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect and traffic burst occurs. The disabled FMM beams can be recovered within the period specified by the powAdjustPeriod (Period for Sector Beam Power Optimization) parameter if the following conditions are met: FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled, the optimization result passes the performance evaluation process, the performance evaluation period ends, and the increase in the PRB usage of FMM beams measured in the current period relative to that measured in the previous period is larger than this parameter value.
item.name: burstyPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage hysteresis for beam recovery in the scenarios where there is still FMM signal coverage after FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect. The disabled FMM beams can be recovered within the period specified by the powAdjustPeriod (Period for Sector Beam Power Optimization) parameter if the following conditions are met: FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled, the optimization result passes the performance evaluation process, the performance evaluation period ends, and the increase in the PRB usage of FMM beams measured in the current period relative to that measured in the previous period is larger than this parameter value.
item.name: beamRecoveryPrbGrowThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the period during which the system determines whether to recover the disabled FMM beams if FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). If FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect and the optimization result passes the performance evaluation process, at the end of the evaluation period, this parameter is used to determine whether to recover the disabled FMM beams within the period specified by this parameter.
item.name: beamRecoveryPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the payload gain threshold for performance evaluation of the FMM-sector-level beam power optimization result. It is used to determine whether the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization passes the performance evaluation process. Within the period specified by the powAdjustPeriod (Period for Sector Beam Power Optimization) parameter after the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the performance evaluation process is met if the optimized FMM-sector-level payload gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: perfEvalIPayloadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the IP throughput gain threshold for performance evaluation of the FMM-sector-level beam power optimization result. It is used to determine whether the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization passes the performance evaluation process. Within the period specified by the powAdjustPeriod (Period for Sector Beam Power Optimization) parameter after the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the performance evaluation process is met if the optimized FMM-sector-level IP throughput gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: perfEvalIPthpThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the IP throughput gain threshold for fast evaluating the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization. It is used to determine whether the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization passes the fast-evaluation process. Within the period specified by the fastEvalPeriod (Fast-Evaluation Period of Sector Beam Power Optimization) parameter after the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the fast-evaluation process is met if the optimized FMM-sector-level IP throughput gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: fastEvalIPthpThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the payload gain threshold for fast evaluating the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization. It is used to determine whether the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization passes the fast-evaluation process. Within the period specified by the fastEvalPeriod (Fast-Evaluation Period of Sector Beam Power Optimization) parameter after the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect, one of the conditions for the optimization result to pass the fast-evaluation process is met if optimized the FMM-sector-level payload gain is larger than or equal to this parameter value.
item.name: fastEvalPayloadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the fast-evaluation period of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). Fast evaluation is to evaluate whether the related indicators meet the specified conditions within the period specified by this parameter after the result of FMM-sector-level beam power optimization takes effect. If the optimization result passes the evaluation process, the optimization result still takes effect. If the optimization result fails to pass the evaluation process, the configurations roll back to those before the optimization.
item.name: fastEvalPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the upper limit of the target PA value of the cells with power increase if FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). If the current cell is determined as a cell with level-1, level-2, or level-3 power increase, this parameter can be used to increase the PA value of the cell. The maximum PA value cannot exceed the parameter value.
item.name: paIncreaseUpperLimit

item.desc: This parameter sets the Energy Per Resource Element (EPRE) increase of the cells with power increase if FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). If the current cell is determined as a cell with level-1, level-2, or level-3 power increase, this parameter can be used to expand the cell coverage to increase the number of UEs in the cell.
item.name: cellCoverErsIncrement

item.desc: This parameter sets the high PRB usage threshold for determining the cells with power increase if FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled. It is used to determine the cells with level-1 power increase. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). If the PRB usage of a cell is larger than or equal to this parameter value, the eNodeB determines that the cell meets one of the conditions of cells with level-1 power increase.For a cell with level-1 power increase, the eNodeB increases the power of the cell based on the highest power increase level, improving the signal strength of the FMM beams and the user experience of the cell.
item.name: powLiftPrbHighThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the medium PRB usage threshold for determining the cells with power increase if FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled. It is used to determine the cells with level-2 power increase. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). If the PRB usage of a cell is larger than or equal to this parameter value and smaller than the value of the powLiftPrbHighThrd (High PRB Usage Threshold of Cells with Power Increase) parameter, the eNodeB determines that the cell meets one of the conditions of cells with level-2 power increase.For a cell with level-2 power increase, the eNodeB increases the power of the cell based on the medium power increase level, improving the signal strength of the FMM beams and the user experience of the cell.
item.name: powLiftPrbMidThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the low PRB usage threshold for determining the cells with power increase if FMM-sector-level beam power optimization is enabled. It is used to determine the cells with level-3 power increase. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). If the PRB usage of a cell is larger than or equal to this parameter value and smaller than the value of the powLiftPrbMidThrd (Medium PRB Usage Threshold of Cells with Power Increase) parameter, the eNodeB determines that the cell meets one of the conditions of cells with level-3 power increase. For a cell with level-3 power increase, the eNodeB increases the power of the cell based on the lowest power increase level, improving the signal strength of the FMM beams and the user experience of the cell.
item.name: powLiftPrbLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage threshold for checking whether to disable FMM beams from cells during FMM-sector-level beam power optimization in a multi-frequency scenario. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). In a multi-frequency scenario, when the PRB usage of a cell is lower than or equal to the parameter value, the FMM beams covering this cell are disabled. In this case, the cell cannot provide FMM network services.
item.name: multiFreqCloseCellPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage threshold for determining whether to disable FMM beams from cells during FMM-sector-level beam power optimization. It is valid if the beamNumAdjustSwch parameter is set to 3 (Beam Power Opt) or 4 (Beam Comb Enhanced And Beam Power Opt). When the PRB usage of a cell is smaller than or equal to the parameter value, the FMM beams covering this cell are disabled. In this case, the cell cannot provide FMM network services.
item.name: closeCellPrbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the radio capability FGI feature information used by the eNodeB to exclude the UEs performing Trace measurement tasks. The content is a readable string in the fixed format of UE accessStratumRelease_FGI Present indication_TDD R8 FGI_TDD R9 FGI_TDD R10 FGI_FDD R8 FGI_FDD R9 FGI_FDD R10 FGI. Where:UE accessStratumRelease corresponds to the accessStratumRelease IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability defined in TS36.331; TDD R8 FGI corresponds to the tdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndicators-r9 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability defined in TS36.331 or the featureGroupIndicators IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability (if the UE does not have the tdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndicators-r9 IE capability information);TDD R9 FGI corresponds to the tdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndRel9Add-r9 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability defined in TS36.331, or the featureGroupIndRel9Add-r9 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability (if the UE does not have the tdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndRel9Add-r9 IE capability information); TDD R10 FGI corresponds to the tdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-v1060featureGroupIndRel10-v1060 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability defined in TS36.331, or the featureGroupIndRel10-r10 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability (if the UE does not have the tdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-v1060featureGroupIndRel10-v1060 IE); FDD R8 FGI corresponds to the fdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndicators-r9 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability defined in TS36.331, or the featureGroupIndicators IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability (if the UE does not have the fdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndicators-r9 IE capability information);FDD R9 FGI corresponds to the fdd -Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndRel9Add-r9 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability defined in TS36.331, or the featureGroupIndRel9Add-r9 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability (if the UE does not have the fdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-r9featureGroupIndRel9Add-r9 IE capability information);FDD R10 FGI corresponds to the fdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-v1060featureGroupIndRel10-v1060 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability defined in TS36.331, or the featureGroupIndRel10-r10 IE in UE-EUTRA-Capability (if the UE does not have the fdd-Add-UE-EUTRA-Capabilities-v1060featureGroupIndRel10-v1060 IE);FGI Present indication consists of six digits 0 and 1, indicating whether the subsequent FGI domain is valid.The value 0 means that the corresponding FGI domain is invalid and three is no relevant information in UE-EUTRA-Capability. A possible FGI feature information is configured as follows: R10_111111_FFCF1EA6_06800000_00340000_FFCF1EA6_06800000_00340000.
item.name: strUeFgiInfo

item.desc: This parameter sets the Trace measurement task based on which the eNodeB can exclude the related UEs according to radio capability FGI feature information. It indicates a bitmap of 32 bits in length. The first bit (bit 1) on the right represents an MDT measurement task, bit 2 an inter-frequency period MR measurement task, and bit 3 an inter-RAT period MR measurement task. Bits 4 to 32 are reserved. If the bit value is 0, the function of excluding UEs according to radio capability FGI feature information is disabled. If the bit value is 1, the function of excluding UEs according to radio capability FGI feature information is enabled.
item.name: strToolFgiFilFuncBitmap

item.desc: This parameter sets the indexes of the IMMCI profile policies for the UEs with SPIDs and the UEs without SPIDs if smart idle-UE distribution is enabled and the cell load is medium. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Each element indicates the index of an IMMCI profile policy for both the UEs with SPIDs and the UEs without SPIDs.
item.name: ref1IdleMobilityProfileLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the probabilities that UEs carry the two IMMCI profile policies if smart idle-UE distribution is enabled and the cell load is medium. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. The first and second elements indicate the probabilities that UEs carry the two IMMCI profile policies corresponding to the first and second elements specified by the SmartNetDistLTE. Ref1IdleMobilityProfileLTE array parameter respectively. A larger element value indicates a higher probability that the UEs carry the corresponding IMMCI profile policy when they are released.
item.name: mLIMMCIProfileIndexPro

item.desc: This parameter sets the indexes of the IMMCI profile policies for the UEs with SPIDs and the UEs without SPIDs if smart idle-UE distribution is enabled and the cell load is high. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Each element indicates the index of an IMMCI profile policy for both the UEs with SPIDs and the UEs without SPIDs.
item.name: ref2IdleMobilityProfileLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets probabilities that UEs carry the two IMMCI profile policies if smart idle-UE distribution is enabled and the cell load is high. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. The first and second elements indicate the probabilities that UEs carry the two IMMCI profile policies corresponding to the first and second elements specified by the refref2IdleMobilityProfileLTE array parameter respectively. A larger element value indicates a higher probability that the UEs carry the corresponding IMMCI profile policy when they are released.
item.name: hLIMMCIProfileIndexPro

It is an array parameter consisting 16 elements and each element indicates the index of an E-UTRAN frequency to which the UEs with SPIDs can be redirected. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that no frequency is specified by the element.
item.name: refEutranFreqLTE

It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements that correspond to the frequencies specified by the refEutranFreqLTE (E-UTRA Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. A larger element value indicates that UEs are more likely to be redirected to the frequency corresponding to the element. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that UEs are not redirected to the frequency corresponding to the element.

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of the PCells used for EN-DC. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements that correspond to the frequencies specified by the EutraFreqIndex (E-UTRAN Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. Each element of this array parameter indicates the priority of the corresponding frequency used for EN-DC anchoring. A larger element value indicates a higher priority. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the frequency corresponding to this element cannot be used for EN-DC anchoring.
item.name: endcPccFreqPrio

item.desc: This parameter sets the indexes of the target E-UTRAN frequencies used for EN-DC anchoring. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. Each element indicates an E-UTRAN frequency that can be used for EN-DC anchoring. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that no frequency is specified by this element.
item.name: refEutranFreqLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of the frequencies used in the EN-DC anchoring IMMCI function for specific UEs. When a specific UE with the EN-DC capability is released, the dedicated IMMCI reselection priority is configured based on this parameter value. A larger parameter value indicates a higher reselection priority. The reselection priorities of the frequencies with the same parameter value are randomly sorted. The frequencies with the parameter value being zero are not carried in the dedicated reselection priority.
item.name: iMMCIEndcAnchFreqPri

item.desc: This parameter sets the priority carried for 2G/3G/4G/5G systems in EN-DC anchoring IMMCI. From left to right, the array subscripts correspond to the NR, E-UTRAN, UTRAN FDD, GERAN, CDMA2000-HRPD, and CDMA2000-1XRTT systems in turn. A larger parameter value indicates a higher IMMCI priority of the corresponding system. The value 0 indicates that the system is not considered. Note: The 4G system priority specified by this parameter is used for non-anchor frequencies only.
item.name: endcAnchIMMCIRATPri

item.name: reserve2

item.desc: This parameter sets the indexes of the target NR frequencies used for EN-DC anchoring. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements. Each element indicates an NR frequency that can be used for EN-DC anchoring. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that no frequency is specified by this element.
item.name: refEnbAdjFreqNRLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of the target frequencies used for NR coverage monitoring in EN-DC anchor-based handover. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements that correspond to the frequencies specified by the NRFreqIndex (NR Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. Each element of this array parameter indicates the priority of the corresponding NR frequency used for EN-DC anchoring. A larger element value indicates a higher priority. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the frequency corresponding to this element cannot be used for EN-DC anchoring.
item.name: endcAnchHoMonNRCovFPrio

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables EN-DC anchor-based handover to a high-priority anchor frequency. If it is set to Open, the NSA UEs in an anchor cell are handed over to a high-priority anchor frequency during an EN-DC anchor-based handover.
item.name: endcAnchToHighPrioSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables EN-DC anchor-based handover to a non-anchor frequency. If it is set to Open, the NSA UEs without any NR frequency available are handed over to a non-anchor frequency during an EN-DC anchor-based handover.
item.name: endcAnchToNonAnchHoSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables EN-DC anchor-based handover to a low-priority anchor frequency. If it is set to Open, the NSA UEs in an anchor cell are handed over to a low-priority anchor frequency during an EN-DC anchor-based handover.
item.name: endcAnchToLowPrioSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the working mode of EN-DC anchor-based handover. If this parameter is set to Handover Based LTE Anchor Coverage, the eNodeB hands over UEs from a non-anchor cell to an anchor neighbor cell that supports EN-DC anchor-based handover. If this parameter is set to Handover Based LTE Anchor and NR Coverage, the eNodeB hands over UEs from a non-anchor cell to an NR-covered anchor neighbor cell that supports EN-DC anchor-based handover.
item.name: endcAnchHoWorkMode

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the reselection from low-priority anchors to high-priority anchors for the EN-DC anchoring IMMCI function. If it is set to Open, after an NSA UE is released from the anchor frequency, the reselection priority in the anchoring IMMCI is determined based on the anchor priority of the serving frequency and that of different frequencies. If it is set to Close, after an NSA UE is released from the anchor frequency, the reselection priority of the serving frequency is set to the highest value and that of other anchor frequencies is sorted by anchor priority.
item.name: highPriAnchImmciSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables EN-DC anchor-based handover between anchors in accordance with the operator-defined strategy or SPID strategy. If this parameter is set to Open and an NSA UE connected to an anchor meets specific SPID conditions or operator-defined conditions and in the coverage without NR frequencies that can be configured as SNs, the eNodeB migrates the UE to another anchor through EN-DC-based handover, so that the UE can be configured with EN-DC on this anchor frequency.
item.name: endcAnchToAnchHoSwch

In the case of non-dual-measurement, only the first set of array elements is valid.

item.desc: This parameter is a two-dimensional array to enable inter-RAT measurement. It corresponds to a set of records of inter-frequency event A2 in the inter-RAT measurement parameter configuration table. One element corresponds to RSRP and the other to RSRQ. In the case of non-dual-measurement, only the first set of array elements is valid.
item.name: opeRatFMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the two-dimensional array indexes and indicates the measurement configurations based on coverage and intra-frequency handover. It corresponds to a set of records based on coverage and intra-frequency handover in the intra-system measurement parameter table. One element corresponds to RSRP and the other to RSRQ. In the case of non-dual-measurement, only the first set of array elements is valid.
item.name: intraFHOMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the two-dimensional array indexes to enable inter-frequency measurement. It corresponds to a set of records of inter-frequency event A2 in the intra-RAT measurement parameter configuration table. One element corresponds to RSRP and the other to RSRQ. In the case of non-dual-measurement, only the first set of array elements is valid.
item.name: opeInterFMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter is a two-dimensional array to disable inter-RAT measurement. It corresponds to a set of records of event A1 in the intra-RAT measurement parameter configuration table.
item.name: clsRatMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the array indexes and indicates the measurement configurations based on coverage and inter-frequency handover. It corresponds to a set of records based on coverage and inter-frequency handover in the intra-system measurement parameter table. One element corresponds to RSRP and the other to RSRQ. In the case of non-dual-measurement, only the first part is valid.
item.name: interFHOMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the index group IDs of inter-frequency PerQCI measurement configurations. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. The elements correspond to the inter-frequency PerQCI measurement configuration indexes specified by the refEutranFreqLTE (E-UTRA Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the configuration of the perQCIInterFreqMeaGrpCfg (Inter-frequency Measurement Configuration Index Group ID by QCI) parameter takes effect for the corresponding frequency at the cell level.

item.desc: This parameter sets the measurement configuration indexes for triggering handover or redirection to NR cells. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. The first through eighth elements correspond to the NR frequency measurement configuration indexes specified by the refEnbAdjFreqNRLTE (NR Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn if the triggering quantity is RSRP. The ninth through sixteenth elements correspond to the NR frequency measurement configuration indexes specified by the refEnbAdjFreqNRLTE (NR Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn if the triggering quantity is RSRQ. If the dualMeasSwitch (Switch of Dual Measurement) parameter is set to 0 (Close), only the first through eighth elements are valid.
item.name: nRMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter is a two-dimensional array to enable NR inter-RAT measurement. It corresponds to a set of records of inter-frequency event A2 in the inter-RAT measurement parameter configuration table. One element corresponds to RSRP and the other to RSRQ. In the case of non-dual-measurement, only the first set of array elements is valid.
item.name: opeNRMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the index group IDs of inter-frequency PerQCI measurement configurations. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. The elements correspond to the inter-frequency PerQCI measurement configuration indexes specified by the refEutranFreqLTE (E-UTRA Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the configuration of the perQCIInterFreqMeaGrpCfg (Inter-frequency Measurement Configuration Index Group ID by QCI) parameter takes effect for the corresponding frequency at the cell level.

item.desc: This parameter sets the index of the directional migration strategy of SA UEs.
item.name: profileIndex

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities for the target inter-RAT NR frequencies of the directional migration of SA UEs. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements, respectively corresponding to the frequencies set by the nRFreqIndex parameter. When the eNodeB delivers a directional migration measurement task for SA UEs, the measurement IDs of the corresponding frequencies are sorted based on the element values of this parameter. A larger element value indicates a higher priority of the frequency corresponding to the measurement ID. If an element is set to 0, the frequency is not selected when the eNodeB delivers a directional migration measurement task for SA UEs.
item.name: sADirectMigTargFreqPri

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of inter-RAT NR frequencies if the directional IMMCI function for SA UEs is enabled. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements. The elements correspond to the dedicated IMMCI priorities of the inter-RAT NR frequencies specified by the refEnbAdjFreqNRLTE (NR Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. A larger element value indicates a higher priority of the corresponding inter-RAT NR frequency. In this case, UEs are more likely to camp on the frequency. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that SA UEs do not carry the corresponding inter-RAT NR frequency when they are released.
item.name: sADirectIMMCINRFreqPri

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of E-UTRAN frequencies if the directional IMMCI function for SA UEs is enabled. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. Each element indicates the index of an E-UTRAN frequency on which SA UEs can camp. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that no E-UTRAN frequency is specified by this element.
item.name: refEutranFreqLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of different intra-RAT frequencies if the directional IMMCI function for SA UEs is enabled. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. The elements correspond to the dedicated IMMCI priorities of the frequencies specified by the refEutranFreqLTE (E-UTRAN Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. A larger element value indicates a higher priority of the corresponding frequency. In this case, UEs are more likely to camp on the frequency.
item.name: sADirectIMMCIInterFPri

item.desc: This parameter sets the priority carried for 2G/3G/4G systems in the directional IMMCI function of SA UEs. From left to right, the priority array subscripts correspond to the E-UTRAN, UTRAN FDD, GERAN, CDMA2000-HRPD, and CDMA2000-1XRTT systems in turn. A larger parameter value indicates a higher IMMCI priority of the corresponding system. The value 0 indicates that the system is not considered.
item.name: sADirectIMMCIRATPri

item.desc: This parameter sets NR frequencies for the directional migration and IMMCI functions of SA UEs. This parameter is an array parameter consisting of eight elements. Each element sets an NR frequency. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that this element does not index any NR frequency.
item.name: refEnbAdjFreqNRLTE

item.desc: This parameter determines how directional migration is executed for SA UEs. If it is set to Handover, the eNodeB migrates SA UEs to the NR system through handover. If it is set to Handover and Redirection, the eNodeB migrates SA UEs to the NR system preferentially through handover and then through redirection. If it is set to Redirection, the eNodeB migrates SA UEs to the NR system through redirection.
item.name: sADirectMigMethod

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique index of a measurement configuration for directional migration measurement of SA UEs. If it is set to 0, it indicates that no measurement configuration is specified for the directional migration of SA UEs.

Each element corresponds to an NR frequency and is uniquely associated with a measurement configuration. If the element corresponding to a frequency is 0, it indicates that no measurement configuration is specified for directional migration of the SA UEs on this frequency.
item.name: sADirectMigFreqMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the indexes of the target NR frequencies used for SN addition in EN-DC scenarios. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements. Each element indicates an NR frequency that can be used for SN addition in EN-DC scenarios. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that no frequency is specified by this element.
item.name: refEnbAdjFreqNRLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the frequency priorities of the PSCells for SN addition in EN-DC scenarios. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements that correspond to the frequencies specified by the NRFreqIndex (NR Carrier Frequency Index) array parameter in turn. Each element of this array parameter indicates the priority of the corresponding NR frequency used for SN addition in EN-DC scenarios. A larger element value indicates a higher priority. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the frequency corresponding to this element cannot be used for SN addition in EN-DC scenarios.
item.name: nrPSCellFreqPrio

item.desc: This parameter sets the voice-based EN-DC restriction strategy. If it is set to No Restrict, the addition of SNs is not restricted for the voice services of UEs. If it is set to No Based PCell Channel Quality and the PCell channel quality is bad for the voice services of UEs, no SN can be added. If it is set to No SN, no SN is added for voice services of UEs.
item.name: enDcRestrictStrgBaseVoice

item.desc: This parameter sets the inter-RAT NR measurement configuration index for SN addition in EN-DC when the SPID policy or the operator-customized policy takes effect. It is an array consisting of eight elements. Each element corresponds to an NR frequency and is uniquely associated with a measurement configuration. If the element corresponding to a frequency is 0, it indicates that no measurement configuration is specified for SN addition on this frequency in EN-DC.

If the ucInterFHOBasedVoLTEQualSwch parameter is set to Open, the measurement configuration corresponding to this index is sent to UEs for inter-frequency handover when the voice quality becomes bad.

item.desc: This parameter sets the measurement frequency indexes of VoLTE quality-based E-UTRAN handover. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. Each element indicates an E-UTRAN frequency that can be used for the VoLTE quality function. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that no frequency is specified by this element.
item.name: refEutranFreqLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the measurement priorities of the target frequencies for VoLTE quality-based inter-frequency handover. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements that indicate the priorities of the frequencies specified by the VoLTEQualProfLTE. RefEutranFreqLTE (Measurement Frequency Index of VoLTE Quality-Based E-UTRAN Handover) array parameter in turn. For the UEs that are identified as those with poor VoLTE quality by the eNodeB, a larger element value indicates that the priority for migrating the UEs to the corresponding frequency is higher. If an element is set to 0, the corresponding frequency is not used as the target frequency for VoLTE quality-based inter-frequency handover.

item.desc: This parameter determines whether the UEs of lower than AC10 can originate emergency calls.
item.name: operAcBarEmerCall

item.desc: This parameter sets the reference value of the probability of the access to a cell when a UE originates a call to establish an RRC connection. If the random number thrown by the UE is smaller than this parameter value, the UE can access the network. Otherwise, the UE cannot access the network. A larger parameter value indicates a higher probability of signaling access. A smaller parameter value indicates a lower probability of signaling access. Whether this parameter works depends on the restricted AC types in the accessClassBarringList parameter and whether the accessBarringInformation parameter is configured. In addition, if the AC Barring Working Mode parameter is set to a non-zero value, this parameter sets the minimum factor that the eNodeB can dynamically adjust to.
item.name: operAcProbFactorSig

item.desc: This parameter sets the average time for which UEs cannot access the network during signaling access. It is used when the timer T305 is configured. A larger parameter value indicates a longer period for signaling access and a longer delay. If it is set to the minimum value by default, the period for signaling access can be decreased.
item.name: operAcBarTimeSig

item.desc: This parameter sets access barring for Access Classes (ACs) 11 to 15 when a UE initiates a calling signaling access. From left to right, the first one is the access baring parameter for AC11, the second one for AC12, the third one for AC13, and so on.
item.name: operAcBarListSig

item.desc: This parameter sets the reference value of the probability of the access to a cell when a UE originates a call to establish an RRC connection. If the random number thrown by the UE is smaller than this parameter value, the UE can access the network. Otherwise, the UE cannot access the network. The parameter value 100% (1) indicates that no barring parameter is used. In addition, if the Ac-barring factors' working mode parameter is set to Dynamic, this parameter sets the minimum factor that the eNodeB can dynamically adjust to.
item.name: operAcProbFactOrig

item.desc: This parameter sets the average time for which UEs cannot access the network during call origination. It is used when the timer T303 is configured.
item.name: operAcBarTimeOrig

item.desc: This parameter determines whether the UEs of lower than AC10 can originate emergency calls.
item.name: operAcBarListOrig

item.desc: This parameter sets the access barring factor for multimedia voice UEs. It is used to prevent UEs from initiating the access procedure of multimedia voice calls. Before a UE initiates an access procedure of a multimedia voice call, a random number is generated. If the random number is smaller than the parameter value, the UE is allowed to initiate the access procedure. If the random number is larger than or equal to the parameter value, the UE is not allowed to initiate the access procedure.
item.name: operVoiceBarringFactor

item.desc: This parameter sets the access barring duration for multimedia voice UEs. It is used to control the interval for a UE to initiate another access procedure of a multimedia voice call. If a UE is forbidden to initiate the access procedure of multimedia voice calls, it cannot initiate another access procedure of a multimedia voice call during this period.
item.name: operVoiceBarringTime

item.desc: This parameter is an array of five elements to prevent the UEs of the corresponding AC levels from initiating multimedia voice calls. The elements correspond to AC11, AC12, AC13, AC14, and AC15 separately. If an element is set to No, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding AC level are allowed to initiate the access procedure of multimedia voice calls. If an element is set to Yes, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding AC level are not allowed to initiate the access procedure of multimedia voice calls.
item.name: operVoiceBarForSpecAC

item.desc: This parameter sets the access barring factor for multimedia video UEs. It is used to prevent UEs from initiating the access procedure of multimedia video calls. Before a UE initiates an access procedure of a multimedia video call, a random number is generated. If the random number is smaller than the parameter value, the UE is allowed to initiate the access procedure. If the random number is larger than or equal to the parameter value, the UE is not allowed to initiate the access procedure.
item.name: operVideoBarringFactor

item.desc: This parameter sets the access barring duration for multimedia video UEs. It is used to control the interval for a UE to initiate another access procedure of a multimedia video call. If a UE is forbidden to initiate the access procedure of multimedia video calls, it cannot initiate another access procedure of a multimedia video call during this period.
item.name: operVideoBarringTime

item.desc: This parameter is an array of five elements to prevent the UEs of the corresponding AC levels from initiating multimedia video calls. The elements correspond to AC11, AC12, AC13, AC14, and AC15 separately. If an element is set to No, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding AC level are allowed to initiate the access procedure of multimedia video calls. If an element is set to Yes, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding AC level are not allowed to initiate the access procedure of multimedia video calls.
item.name: operVideoBarForSpecAC

item.desc: This parameter sets the access barring factor for CSFB UEs. It is used to prevent UEs from initiating the access procedure of CSFB services. Before a UE initiates an access procedure of a CSFB service, a random number is generated. If the random number is smaller than the parameter value, the UE is allowed to initiate the access procedure. If the random number is larger than or equal to the parameter value, the UE is not allowed to initiate the access procedure.
item.name: operCSFBBarringFactor

item.desc: This parameter sets the access barring duration for CSFB UEs. It is used to control the interval for a UE to initiate another access procedure of a CSFB service. If a UE is forbidden to initiate the access procedure of CSFB services, it cannot initiate another access procedure of a CSFB service during this period.
item.name: operCSFBBarringTime

item.desc: This parameter is an array of five elements to prevent the UEs of the corresponding AC levels from initiating CSFB services. The elements correspond to AC11, AC12, AC13, AC14, and AC15 separately. If an element is set to No, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding AC level are allowed to initiate the access procedure of CSFB services. If an element is set to Yes, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding AC level are not allowed to initiate the access procedure of CSFB services.
item.name: operCSFBBarForSpecAC

It is used to determine whether to execute the camping load balancing based on the number of NSA UEs. If the proportion of the NSA UEs in a cell is larger than or equal to this threshold, the camping load balancing based on the number of NSA UEs is executed.

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum MCS value that can be used for downlink scheduling of SPID VoLTE UEs with QCI1 services. It is not applicable to the SPS function.

item.desc: This parameter sets the target BLERs for closed-loop power control of SPID QCI1 UEs. It is an array parameter consisting of four elements. The eNodeB calculates three path loss thresholds, A0, A1, and A2, which are in an ascending order. The following four path loss ranges are obtained based on the three thresholds: less than or equal to A0, A0 to A1, A1 to A2, and greater than A2. The four elements respectively set the target BLERs for SPID QCI1 UEs with path loss values in the four ranges, allowing refined power adjustment for SPID QCI1 UEs with different path loss values.
item.name: qci1TargetBler4Spid

item.desc: This parameter sets the target BLERs for closed-loop power control of SPID QCI2 UEs. It is an array parameter consisting of four elements. The eNodeB calculates three path loss thresholds, A0, A1, and A2, which are in an ascending order. The following four path loss ranges are obtained based on the three thresholds: less than or equal to A0, A0 to A1, A1 to A2, and greater than A2. The four elements respectively set the target BLERs for SPID QCI2 UEs with path loss values in the four ranges, allowing refined power adjustment for SPID QCI2 UEs with different path loss values.
item.name: qci2TargetBler4Spid

item.desc: This parameter sets the target MCS values for closed-loop power control of SPID QCI1 UEs. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements. The eNodeB calculates three path loss thresholds, A0, A1, and A2, which are in an ascending order. The following four path loss ranges are obtained based on the three thresholds: less than or equal to A0, A0 to A1, A1 to A2, and greater than A2. Elements 1 through 4 respectively set the target MCS values for SPID QCI1 UEs whose path loss values are in the four ranges in the scenario where 16QAM is used. Elements 5 through 8 respectively set the target MCS values for SPID QCI1 UEs whose path loss values are in the four ranges in the scenario where 64QAM or 256QAM is used. This parameter allows refined power adjustment for SPID QCI1 UEs with different path loss values.
item.name: qci1PcTargetMcs4Spid

item.desc: This parameter sets the target MCS values for closed-loop power control of SPID QCI2 UEs. It is an array parameter consisting of eight elements. The eNodeB calculates three path loss thresholds, A0, A1, and A2, which are in an ascending order. The following four path loss ranges are obtained based on the three thresholds: less than or equal to A0, A0 to A1, A1 to A2, and greater than A2. Elements 1 through 4 respectively set the target MCS values for SPID QCI2 UEs whose path loss values are in the four ranges in the scenario where 16QAM is used. Elements 5 through 8 respectively set the target MCS values for SPID QCI2 UEs whose path loss values are in the four ranges in the scenario where 64QAM or 256QAM is used. This parameter allows refined power adjustment for SPID QCI2 UEs with different path loss values.
item.name: qci2PcTargetMcs4Spid

item.desc: This parameter sets the window length for closed-loop PUSCH power control of SPID QCI1 UEs. When the number of scheduling operations performed for a SPID QCI1 UE reaches this parameter value, a new evaluation window for adjusting power control is started.
item.name: qci1PCWinThr4Spid

item.desc: This parameter sets the window length for closed-loop PUSCH power control of SPID QCI2 UEs. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Elements 0 and 1 set the window lengths for closed-loop PUSCH power control in LTE FDD cells. When the number of scheduling operations performed for a SPID QCI2 UE in an LTE FDD or LTE TDD cell reaches the values of elements 0 and 1, a new evaluation window for adjusting power control is started.
item.name: qci2PCWinThr4Spid

item.desc: This parameter sets the conservative value of the CCE aggregation level and power offset of the PDCCH for SPID QCI1 or QCI2 UEs (UEs that are configured with SPIDs and have QCI1 or QCI2 services). During a PDCCH adaptation procedure, the CCE aggregation level and power offset of the PDCCH are obtained based on the equivalent spectrum efficiency of the UE and this parameter value.
item.name: pdcchConsSwitch4SpidVoLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the conservative value of the CCE aggregation level and power offset of the PDCCH for SPID QCI1 or QCI2 UEs (UEs that are configured with SPIDs and have QCI1 or QCI2 services) when the CFI is 1. If the CFI is 1, the PDCCH is likely subject to interference. This parameter can be used to adjust the PDCCH index so that the PDCCH can use a higher CCE aggregation level or larger transmit power, avoiding PDCCH false-detection caused by neighbor cell interference.
item.name: cFI1Cons4SpidVoLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum increase of the PDCCH indexes to exceed the corresponding SE thresholds for SPID QCI1 or QCI2 UEs (UEs that are configured with SPIDs and have QCI1 or QCI2 services). During a PDCCH adaptation procedure, the PDCCH index can be obtained from this parameter.
item.name: pdcchIdxLimit4SpidVT

item.desc: This parameter sets the SPID configuration index of service-based handover policies. To apply different cell-level service-based handover policies for SPID UEs, set this parameter to the corresponding configuration index of the service-based handover policy. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that cell-level service-based handover policies are applied.

It can be used to index the corresponding VoLTE guarantee policy profile defined by the operator to enable the policy profile that is different from the cell-level VoLTE guarantee policy profile for SPID UEs. If this parameter is set to 0, the SPID-level VoLTE guarantee policy profile is disabled.

If it is set to Effective SA only, the eNodeB considers the UEs as single-mode SA UEs. If it is set to SA Priority, the eNodeB preferentially considers the UEs as SA UEs.

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of the dedicated-reselection and redirection functions. It is an array consisting of 16 elements. The functions corresponding to the first ten priority values of the array elements are as follows in turn: camping load balancing, CA UE-specific reselection priority policy, self-adaptive IMMCI adjustment for congestion control, intelligent-network distribution based on redirection for idle SPID UEs, intelligent-network distribution based on IMMCI for idle SPID UEs/SPID-based idle-mode mobility control, intelligent-network distribution for idle non-SPID UEs, EN-DC carrier anchoring in IMMCI/directional reselection of SA UEs in IMMCI, customized UE-specific IMMCI, MM network coordination based on UE migration in IMMCI, and IMMCI based on special UEs. A larger element value indicates a higher priority of the corresponding function. Other array elements (elements 11 to 16) are reserved.
item.name: idleUserDisFuncPri

The eNodeB does not select the E-UTRAN frequencies specified by this array parameter as the target frequencies for handover or redirection.

The eNodeB does not select the GERAN frequencies specified by this array parameter as the target frequencies for handover or redirection.
item.name: refGSMFreqLTE

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of 32 elements, each of which indicates a CDMA frequency where the UEs of the operator cannot be handed over or redirected. The eNodeB does not select the CDMA frequencies specified by this array parameter as the target frequencies for handover or redirection.
item.name: refCDMAFreqLTE

item.desc: This parameter determines whether the redirection to 2G/3G/4G systems can be triggered for the operator-defined UEs with QCI1 services. If it is set to 0 (Close), the redirection to 2G/3G/4G systems cannot be triggered for the UEs with QCI1 services. If it is set to 1 (Open), the redirection to 2G/3G/4G systems can be triggered for the UEs with QCI1 services.
item.name: qCI1RedSwch

item.desc: This parameter determines whether the redirection to NR systems can be triggered for the operator-defined UEs with QCI1 services. If it is set to 0 (Close), the redirection to NR systems cannot be triggered for the UEs with QCI1 services. If it is set to 1 (Open), the redirection to NR systems can be triggered for the UEs with QCI1 services.
item.name: nRQCI1RedSwch

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of 8 elements, each of which indicates an NR frequency where the UEs of the operator cannot be handed over or redirected. The eNodeB does not select the NR frequencies specified by this array parameter as the target frequencies for handover or redirection.
item.name: ref1EnbAdjFreqNRLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the list of NR frequencies to which the UEs with VoLTE services cannot be redirected. The NR frequency list is in the customized policy of the operator. A maximum of eight frequencies can be configured. If the OptSpecUsrStgyLTE. NRQCI1RedSwch (Switch of QCI1 Redirection to NR) parameter is set to Open, the frequencies in the frequency list cannot be used as the target frequencies of the UEs with VoLTE services when the UEs trigger redirection to the NR system. If the items in the list are all set to 0, it indicates that no frequency is forbidden to serve as the target frequency for redirection.
item.name: ref2EnbAdjFreqNRLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the operator-defined profile index of the customized strategy for cell-level specific voice scenarios. If the operator needs to make the strategy that is different from the customized strategy for cell-level specific voice scenarios effective, this parameter needs to be set to the corresponding profile index of the customized strategy for cell-level specific voice scenarios. If it is set to 0, it indicates that the customized strategy for cell-level specific voice scenarios takes effect.
item.name: refWcpStrategyProfLTE

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the interoperation function for SA UEs to be migrated to 5G networks. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the following functions can be enabled for UEs: migration from 4G to 5G based on coverage, fast return, directional migration in SA scenarios, and IMMCI-based directional migration in SA scenarios for idle UEs. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the following functions are disabled for UEs: migration from 4G to 5G based on coverage, fast return, directional migration in SA scenarios, and IMMCI-based directional migration in SA scenarios for idle UEs.
item.name: sAInterOperSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the Mobile Country Codes (MCCs) of equivalent PLMNs customized by the operator. It is an array parameter consisting of six elements. Elements 0 through 5 set the MCCs of PLMN1 through PLMN6 respectively. A PLMN is jointly determined by a Mobile Network Code (MNC) and an MCC.
item.name: custEquivalentMcc

item.desc: This parameter sets the Mobile Network Codes (MNCs) of equivalent PLMNs customized by the operator. It is an array parameter consisting of six elements. Elements 0 through 5 set the MNCs of PLMN1 through PLMN6 respectively. A PLMN is jointly determined by an MNC and a Mobile Country Code (MCC).
item.name: custEquivalentMnc

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables service-based handover. If this parameter is set to 1 (General Strategy), based on the services of a UE, the eNodeB attempts to hand over the UE to the target frequency corresponding to the QCI with the highest policy priority specified by the strategyPriority (Strategy Priority) parameter. If this parameter is set to 2 (WCP Strategy), the eNodeB triggers an inter-frequency or inter-RAT handover or redirection procedure and attempts to migrate the UE out of the current serving frequency when receiving a VoLTE service establishment request from the UE. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB does not trigger migration operations based on the services of UEs.
item.name: hOBaseServiceSwch

If the memory usage (used memory x 100/total memory) is higher than this threshold, it is considered that the load on the baseband board is high. In this case, the UDC function of the UEs to be connected to the network is controlled.
