item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the protection function for RRC reconfiguration. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Element 0 sets whether to enable the function for UEs using the data service, and element 1 sets whether to enable the function for UEs using the voice service. If an element is set to Open, the base station preferentially triggers the blind redirection procedure for the UEs whose RRC reconfiguration times out. If an element is set to Close, the base station triggers the release procedure (due to improper operation) for the UEs whose RRC reconfiguration times out.
item.name: rRCRecfgProtSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables intra-eNodeB inter-PLMN handover based on path switching. This parameter takes effect only if the Switch for Inter-PLMN Intra-eNodeB Handover (intraEnbInterPlmnHOSwch) parameter is set to 1 (Open). In network sharing scenarios, if this function is enabled, the eNodeB performs intra-eNodeB inter-PLMN handover based on the path switching message procedure. If this function is disabled, the eNodeB performs the intra-eNodeB inter-PLMN handover based on the HANDOVER REQUIRED message procedure.
item.name: intraEnbInterPlmnHOMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the load thresholds that are used for checking whether the average downlink spectrum efficiency of the cell is valid in the case that the downlink perception estimation policy is used. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements.Element 0 sets the threshold number of UEs used for checking whether the average downlink spectrum efficiency of the cell is valid. If this element is set to 20, it indicates that the threshold number of UEs is 20.Element 1 sets the downlink PRB usage threshold that is used for checking whether the average downlink spectrum efficiency of the cell is valid. If this element is set to 10, it indicates that the downlink PRB usage threshold is 10%. If this element is set to a value larger than 100, 100 is used.If the number of UEs in the cell is larger than or equal to the value of element 0 and the downlink PRB usage is larger than or equal to the value of element 1, the average downlink spectrum efficiency of the cell is valid.
item.name: percEstSEValidLoadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the reference factor indications for perception estimation. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements.Element 0 sets whether perception estimation is based on the downlink spectrum efficiency and indicates the specific reference downlink spectrum efficiency.If this element is set to 0, it indicates that perception estimation is based on the number of downlink MIMO layers instead of the downlink spectrum efficiency.If this element is set to 1, it indicates that perception estimation is preferentially based on the downlink fitting spectrum efficiency. If the information about the downlink fitting spectrum efficiency is incomplete, the eNodeB rolls back the downlink fitting spectrum efficiency to the number of downlink MIMO layers.If this element is set to 2, it indicates that perception estimation is preferentially based on the average downlink spectrum efficiency of the cell. If the information about the average downlink spectrum efficiency is incomplete, the eNodeB rolls back the average downlink spectrum efficiency to the number of downlink MIMO layers.Element 1 is reserved.
item.name: percEstRefeFactInd

item.desc: This parameter sets the intra-frequency neighbor cell selection policy. If this parameter is set to 0 (Overlapping Coverage Degree Mode), the eNodeB selects neighbor cells based on the overlapping coverage degree of the cells. If this parameter is set to 1 (Handover Ratio Mode), the eNodeB selects neighbor cells based on handover statistics and the default statistical period is 15 minutes. If this parameter is set to 0 (Overlapping Coverage Degree Mode), the statistical period is long (7 days by default) and measurement tasks need to be delivered by the eNodeB.
item.name: intraFreqNbrSelMode

item.desc: This parameter indicates an FGI mask. If a bit of the FGI is 1, the bit is valid.

item.desc: This parameter indicates the extended FGI of an R9 UE.

item.desc: This parameter indicates the extended FGI mask of an R9 UE. If a bit of the FGI is 1, the bit is valid.
item.name: specFGIR9AddMask

item.desc: This parameter indicates the extended FGI of an R10 UE.
item.name: specFGIR10Add

item.desc: This parameter indicates the extended FGI mask of an R10 UE. If a bit of the FGI is 1, the bit is valid.

item.desc: This parameter indicates the start digit of the software version number of a UE in the IMEISV.
item.name: minSpecSVN

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the PLMN-level DECOR function. It is an array parameter consisting of a maximum of eight elements. Each element of this parameter corresponds to one element of the MCC (Mobile Country Code) array parameter and one element of the MNC (Mobile Network Code) array parameter, indicating whether the DECOR function is enabled for the corresponding PLMN. If the decorSwch (Switch for DECOR) parameter is set to 1 (Open) and an element of this parameter is set to 1 (Open), it indicates that the DECOR function is enabled for the corresponding PLMN. If the DECOR function is enabled for a PLMN, the UEs in this PLMN can use the DCN configurations when selecting an MME during initial access and support rerouting on the S1 interface.
item.name: decorSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the Mobile Country Codes (MCCs) corresponding to the PLMN-level DECOR function. It is an array parameter consisting of a maximum of eight MCCs. The combination of an MCC and a Mobile Network Code (MNC) can determine a PLMN. This parameter is used to set whether the DECOR function can be enabled for a PLMN.
item.name: mcc

item.desc: This parameter sets the Mobile Network Codes (MNCs) corresponding to the PLMN-level DECOR function. It is an array parameter consisting of a maximum of eight MNCs. The combination of a Mobile Country Code (MCC) and an MNC can determine a PLMN. This parameter is used to set whether the DECOR function can be enabled for a PLMN.
item.name: mnc

item.desc: This parameter is DL SPS activation higher MCS threshold, used for limit MAC layer not enable DL SPS at high SINR. When higher layer enable DL SPS, the parameter should be configurable. And the parameter should be adjusted in the range of bigger than MCS15.
item.name: spsMcsHighThrDl

item.desc: This parameter is the percent of the PDSCH bandwidth to be occupied for DL SPS in a sub-frame, which is used for limit the RB number of DL SPS.

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of short-interval SPS. It determines the way that resources are allocated for short-interval SPS. If it is set to Fixed MCS/RB, the allocation with the fixed MCS or RB is used. If it is set to Fixed Bsr, the allocation with the fixed BSR is used.
item.name: shortSPSScheType

item.desc: This parameter sets the MCS that is used when the resource allocation type of short-interval SPS is fixed scheduling.
item.name: shortSPSFixedMCS

item.desc: This parameter sets the RB that is used when the resource allocation type of short-interval SPS is fixed scheduling.
item.name: shortSPSFixedRB

item.desc: This parameter sets the BSR that is used when the resource allocation type of short-interval SPS is fixed scheduling.
item.name: shortSPSFixedBSR

item.desc: This parameter sets the ratio of the bandwidth resources occupied by short-interval SPS UEs to total bandwidth resources.
item.name: shortSPSRbRatio

item.desc: This parameter sets the SINR activation threshold for short-interval SPS. When the SINR of a UE is higher than or equal to this threshold, short-interval SPS may be activated for the UE.
item.name: shortSPSSinrActThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the SINR deactivation threshold for short-interval SPS. When the SINR of a UE is lower than or equal to this threshold, short-interval SPS needs to be deactivated for the UE.
item.name: shortSPSSinrDeActThr

item.desc: When both QoS guarantee and short-interval SPS are enabled, this parameter is used to select the guaranteed services for which short-interval SPS can be activated. The eNodeB identifies the service type of a UE. When this parameter is set to a type, short-interval SPS is activated only for the UEs that have the service of this type. When this parameter is set to Close, short-interval SPS is likely to be activated for all the UEs that are configured with short-interval SPS services.
item.name: shortSPSGranType

item.desc: This parameter sets the timer for waiting for a response to a successful intra-RAT or inter-RAT handover of an LTE TDD VoLTE UE. It is called T304 for short. This timer is started when the VoLTE UE receives a handover command. When the response is received and indicates that the handover is successful, the timer stops. When the timer expires, indicating that the handover fails, the T311 (t311_Ue) timer is started and the cell with the best signal quality is selected as the target cell for handover.
item.name: t304Tdd4VoLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the timer for waiting for a response to a successful intra-RAT or inter-RAT handover of an LTE FDD VoLTE UE. It is called T304 for short. This timer is started when the VoLTE UE receives a handover command. When the response is received and indicates that the handover is successful, the timer stops. When the timer expires, indicating that the handover fails, the T311 (t311_Ue) timer is started and the cell with the best signal quality is selected as the target cell for handover.
item.name: t304Fdd4VoLTE

item.desc: This parameter indicates the maximum number of consecutive out-of-synchronization indications received by VoLTE UEs from the lower layers.
item.name: n310_VoLTE

item.desc: This parameter indicates the maximum number of consecutive synchronization indications received by VoLTE UEs from the lower layers.
item.name: n311_VoLTE

item.desc: Upon detecting a radio link problem, the VoLTE UE starts the timer T310_UE. Upon receiving an N311_UE in-sync indication, or triggering the handover procedure and the RRC re-establishment procedure, the UE stops the timer T310_UE. When the timer expires, the UE is in IDLE state if the security mode is not activated; otherwise, the RRC re-establishment procedure is initiated.
item.name: t310_Ue_VoLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets a timer to wait for a release command from the MME during an S1-based handover of a VoLTE UE. During the S1-based handover, this timer is started after the source eNodeB receives a handover command from the core network. The timer is stopped when the eNodeB receives a release command from the core network. If the eNodeB receives no release command from the core network when the timer expires, it indicates that the handover fails.
item.name: s1HoOverAllTimer4VoLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets a timer to wait for RRC connection completion of VoLTE UEs. This timer is started when the eNodeB sends an RRC Connection Reconfiguration message to a VoLTE UE. It is stopped when the eNodeB receives an RRC Connection Reconfiguration Complete message or an RRC Connection Re-establishment message. When the timer expires, the eNodeB releases the UE.
item.name: rRcReCfgTimer4VoLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets a timer to wait for a release message during an X2-based handover of a VoLTE UE. During the X2-based handover, this timer is started after the source eNodeB receives a Handover Request Acknowledge message. The timer is stopped when the eNodeB receives a release message from the target side. If the eNodeB receives no context release message from the target side when the timer expires, it indicates that the handover fails.
item.name: x2HoRelTimer4VoLTE

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the admission of the E-RABs of QCI1/QCI2 for eMTC terminals. If it is set to Open (1), the system allows eMTC terminals to establish the E-RABs of QCI1/QCI2. If it is set to Close (0), the system does not allow eMTC terminals to establish the E-RABs of QCI1/QCI2.
item.name: eMTCVoLTESwch

item.desc: This parameter is related to VoLTE ROHC. The reserved value for QCI1 is valid when VoLTE ROHC is enabled. A larger parameter value indicates a larger maxCID value reserved for QCI1, more flows established on QCI1, and smaller maxCID values for other QCIs.
item.name: qCI1RsvCid

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration from the time when the INVITE message is sent to the time when the setup of the QCI1 bearer stops or the timer expires. It is used to guarantee successful call setup in the scenarios where the QCI1 bearer has not been established.
item.name: forbidRedTimer

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables penalty for SRVCC-based handover preparation failures. For the cells where an SRVCC-based handover preparation failure is detected, if this parameter is set to Open, a penalty strategy is triggered based on the failure cause value.
item.name: sRVCCPunishSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the level-1 penalty timer for SRVCC preparation failures. The timer is enabled when the SRVCC penalty switch is set to Open.
item.name: sRVCCLevel1PunishTimer

item.desc: This parameter sets the level-2 detection timer for SRVCC preparation failures. The timer is enabled when the SRVCC penalty switch is set to Open.
item.name: sRVCCLevel2DetectTimer

item.desc: This parameter sets the level-2 penalty timer for SRVCC preparation failures. The timer is enabled when the SRVCC penalty switch is set to Open.
item.name: sRVCCLevel2PunishTimer

item.desc: This parameter sets the level-3 penalty timer for SRVCC preparation failures. The timer is enabled when the SRVCC penalty switch is set to Open.
item.name: sRVCCLevel3PunishTimer

item.desc: This parameter sets the level-3 detection timer for SRVCC preparation failures. The timer is enabled when the SRVCC penalty switch is set to Open.
item.name: sRVCCLevel3DetectTimer

item.desc: This parameter determines whether to recognize VoLTE MTs based on paging priorities. If it is set to Open, voice and video MTs can be recognized based on the paging priorities. This parameter can be used only when the core network marks the paging priorities for voice and video MTs.
item.name: voLTEMTRecogSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the valid period for recognizing the ID of a VoLTE MT. If a UE initiates an access procedure within a valid period after the paging priority of the UE is sent, the UE is regarded as a VoLTE MT; otherwise, it is not a VoLTE MT.
item.name: voLTEMTRecogPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the paging priority for recognizing VoLTE MTs. The first element of this parameter is used to identify the paging priority of a voice MT, and the second to identify that of the a video MT. If the paging priority of a UE is equal to the first element, the UE is regarded as a voice MT. If the paging priority of a UE is equal to the second element, the UE is regarded as a video MT.
item.name: voLTEMTPagingPriority

item.desc: This parameter sets the penalty strategy for an ordinary cause value of the SRVCC handover preparation failure. Three penalty strategies are available.
item.name: sRVCCNormCausePunishStgy

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of retries after an SRVCC handover preparation failure occurs. If the number of times that an SRVCC handover preparation failure occurs again during a specific period of time exceeds the threshold, the corresponding penalty strategy is implemented.
item.name: sRVCCRetryNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of penalties when the number of SRVCC handover preparation failures reaches the upper limit.
item.name: sRVCCPunishNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration for retry after an SRVCC handover preparation failure occurs. If the number of times that an SRVCC handover preparation failure occurs again during this period of time exceeds the threshold, the corresponding penalty strategy is implemented.
item.name: sRVCCRetryTmr

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the UE EUTRAN capability deletion function in the SRVCC procedure. If this switch is turned on, the UE EUTRAN capability information is not carried in the handover request during SRVCC. If this switch is turned off, the UE EUTRAN capability information in the SRVCC handover request is carried normally.
item.name: srvccUeCapDelSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the access identification strategy for the UEs with the EPS fallback service. If it is set to 0 (fuzzy identification), the eNodeB identifies all the connected SA UEs as the UEs with the EPS fallback service. If it is set to 1 (accurate identification), the eNodeB identifies the SA UEs with the access cause of mo-VoiceCall or emergency as the UEs with the EPS fallback service. For the identified UEs with the EPS fallback service, the eNodeB starts the protection timer to forbid the UEs to be handed over/redirected to the 5G system.
item.name: ePSFBAcIdentifyStgy

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables UE-level penalty in the case of SRVCC-based handover preparation failures. If it is set to Open, during the period specified by the UE-Level Penalty Timer for SRVCC-Based Handover Preparation Failures parameter, the eNodeB forbids a UE from triggering SRVCC-based handover to any neighbor cell if the eNodeB detects that the number of consecutive preparation failures in SRVCC-based handover of the UE to any neighbor cell is larger than or equal to the value of the Number of UE-Level SRVCC-Based Handover Preparation Failures parameter.
item.name: sRVCCPreFailUEPunSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration of the UE-level timer for detecting SRVCC-based handover preparation failures. If the value of the Number of UE-Level SRVCC-Based Handover Preparation Failures parameter is larger than 1, the eNodeB starts this timer when detecting a preparation failure in SRVCC-based handover to a neighbor cell. During the operation of this timer, if the eNodeB detects that the number of consecutive preparation failures in SRVCC-based handover of the UE to any neighbor cell is larger than or equal to the value of the Number of UE-Level SRVCC-Based Handover Preparation Failures parameter, the eNodeB stops this timer and starts the timer specified by the UE-Level Penalty Timer for SRVCC-Based Handover Preparation Failures parameter. If this timer expires, the eNodeB stops the detection. If this parameter is set to 65535, it indicates that this timer will never expire.
item.name: sRVCCPreFailDetectTimer

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration of the UE-level penalty timer for SRVCC-based handover preparation failures. If the eNodeB detects that the number of consecutive preparation failures in SRVCC-based handover of a UE to any neighbor cell is larger than or equal to the value of the Number of UE-Level SRVCC-Based Handover Preparation Failures parameter, the eNodeB starts this timer. During the operation of this timer, the UE cannot trigger SRVCC-based handover to any neighbor cell. If this parameter is set to 65535, the timer will never expire.
item.name: sRVCCPreFailPunishTimer

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of UE-level SRVCC-based handover preparation failures. If the eNodeB detects that the number of consecutive preparation failures in SRVCC-based handover of a UE to any neighbor cell is larger than or equal to this parameter value, it starts the timer specified by the UE-Level Penalty Timer for SRVCC-Based Handover Preparation Failures parameter. During the operation of the timer, the eNodeB forbids the UE from triggering SRVCC-based handover to any neighbor cell.
item.name: sRVCCPreFailDetNumber

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the delay in the release of VoLTE calls, that is, it determines whether the user inactivity function takes effect immediately. If it is set to Open, a UE starts the timer for delaying the release of its VoLTE service (UeTimerLTE. TUserInacVoLTE) after the VoLTE release procedure is initiated. The user inactivity function does not take effect until the timer expires. If this parameter is set to Close, the user inactivity function takes effect immediately after the VoLTE release procedure is initiated.
item.name: delayUserInacSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables UE capability enquiry optimization for voice UEs. If it is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB does not perform a second UE capability enquiry on the UEs in the EPSFB procedure or the voice UEs handed over from NR cells to LTE cells. If it is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB performs a second UE capability enquiry normally.
item.name: ePSFBUeCapEueryOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the timer (T304) for EPSFB TDD UEs to wait for successful handover. When an EPSFB UE receives a handover command during a handover from the 5G cell to the LTE TDD cell, this timer is started. If the UE is successfully handed over, this timer is stopped. If this timer expires, it indicates that the UE fails to be handed over. At this time, the timer T311 (Timer for UE to monitor radio link failure to idle (T311_UE)) is started.
item.name: t304Tdd4EPSFB

item.desc: This parameter sets the timer (T304) for EPSFB FDD UEs to wait for successful handover. When an EPSFB UE receives a handover command during a handover from the 5G cell to the LTE FDD cell, this timer is started. If the UE is successfully handed over, this timer is stopped. If this timer expires, it indicates that the UE fails to be handed over. At this time, the timer T311 (Timer for UE to monitor radio link failure to idle (T311_UE)) is started.
item.name: t304Fdd4EPSFB

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the adaptive recovery of speech waveform integrity based on packet prediction. If this parameter is set to Open and the eNodeB detects that a large number of packets are lost during VoLTE calls and user experience is affected, the eNodeB predicts the waveform based on the existing packets to recover the lost packets, achieving a smooth speech waveform and improve user experience.
item.name: volteRcySwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the downlink Code Mode Request (CMR) function. During a VoLTE call, if the downlink channel quality of the calling party is poor, the perception of the calling party is affected. If this parameter is set to Open, the eNodeB instructs the called party to reduce the coding rate, improving the perception of the calling party.
item.name: volteDlCmrSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the coherent-time threshold for abnormal release of QCI1 E-RABs. Suppose T2 (unit: 100 ms) is the time when the user plane receives a QCI1 E-RAB release message, carrying the release cause E-UTRAN Generated Reason, and T1 (unit: 100 ms) is the time when the user plane receives the latest uplink or downlink QCI1 RTP packet before receiving this release message. If the difference between T2 and T1 is larger than the parameter value, the abnormal QCI1 E-RAB release is considered to be a perceived call drop; otherwise, the abnormal QCI1 E-RAB release is considered to be a non-perceived call drop.
item.name: qci1ReleaseTimeThr

item.desc: If the core network sends a QCI1 E-RAB release message to the eNodeB, carrying the release cause E-UTRAN Generated Reason, it indicates that QCI1 E-RABs are abnormally released. This parameter enables or disables the identification of the QCI1 E-RABs that are abnormally released for this reason. Suppose T2 is the time when the user plane receives a QCI1 E-RAB release message, carrying the release cause E-UTRAN Generated Reason, and T1 is the time when the user plane receives the latest uplink or downlink QCI1 RTP packet before receiving this release message. If this parameter is set to Open and the difference between T2 and T1 is larger than the Qci1ReleaseTimeThr parameter (Coherent-Time Threshold for Abnormal QCI1 E-RAB Release), the abnormal QCI1 E-RAB release is considered to be a perceived call drop.
item.name: qci1RelByGeneratedSwch

item.desc: This parameter determines whether the special voice policy allows UE redirection to 4G networks. If this parameter is set to Open, UEs can be redirected to 4G cells after the service-based measurement waiting timer (ControlPlaneTimerLTE. MeasTimerBasedService) expires. If this parameter is set to Close, UEs cannot be redirected to 4G cells.
item.name: voiceAllowRdToEutranSwch

item.desc: This parameter controls the retransmission enhancement of downlink VoLTE RTP packets. This function can reduce the loss rate of downlink RTP packets by increasing the chances of RTP packet retransmission, improving the perception of users with VoLTE services. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), retransmission enhancement of downlink VoLTE RTP packets is disabled. If it is set to 1 (Retrans Enhance Based On HarqFailure), retransmission enhancement of downlink VoLTE RTP packets triggered by HARQ failures is enabled. If it is set to 2 (Retrans Enhance Based On HarqNack), retransmission enhancement of downlink VoLTE RTP packets triggered by HARQ NACK feedback is enabled. If it is set to 3, 4, or 5 (reserved value), it indicates that the function is disabled.
item.name: volteDlRtpReTxSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of times that the eNodeB receives HARQ NACK feedback messages before RTP packet retransmission is triggered. It is used to control the time at which RTP packets are retransmitted. If the ucVolteDlRtpReTxSwch (Switch for DL VoLTE RTP Retransmission Enhancement) parameter is set to 2 (Retrans Enhance Based On HarqNack) and the number of times that the eNodeB receives HARQ NACK feedback messages before RTP packet retransmission is triggered reaches this parameter value, the eNodeB determines whether RTP packet retransmission is triggered based on the MCS value of the current packet.
item.name: nackTime4TriggerDlReTx

item.desc: This parameter sets the MCS value threshold for triggering RTP packet retransmission. If the ucVolteDlRtpReTxSwch (Switch for DL VoLTE RTP Retransmission Enhancement) parameter is set to 2 (Retrans Enhance Based On HarqNack), the number of times that the eNodeB receives HARQ NACK feedback messages before RTP packet retransmission is triggered reaches the value of the ucNackTime4TriggerDlReTx (HARQ NACK Occasion for Triggering RTP Packet Retransmission) parameter, and the MCS value of the current packet is smaller than or equal to this parameter value, RTP packet retransmission is triggered.
item.name: mcsThrd4DlReTx

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of times that an RTP packet is retransmitted. If the ucVolteDlRtpReTxSwch (Switch for DL VoLTE RTP Retransmission Enhancement) parameter is set to 2 (Retrans Enhance Based On HarqNack) and RTP packet retransmission is triggered, the maximum number of times that an RTP packet is retransmitted is the value of this parameter.
item.name: rtpTransNum4DlReTx

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval for which RTP packets are retransmitted. If the ucVolteDlRtpReTxSwch (Switch for DL VoLTE RTP Retransmission Enhancement) parameter is set to 2 (Retrans Enhance Based On HarqNack) and RTP packet retransmission is triggered, RTP packets are retransmitted at the interval configured by this parameter and the number of times that RTP packets are retransmitted does not exceed the value of the ucRtpTransNum4DlReTx (Number of Times That an RTP Packet Is Retransmitted) parameter.
item.name: interval4DlReTx

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables VoLTE dejitter. If VoLTE dejitter is enabled, the eNodeB sets a cache area to evenly control the interval for sending RTP packets, reducing the jitter when UEs receive packets and improving the perception of users with VoLTE services. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), VoLTE dejitter is disabled. If it is set to 1 (Open), VoLTE dejitter is enabled. If it is set to 2 or 3 (reserved value), it indicates that VoLTE dejitter is disabled.
item.name: vtDejitterSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of RTP packets if VoLTE dejitter is enabled. It is an array parameter consisting of four elements. The first and second elements specify the thresholds of the number of RTP packets and are used to control the uplink jitter of RTP packets if VoLTE dejitter is enabled. The number of RTP packets is divided into three ranges: less than or equal to the first element value, larger than the first element value and less than or equal to the second element value, and larger than the second element value. The third and fourth elements specify the thresholds of the number of RTP packets and are used to control the downlink jitter of RTP packets if VoLTE dejitter is enabled. The number of RTP packets is divided into three ranges: less than or equal to the third element value, larger than the third element value and less than or equal to the fourth element value, and larger than the fourth element value. The first two ranges of the number of RTP packets specified by the first and second elements respectively correspond to the first and second elements of the aucRtpSendIntvl4Dejitter (Interval of RTP Packet Sending for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the uplink cache of the eNodeB is in the first range, the eNodeB sends uplink RTP packets at the interval specified by the first element of the aucRtpSendIntvl4Dejitter[4] (Interval of RTP Packet Sending for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the uplink cache of the eNodeB is in the second range, the eNodeB sends uplink RTP packets at the interval specified by the second element of the aucRtpSendIntvl4Dejitter[4] (Interval of RTP Packet Sending for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the uplink cache of the eNodeB is in the third range, the eNodeB continuously sends uplink RTP packets without any interval. The first two ranges of the number of RTP packets specified by the third and fourth elements respectively correspond to the third and fourth elements of the aucRtpSendIntvl4Dejitter (Interval of RTP Packet Sending for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the downlink cache of the eNodeB is in the first range, the eNodeB sends downlink RTP packets at the interval specified by the third element of the aucRtpSendIntvl4Dejitter[4] (Interval of RTP Packet Sending for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the downlink cache of the eNodeB is in the second range, the eNodeB sends downlink RTP packets at the interval specified by the fourth element of the aucRtpSendIntvl4Dejitter[4] (Interval of RTP Packet Sending for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the downlink cache of the eNodeB is in the third range, the eNodeB continuously sends downlink RTP packets without any interval.
item.name: thrRtpNum4Dejitter

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval at which RTP packets are sent if VoLTE dejitter is enabled. It is an array parameter consisting of four elements. The first and second elements correspond to the first and second ranges (specified by the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] (Threshold Number of RTP Packets for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter) of the numbers of RTP packets respectively and are used to control the uplink jitter of RTP packets if VoLTE dejitter is enabled. The third and fourth elements correspond to the third and fourth ranges (specified by the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] (Threshold Number of RTP Packets for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter) of the numbers of RTP packets respectively and are used to control the downlink jitter of RTP packets if VoLTE dejitter is enabled. If the number of RTP packets in the uplink cache of the eNodeB is smaller than or equal to the value of the first element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] (Threshold Number of RTP Packets for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter, the eNodeB sends uplink RTP packets at the interval specified by the first element of this parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the uplink cache of the eNodeB is larger than the value of the first element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] array parameter and smaller than or equal to the value of the second element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] array parameter, the eNodeB sends uplink RTP packets at the interval specified by the second element of this parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the uplink cache of the eNodeB is larger than the value of the second element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] array parameter, the eNodeB continuously sends uplink RTP packets without any interval. If the number of RTP packets in the downlink cache of the eNodeB is smaller than or equal to the value of the third element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] (Threshold Number of RTP Packets for VoLTE Dejitter) array parameter, the eNodeB sends downlink RTP packets at the interval specified by the third element of this parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the downlink cache of the eNodeB is larger than the value of the third element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] array parameter and smaller than or equal to the value of the fourth element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] array parameter, the eNodeB sends downlink RTP packets at the interval specified by the fourth element of this parameter. If the number of RTP packets in the downlink cache of the eNodeB is larger than the value of the fourth element of the ucThrRtpNum4Dejitter[4] array parameter, the eNodeB continuously sends downlink RTP packets without any interval.
item.name: rtpSendIntvl4Dejitter

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the interval for the eNodeB to cache RTP packets when VoLTE dejitter is enabled. It is used to control the cache overhead of the eNodeB. If the vtDejitterSwch (VoLTE Dejitter Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), an RTP packet is cached when the eNodeB receives the RTP packet and the buffer is not empty. If the buffer is empty and the interval between the current time and the time when an RTP packet is sent is shorter than the parameter value, the eNodeB caches the RTP packet. If the buffer is empty and the interval between the current time and the time when an RTP packet is sent is longer than or equal to the parameter value, the eNodeB sends the RTP packet without caching it.
item.name: thrInterval4BufferRTP

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to identify the EVS scheme. When a UE is using the VoLTE service and the eNodeB identifies the speech coding scheme of the UE, the eNodeB uses the processing policy for the voice packets in accordance with the speech coding scheme, improving user perception. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open for SIP Unencrypted) and SIP packets are not encrypted, the eNodeB identifies whether the speech coding scheme used by UEs is EVS by using the SIP messages (plaintext). If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB does not identify whether the speech coding scheme used by UEs is EVS.
item.name: evsIdentifySwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables CSFB delay optimization. If this parameter is set to 1, a UE can fall back to a 2G/3G network sooner when the eNodeB receives a CSFB instruction, reducing the CSFB delay and optimizing the CSFB handover performance.
item.name: csfbDelayOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether the eNodeB implements ROHC optimization for UEs. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB implements the ROHC optimization policy for the UEs that are handed over when they are performing VoLTE services, reducing the number of lost voice packets and improving the perception of the VoLTE UEs. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB does not implement the ROHC optimization policy for UEs.
item.name: rohcHoWithOpt

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables smart-CDR control. It is used to manually control the smart-CDR tool. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the smart-CDR tool can collect eNodeB data. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the smart-CDR tool cannot collect eNodeB data.
item.name: volteCdrControlSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of consecutive null voice packets. When the number of downlink RTP packets consecutively lost on the S1 interface or the number of downlink RTP packets consecutively lost due to HARQ failures is larger than the threshold, the ROHC end sends packets to reduce the number of ROHC decompression failures of UEs caused by packet loss on the S1 interface or downlink packet loss on the Uu interface.
item.name: rohcDlPktLossThr

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to forbid the redirection timer information from being transmitted between base stations. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the timer specified by the forbidRedTimer (Redirection Timer Forbidding) parameter is started, and an inter-site handover or re-establishment procedure is triggered, the eNodeB transmits the duration information of this timer to the target eNodeB, so that the timer can still take effect on the target eNodeB. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB does not transmit the duration information of this timer to the target eNodeB.
item.name: forbidRdTmrInheritSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables EPS fallback ringing protection. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB forbids handover or redirection of the EPS fallback UEs that are in the ringing phase and have no QCI1 bearer. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB does not provide this protection for EPS fallback UEs in the ringing phase.
item.name: ePSFB180RingProtectSwch

In MCG mode, a UE can set up bearers only on the 4G side. In SCG mode, the bearers of a UE can be migrate from the 4G side to the 5G side. In SCG Split mode, a UE can set up bearers on both the 4G side and 5G side.

If a GTPU path fails to be kept alive (that is, the link between the eNodeB and the SGW is disconnected), the Internet access services of the UE on the link are interrupted. This parameter controls whether the eNodeB releases the bearers of the UE on the link.
item.name: pathUnavailbleRptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the QCI corresponding to a service type. The eNodeB can detect service QoS parameters and application parameters through QCIs. The standard QCIs (QoS Classification Identifiers) represent QoS attributes, such as packet scheduling, delay, and packet loss rate. The transmission of standard QCI parameters among different NEs in an EPS helps the interconnection of the equipment from different vendors and flexible operator configuration.
item.name: qCI

item.desc: This parameter indicates the period of a DU's reporting data request status to the CU. With the feedback status-based flow control policy, flow control is executed at the CU side based on the fields carried in the status reports.
item.name: dataStatusReportPeriod

item.desc: This parameter indicates the range of historical scheduling-rate statistics (at the DU side). It is used to set the time window for calculating the historical scheduling rate for each bearer.
item.name: thpWindowCoeff

item.desc: This parameter indicates the step of historical-rate calculation for each bearer. The historical-rate time window is updated every wStepWindow (in ms), and the rate in the historical-rate time window is simultaneously updated.
item.name: stepWindow

item.desc: This parameter is used to calculate the historical rate when there is no BSR at the DU side. If the actual data size is very small, this parameter is used to calculate the rate in the historical-rate time window to keep service continuity.
item.name: minDataSize

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of times that a bearer at the DU side is congested. If the threshold is reached, it is considered that the radio link is congested.
item.name: dUConNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to determine whether the DU side needs to enter the congestion state based on the waiting delay in the dynamic flow control of 4G and 5G convergence. The DU side determines whether it needs to enter the congestion state based on the delay during which packets wait for scheduling. If the waiting delay exceeds the threshold value, it is considered that the DU is congested; otherwise, it is considered that the DU is not congested.
item.name: dUWaitDelayConThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to determine whether the DU side needs to relieve the congestion state based on the waiting delay in the flow control of 4G and 5G convergence. The DU side determines whether it needs to relieve the congestion state based on the delay during which packets wait for scheduling. If the waiting delay is shorter than the threshold, the DU side relieves the congestion state. If the waiting delay is longer than the threshold, the DU side maintains the congestion state.
item.name: dUWaitDelayDeConThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to determine whether the DU side needs to enter the congestion state based on the RLC buffer in the dynamic flow control of 4G and 5G convergence. The DU side determines whether it needs to enter the congestion state based on the delay during which packets wait for scheduling. If the waiting delay exceeds the threshold value, it is considered that the DU is congested; otherwise, it is considered that the DU is not congested.
item.name: rLCBufferingConThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to determine whether the DU side needs to relieve the congestion state based on the RLC buffer in the flow control of 4G and 5G convergence. The DU side determines whether it needs to relieve the congestion state based on the delay during which packets wait for scheduling. If the waiting delay is shorter than the threshold, the DU side relieves the congestion state. If the waiting delay is longer than the threshold, the DU side maintains the congestion state.
item.name: rLCBufferingDeConThrd

item.desc: This parameter determines whether an F1-U delay is considered in the downlink shunting of SCG split bearers. If this parameter is set to Open, the F1-U delay is considered during shunting. If this parameter is set to Close, the F1-U delay is not considered during shunting.
item.name: f1uDelayDetectSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval for obtaining the F1-U delay.
item.name: f1uDelayDetectPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the period for buffering the maximum data volume allowed by a bearer. It is used to calculate the maximum buffered data volume of the current air interface.
item.name: targetBufferingTime1

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum size of the cached data requested by the LTE DU side from the CU side. A larger parameter value indicates a larger amount of cached data volume that is requested.
item.name: minDesireBuffSize

item.desc: This parameter sets the policy used for calculating the flow control rate if there is no scheduling on the air interface.
item.name: flowCtrlRateCalcMethod

item.desc: This parameter sets inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategies to prevent ping-pong handover during 4G-5G interoperation. The parameter values are applicable to different ping-pong handover scenarios.
item.name: nRPreventPingPongStgy

item.desc: This array parameter enables or disables inter-RAT NR ping-pong prevention strategies (specified by the nRPreventPingPongStgy parameter). It consists of eight elements. The first element enables or disables the coverage-based ping-pong handover prevention strategy. If this element is set to 1 (Open) and coverage-based inter-RAT NR measurement configurations need to be delivered to UEs, the measurement configurations are delivered to the UEs based on the nRPrePingPongHOMeasCfg (Coverage-Based Inter-RAT NR Ping-Pong Handover Prevention Measurement Configuration) parameter value. The second element enables or disables the ping-pong handover prevention strategy for directional SA migration. If this element is set to 1 (Open) and the prePingPongSAMigMode (Ping-Pong Handover Prevention Policy for Directional SA Migration) parameter is set to 1 (Use Prevention Ping-Pong Handover Measurement Trigger Migration), measurement configurations for directional SA migration are delivered to UEs based on the prePingPongSAMigMeasCfg (Ping-Pong Handover Prevention Measurement Configuration for Directional SA Migration) parameter value. If the prePingPongSAMigMode parameter is set to 0 (Not Trigger Migration), no measurement configuration for directional SA migration is delivered to UEs. The remaining six elements are reserved.
item.name: nRPrePingPongSwch

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of 255 elements, indicating whether to enable inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategies based on QCI1 to QCI255 in turn. If an element is set to 1 (Yes), the eNodeB can enable the ping-pong handover prevention strategy for the QCI service corresponding to the element. If an element is set to 0 (No), the eNodeB disables the ping-pong handover prevention strategy for the QCI service corresponding to the element. The eNodeB can enable an inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategy (specified by the nRPreventPingPongStgy parameter) for a UE only if the inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategy indications of all the QCI services of the UE are set to 1 (Yes).
item.name: nRPerQCIPrePingPongInd

item.desc: This array parameter sets the frequencies for inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention. It consists of eight elements. Each element represents an index of an NR frequency. If an element is set to the index of a frequency, the eNodeB can enable an inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategy (nRPreventPingPongStgy) corresponding to this frequency.
item.name: refEnbAdjFreqNRLTE

item.desc: This array parameter sets the measurement configurations for coverage-based inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention. It consists of two elements. The first element corresponds to a set of inter-RAT NR measurement configuration items related to the RSRP and the second element corresponds to a set of inter-RAT NR measurement configuration items related to the RSRQ. If the dualMeasSwitch (Switch of Dual Measurement) parameter is set to 0 (Close), only the first element is valid.
item.name: nRPrePingPongHOMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets a ping-pong handover prevention strategy for directional SA migration. If it is set to 0 (Not Trigger Migration), no directional SA migration is performed on the UEs that are migrated from NR cells to LTE cells due to specific causes. If it is set to 1 (Use Prevention Ping-Pong Handover Measurement Trigger Migration), directional SA migration is performed on the UEs that are migrated from NR cells to LTE cells due to specific causes and the prePingPongSAMigMeasCfg (Ping-Pong Handover Prevention Measurement Configuration for Directional SA Migration) parameter takes effect.
item.name: prePingPongSAMigMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the ping-pong handover prevention measurement configuration for directional SA migration. It is an index that corresponds to an inter-RAT NR measurement configuration item.
item.name: prePingPongSAMigMeasCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention inheritance strategies. When an LTE UE carrying an inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention cause value initiates a handover to another LTE cell, this parameter is used to determine whether the cause value is carried during the handover procedure and whether to make an inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategy (specified by the nRPreventPingPongStgy parameter) still valid. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. The first element corresponds to the coverage-based handover function and the second element corresponds to a handover function other than coverage-based handover. If an element of this parameter is set to 1 (Yes) and the intra-RAT handover procedure corresponding to this element is triggered, an inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention cause value is carried and the configured inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategy is still valid after the UE is handed over to the target LTE cell. If an element of this parameter is set to 0 (No) and the intra-RAT handover procedure corresponding to this element is triggered, no inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention cause value is carried and the configured inter-RAT NR ping-pong handover prevention strategy is invalid for this UE after the UE is handed over to the target LTE cell.
item.name: nRPrePingPongInheritStgy

item.desc: This parameter sets the index of a smart space-division cell group. It indicates the unique ID of a space-division cell group in an eNodeB.
item.name: sSCGID

item.desc: This parameter sets the list of the cells within a smart space-division cell group. Each smart space-division cell group consists of one to four cells that are selected from the physical cells.
item.name: refCUEUtranCellFDDLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the space division mode of smart space-division cell groups: horizontal space division and horizontal-vertical space division, depending on UE distribution.
item.name: spaceDivMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of cells in a smart space-division cell group.
item.name: cellNumInSSCG

item.desc: This parameter sets the broadcast weight index of a smart space-division cell group. It identifies the broadcast weights used by the cells in a smart space-division cell group. Note: The letter H represents the width of horizontal beams, V represents the width of vertical beams, A represents the orientation of horizontal beams, and T represents the orientation of vertical beams. For example, 'P4_MAP0213_SDM0_CellNum4' in 79:P4_MAP0213_SDM0_CellNum4[C0:H12_V18_A-45_T0][C1:H12_V18_A-15_T0][C2:H12_V18_A15_T0][C3:H12_V18_A45_T0] reflects the H, V, A, and T values. 'P4' indicates that the number of Tx antenna ports supported by a cell is 4. 'MAP0213' indicates that the mapping relation of antenna ports and antenna channels is 02130213021302130213021302130213. SDM0 indicates that the space division mode of the smart space-division cell group is horizontal space division. If it is SDM1, it indicates that the space division mode is horizontal-vertical space division. 'CellNum4' indicates that the number of cells in the smart space-division cell group is 4. In [C0:H12_V18_A-45_T0][C1:H12_V18_A-15_T0][C2:H12_V18_A15_T0][C3:H12_V18_A45_T0], each [] contains the broadcast weight information (H, V, A, and T values) of a cell and C0 to C3 represents four cells separately.
item.name: bCIndexInSSCG1

item.desc: This parameter sets the broadcast weight index of a smart space-division cell group. It identifies the broadcast weights used by the cells in a smart space-division cell group. Note: The letter H represents the width of horizontal beams, V represents the width of vertical beams, A represents the orientation of horizontal beams, and T represents the orientation of vertical beams. For example, 'P4_MAP0213_SDM0_CellNum4' in 79:P4_MAP0213_SDM0_CellNum4[C0:H12_V18_A-45_T0][C1:H12_V18_A-15_T0][C2:H12_V18_A15_T0][C3:H12_V18_A45_T0] reflects the H, V, A, and T values. 'P4' indicates that the number of Tx antenna ports supported by a cell is 4. 'MAP0213' indicates that the mapping relation of antenna ports and antenna channels is 02130213021302130213021302130213. SDM0 indicates that the space division mode of the smart space-division cell group is horizontal space division. If it is SDM1, it indicates that the space division mode is horizontal-vertical space division. 'CellNum4' indicates that the number of cells in the smart space-division cell group is 4. In [C0:H12_V18_A-45_T0][C1:H12_V18_A-15_T0][C2:H12_V18_A15_T0][C3:H12_V18_A45_T0], each [] contains the broadcast weight information (H, V, A, and T values) of a cell and C0 to C3 represents four cells separately.
item.name: bCIndexInSSCG2

item.desc: This parameter sets the broadcast weight index of a smart space-division cell group. It identifies the broadcast weights used by the cells in a smart space-division cell group. Note: The letter H represents the width of horizontal beams, V represents the width of vertical beams, A represents the orientation of horizontal beams, and T represents the orientation of vertical beams. For example, 'P4_MAP0213_SDM0_CellNum4' in 79:P4_MAP0213_SDM0_CellNum4[C0:H12_V18_A-45_T0][C1:H12_V18_A-15_T0][C2:H12_V18_A15_T0][C3:H12_V18_A45_T0] reflects the H, V, A, and T values. 'P4' indicates that the number of Tx antenna ports supported by a cell is 4. 'MAP0213' indicates that the mapping relation of antenna ports and antenna channels is 02130213021302130213021302130213. SDM0 indicates that the space division mode of the smart space-division cell group is horizontal space division. If it is SDM1, it indicates that the space division mode is horizontal-vertical space division. 'CellNum4' indicates that the number of cells in the smart space-division cell group is 4. In [C0:H12_V18_A-45_T0][C1:H12_V18_A-15_T0][C2:H12_V18_A15_T0][C3:H12_V18_A45_T0], each [] contains the broadcast weight information (H, V, A, and T values) of a cell and C0 to C3 represents four cells separately.
item.name: bCIndexInSSCG3

item.desc: This parameter sets the broadcast weight index of a smart space-division cell group. It identifies the broadcast weights used by the cells in a smart space-division cell group. item.name: bCIndexInSSCG4

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables downlink power sharing for the UEs in smart space-division cell groups. If it is set to Open, the UEs in smart space-division cell groups can share downlink power in the same cell or between cells.
item.name: sSCGDLPowerShareSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets a downlink power sharing scheme for the UEs in smart space-division cell groups when the Switch for DL Power Sharing of the UEs in Smart Space-Division Cell Groups parameter is set to Open. It can be set to 0 (Dynamic Power Sharing Scheme), 1 (Power Sharing Scheme with Semi-static Correction of ERS Power), or 2 (Power Sharing Scheme with Semi-static Correction of PA Power). If it is set to Dynamic Power Sharing Scheme, it indicates that power sharing is implemented between beams at the TTI level. If it is set to Power Sharing Scheme with Semi-static Correction of ERS Power, it indicates that power sharing is implemented through the adjustment of ERS power between beams in a semi-static manner. If it is set to Power Sharing Scheme with Semi-static Correction of PA Power, it indicates that power sharing is implemented through the adjustment of the PA between beams in a semi-static manner.
item.name: sSCGDLPowerShareMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum CRS power increase if the power sharing scheme with the semi-statically corrected ERS is used for smart space-division cell groups. During power sharing, the CRS power increase of a busy cell cannot exceed the parameter value.
item.name: sSCGPwrShareMaxDeltaERS

item.desc: This parameter sets the PUCCH resource coordination mode of the cells in smart space-division groups. If it is set to 0, neighbor cells do not coordinate with each other. In this case, the number of occupied RBs is small. If it is set to 1, the frequency domains between neighbor cells are completely orthogonal. In this case, the number of occupied RBs is the maximum. If it is set to 2, the frequency domains between neighbor cells are partially orthogonal. In this case, the number of RBs occupied by the PUCCH matches the PUCCH interference coordination performance.
item.name: pucchMode4SSCG

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables HVAT-based broadcast weights for a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG). If it is set to 1 (Open), the broadcast weights of an SSCG can be adjusted based on HVAT values as required.
item.name: sSCGHVATCfgSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the HVAT-based broadcast weight mode of a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG). It is valid when the cellRSPortNum (Number of Tx Antenna Port in Cell) parameter is set to 4.
item.name: sSCGHVATMode

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of four elements. It is used to adjust the horizontal beamwidths of four cells in a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG). It takes effect if the sSCGHVATCfgSwch (HVAT-Based Broadcast Weight Switch of an SSCG) parameter is set to 1 (Open). The four elements of the array parameter indicate the horizontal beamwidths (in degrees) of cell 0, cell 1, cell 2, and cell 3 separately.
item.name: sSCGHorizontalBeamwidth

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of four elements. It is used to adjust the vertical beamwidths of four cells in a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG). It takes effect if the sSCGHVATCfgSwch (HVAT-Based Broadcast Weight Switch of an SSCG) parameter is set to 1 (Open). The four elements of the array parameter indicate the vertical beamwidths (in degrees) of cell 0, cell 1, cell 2, and cell 3 separately.
item.name: sSCGVerticalBeamwidth

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of four elements. It is used to adjust the horizontal beam directions of four cells in a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG). It takes effect if the sSCGHVATCfgSwch (HVAT-Based Broadcast Weight Switch of an SSCG) parameter is set to 1 (Open). The four elements of the array parameter indicate the horizontal beam directions (in degrees) of cell 0, cell 1, cell 2, and cell 3 separately.
item.name: sSCGHorizontalDIRA

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of four elements. It is used to adjust the vertical beam directions of four cells in a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG). It takes effect if the sSCGHVATCfgSwch (HVAT-Based Broadcast Weight Switch of an SSCG) parameter is set to 1 (Open). The four elements of the array parameter indicate the vertical beam directions (in degrees) of cell 0, cell 1, cell 2, and cell 3 separately.
item.name: sSCGVerticalDIRT

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables differentiated power sharing for the UEs in Smart Space-Division Cell Groups (SSCGs). It is used to determine whether to preferentially perform power sharing for specified types of UEs. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB preferentially performs power sharing for specified types of UEs. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB does not preferentially perform power sharing for specified types of UEs. The specified types of UEs refer to the UEs for which the dLKeyServType (Downlink Key Service Type Indicators) parameter is set to 1.
item.name: sSCGDiffPwrShareSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the subframe offset strategy of CSI-RS resources of the cells in SSCGs of LTE FMM base stations. It is used to control CSI-RS staggering in the time domains. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the CSI-RS resources of the cells in SSCGs are transmitted in different time domains, and the data service interference of neighbor cells can be detected through CSI-RS measurement. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the CSI-RS resources of the cells in SSCGs are transmitted in the same time domain, and the data service interference of neighbor cells cannot be detected through CSI-RS measurement.
item.name: cSIRSSfOffsetSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the policy for limiting the maximum number of available uplink RBs in a smart space-division cell group.If this parameter is set to 0, there is no limitation on the maximum number of available uplink RBs in a smart space-division cell group.If this parameter is set to 1, the number of available PUSCH PRBs in a cell cannot exceed 50% of the total number of RBs available for PUSCHs in the available uplink bandwidth of the entire cell.If this parameter is set to 2, the number of available PUSCH PRBs in a cell cannot exceed 1/N (N is the number of cells in the smart space-division group) of the total number of resource blocks available for PUSCHs in the available uplink bandwidth of the entire cell.If this parameter is set to 3, the number of available PUSCH PRBs in a cell can be adjusted adaptively.
item.name: ulSSCGRbLimitPolicy

item.desc: This parameter sets the actual number of RBs occupied by the PUCCH for the cells in a Smart Space-Division Group (SSCG). It is used for inter-cell PUCCH resource coordination in a synchronized shared control channel group scenario. The eNodeB coordinates the communication among the cells based on this parameter value to optimize the resource allocation on the PUCCH.
item.name: sSCGPucchRbNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of blanking RBs occupied by the PUCCH for the cells in a Smart Space-Division Group (SSCG). The eNodeB coordinates the PUCCH usage among the cells in the SSCG based on this parameter value to reduce interference and improve the uplink resource usage.
item.name: sSCGPucchBlankNum

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables PUCCH resource coordination optimization among the cells in a Sub-Slot Coordination Group (SSCG). If this parameter to 0 (Close) and the number of RBs occupied by the PUCCH is different for the cells in the SSCG, the effect of PUCCH resource coordination among cells may be weakened, reducing the communication efficiency. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), PUCCH resources can be effectively coordinated among cells to ensure communication quality and improve system resource utilization.
item.name: sSCGPucchOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to restrict the maximum number of streams scheduled in TM9 mode. It is used to control the TM9 scheduling policy. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the maximum number of streams in all the cells in an SSCG in TM9 mode does not exceed the value of the cellRSPortNum (Number of Tx Antenna Port in Cell) parameter of the corresponding cells to prevent resource allocation from exceeding the physical-resource allocation capability and ensure communication quality.
item.name: tM9MaxFlowLimitSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables resource pooling for the cells in a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG). If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the cells that are in the SSCG and involved in DSS can share the same optical fiber channel with NR cells, thus optimizing the usage of optical fiber resources.
item.name: dSSPoolingSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the Traffic Offload Function (TOF). If it is set to Open, the eNodeB sends uplink data to the MEC for traffic offload, reducing the delay in data services.
item.name: tofSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of the Traffic Offload Function (TOF). It takes effect when the tofSwitch (TOF Switch) parameter is set to Open. If it is set to Full Shunting Mode, it indicates that the TOF is performed on all the uplink data. If it is set to PLMN-Based Shunting Mode, it indicates that the TOF is performed on uplink data based on PLMNs, that is, the TOF is performed on only the UEs in the selected PLMNs.
item.name: tofStrategy

item.desc: A PLMN-based local Traffic Offload Function (TOF) strategy identifies UEs based on the Mobile Country Code (MCC) and Mobile Network Code (MNC) of the PLMN.
item.name: refPlmn

item.desc: This parameter sets a list of SPIDs configured for the TOF. It is an array parameter consisting of a maximum of eight elements. If the tofSwitch (TOF Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the TofSpidSwch (SPID-Based TOF Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), and the SPID of a UE is in the list specified by this array parameter, the eNodeB offloads the traffic of the UE data to the PDN server on the MEC platform.
item.name: tofSPID

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the TOF based on SPIDs. If the tofSwitch (TOF Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), this parameter is set to 1 (Open), and the SPID of a UE is in the list specified by the TofSPID (SPIDs for the TOF) array parameter, the eNodeB offloads the traffic of the UE data to the PDN server on the MEC platform.
item.name: tofSpidSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the index of a migration policy for energy saving by traffic guidance. It uniquely identifies a migration policy for energy saving by traffic guidance.
item.name: eCGuidMigStgCfgIdx

item.desc: This parameter indicates the currently applied traffic guidance mode for energy saving. In normal traffic guidance mode, it is required that UE migration for energy saving by traffic guidance should not degrade user experience too much. In deep traffic guidance mode, UE migration for energy saving by traffic guidance aims to achieve the best energy saving effect and thus user experience may not be guaranteed.
item.name: eCGuidMod

item.desc: This parameter sets the UE migration period for energy saving by traffic guidance. If the Switch of UE Migration for Energy Saving by Traffic Guidance parameter is set to 1 (Open), the system migrates UEs for energy saving by traffic guidance every the period specified by this parameter.
item.name: eCGuidMigCycle

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of UEs migrated for energy saving by traffic guidance in every period.
item.name: eCGuidMigUENum

item.desc: This parameter indicates whether the UEs of a QCI service can be migrate out of the target cell for energy saving by traffic guidance. This parameter is valid when the Switch of UE Migration for Energy Saving by Traffic Guidance parameter is set to 1 (Open). This parameter is an array with 25 elements. Element 1-9 respectively indicate whether the UEs of the services containing QCIs 1, 2, 3,... 9 can be migrated out of the cell for energy saving by traffic guidance. The last 16 elements of the array are reserved. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding QCI service can be migrated out of the cell for energy saving by traffic guidance. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the UEs of the corresponding QCI service cannot be migrated out of the cell for energy saving by traffic guidance.
item.name: eCGuidMigQCIList

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the uplink PRB usage in the serving cell for triggering UE migration for energy saving by traffic guidance. When the uplink PRB usage in the serving cell is lower than the threshold, UEs can be triggered to migrate to neighbor cells for energy saving by traffic guidance.
item.name: guidServULPRBRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the downlink PRB usage in the serving cell for triggering UE migration for energy saving by traffic guidance. When the downlink PRB usage in the serving cell is lower than the threshold, UEs can be triggered to migrate to neighbor cells for energy saving by traffic guidance.
item.name: guidServDLPRBRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the uplink PRB usage of the migration target cell for energy saving of the serving cell by traffic guidance. A cell can be selected as a candidate migration target cell only when the uplink PRB usage in the cell is lower than or equal to the threshold.
item.name: guidNeighULPRBRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the downlink PRB usage of the migration target cell for energy saving of the serving cell by traffic guidance. A cell can be selected as a candidate migration target cell only when the downlink PRB usage in the cell is lower than or equal to the threshold.
item.name: guidNeighDLPRBRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink PDCP rate threshold for migrating UEs for energy saving by traffic guidance. If the downlink PDCP packet rate of a UE is lower than or equal to the threshold for N consecutive evaluation periods, the UE is considered as a low-rate UE. N indicates the Number of DL Rate Evaluation Periods for UEs of Traffic Guidance. If the downlink PDCP packet rate of a UE is larger than the threshold in an evaluation period, the UE is considered as a non-low-rate UE. if a UE does not meet the condition for a low-rate UE or the condition for a non-low-rate UE, the UE rate status remains unchanged. With the traffic guidance function for energy saving, only the low-rate UEs are migrated. If this parameter is set to the maximum value, all UEs are considered as downlink low-rate UEs.
item.name: guidUEDLPDCPRateThd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold ratio of the RRC-connection UEs in the serving cell for triggering UE migration for energy saving by traffic guidance. When the ratio of the RRC-connection UEs in the serving cell is lower than the threshold, UEs can be triggered to migrate to neighbor cells for energy saving by traffic guidance.
item.name: guidServRRCRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the coverage overlapping degree threshold for selecting target neighbor cells to which UEs are migrated for energy saving by traffic guidance. A neighbor cell can be selected as a candidate migration target cell only when the overlapping coverage degree between the neighbor cell and the serving cell is larger than the threshold.
item.name: guidNeighCovOverlapThd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold ratio of the RRC-connection UEs in the target cell for triggering UE migration for energy saving by traffic guidance. A cell can be selected as a candidate migration target cell only when the ratio of the RRC-connection UEs in the cell is lower than or equal to the threshold.
item.name: guidNeighRRCRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of periods for which a UE migrated out of the cell by traffic guidance is consecutively evaluated for the downlink rate. If the downlink PDCP packet rate of a UE is lower than or equal to the DL PDCP Rate Threshold for UEs Migrated Out for Energy Saving by Traffic Guidance for the number of consecutive periods configured by this parameter, the UE is considered as a low-rate UE;
item.name: guidDLRateEvalPeriNum

item.name: perQCIStrategyGrpCfg

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration of the service-based measurement waiting timer. After delivering a service-based inter-frequency handover measurement configuration, the eNodeB starts this timer and waits for a measurement report. Before this timer expires, the eNodeB attempts to trigger a handover to the target frequency if it receives the measurement report. After this timer expires, the eNodeB redirects the UE to the target frequency if the hoBaseServiceMeasExpiRedSwch parameter is set to Open. Otherwise, the delivered service-based handover measurement configuration is deleted. The parameter value 65535 indicates that the timer duration is infinite, that is, the eNodeB does not redirect any UE to the target frequency or delete the delivered service-based handover measurement configuration.
item.name: measTimerBasedService

item.desc: This parameter sets the cell capacity type. It indicates the number of UEs that can be configured with SR, CQI, or SRS resources in the cell. If this parameter is set to 0 (1200 user capacity), it indicates that about 1200 UEs can be supported. If this parameter is set to 1 (800 user capacity), it indicates that about 800 UEs can be supported. If this parameter is set to 2 (400 user capacity), it indicates that about 400 UEs can be supported. If this parameter is set to 3 (200 user capacity), it indicates that about 200 UEs can be supported. If this parameter is set to 4 (adaptive capacity), it indicates that the SR, CQI, or SRS resources can be configured based on the cell capacity type corresponding to the actual number of UEs in the cell. If this parameter is set to 0 or 1, CQI resources may fail to be configured for 1200 or 800 UEs in some TDD scenarios.

item.desc: The sampling rate determines the capacity of optical ports. A lower sampling rate requires a smaller optical-port capacity. For a 20 MHz bandwidth, if the sampling rate mode is set to 0, it indicates that the sampling rate is 30.72 Mbps.For a 20 MHz bandwidth, if the sampling rate mode is set to 1, it indicates that the sampling rate is 23.04 Mbps.For a 20 MHz bandwidth, if the sampling rate mode is set to 2, it indicates that the sampling rate is 19.2 Mbps.For a 15 MHz bandwidth, if the sampling rate mode is set to 0, it indicates that the sampling rate is 30.72 Mbps.For a 15 MHz bandwidth, if the sampling rate mode is set to 1, it indicates that the sampling rate is 23.04 Mbps.For a 15 MHz bandwidth, if the sampling rate mode is set to 2, it indicates that the sampling rate is 19.2 Mbps.For a 10 MHz, 5 MHz, 3 MHz, or 1.4 MHz bandwidth, the sampling rate mode can be set to 0 only.In this case:For a 10 MHz bandwidth, the sampling rate is 15.36 Mbps.For a 5 MHz bandwidth, the sampling rate is 7.68 Mbps.For a 3 MHz bandwidth, the sampling rate is 7.68 Mbps.For a 1.4 MHz bandwidth, the sampling rate is 7.68 Mbps.Only the sampling rate modes, instead of the specific sampling rate values, are displayed on the GUI.
item.name: sampleRateCfg

item.desc: This parameter indicates the type of the noise matrix. If it is set to MRC, the MRC algorithm is used for interference suppression. If it is set to IRC, the IRC algorithm is used for interference suppression. If it is set to Adaptive-Config, the interference suppression algorithm is adaptively selected based on the NI interference value.
item.name: matrixType

item.desc: This parameter sets how to divide RB resources in a network sharing scenario. It is used to select an RB division method when multiple operators share cell bandwidth resources. It is valid only when the number of operators to which the cells belong is larger than 1. Case 1: The operators can occupy a part of spectrum resources separately and can share some spectrum resources, but cannot preempt non-shared resources. Case 2: The operators can occupy a part of spectrum resources separately, but cannot share or preempt any spectrum resource. Case 3: The operators can share all the spectrum resources of a cell, which means that RB division is disabled. Case 4: The operators can occupy a part of spectrum resources separately and can preempt spectrum resources. Case 5: In congestion scenarios, the operators can share all the spectrum resources or admit UE access requests proportionally; in non-congestion scenarios, the operators can admit all the UE access requests. Case 6: The RB resource preemption policy based on the operator group priority is used. Case 7: The RB resource preemption policy with flexible ratio is used.
item.name: rbSharMode

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of six elements. It is used to set the proportions of downlink bandwidth resources allocated to PLMNs in network sharing scenarios. The elements in the array parameter indicate the proportions of the downlink bandwidth resources allocated to PLMN 1 through PLMN 6 configured for a cell in turn.
item.name: ratioOperatorn

item.desc: This parameter sets the proportion of downlink bandwidth resources shared by PLMNs. The downlink bandwidth resources allocated in the proportion specified by this parameter can be shared by multiple PLMNs.
item.name: ratioShared

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables downlink MU-MIMO in TM7, TM78, and TM9 modes. For a macro station, the bits in the bitmap indicate TM7, TM8, and TM9 from low to high bits, with the bit value 0 indicating SU-MIMO and 1 indicating MU-MIMO. If a bit is set to 1, MU-MIMO is enabled for the corresponding TM. In this case, the UEs in this TM attempt to perform MU-MIMO pairing with other UEs that are in similar conditions. If a bit is set to 0, MU-MIMO is disabled for the corresponding TM. In this case, the UEs in the corresponding TM do not attempt to perform MU-MIMO pairing with other UEs. In a TMM scenario, if this parameter is set to 8, TM7 MU-MIMO and TM8 MU-MIMO are supported, but hybrid TM7-TM8 MU-MIMO or TM9 MU-MIMO is not supported. If this parameter is set to 9, TM7 MU-MIMO, TM8 MU-MIMO, and hybrid TM7-TM8 MU-MIMO are supported, but TM9 MU-MIMO is not supported. If this parameter is set to 10, TM7 MU-MIMO, TM8 MU-MIMO, TM9 MU-MIMO, and hybrid TM7-TM8-TM9 MU-MIMO are supported.
item.name: bfmumimoEnableDl

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables power or spectrum sharing. If it is set to 1, LTE cells can use the shared GSM spectrum resources. If it is set to 2, LTE cells can use the shared UMTS spectrum resources. If it is set to 4, the NB-IoT network can use LTE spectrum resources. If it is set to 8, the NB-IoT network can use LTE power resources. The mapping relation between the parameter values and the functions is as follows:1: Magic Radio GLCSS switch 2: Magic Radio ULCSS switch 4: Switch for spectrum sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks 5: Switch for Magic Radio GLCSS and spectrum sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks 6: Switch for Magic Radio ULCSS and spectrum sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks 8: Switch for power sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks 9: Switch for Magic Radio GLCSS and power sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks 10: Switch for Magic Radio ULCSS and power sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks 12: Switch for spectrum sharing and power sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks 13: Switch for spectrum sharing and power sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks, and Magic Radio GLCSS 14: Switch for spectrum sharing and power sharing between LTE and NB-IoT networks, and Magic Radio ULCSS.

item.desc: This parameter is used to support the selection of PUSCH channel estimation,between time domain estimation, Frequency domain estimation and optimized Frequency domain estimation.
item.name: puschChEstType

item.desc: This parameter sets the highest speed of the high-speed railways covered by the serving cell. Based on the highest speed, the baseband adaptively adjusts the thresholds related to uplink frequency deviation processing and downlink frequency deviation pre-compensation.
item.name: speedInd

item.desc: The Time Threshold to Exit Atmospheric Duct Interference.
item.name: atmosphericQuitPerid

item.desc: This parameter sets the power decrease threshold for atmospheric duct interference. A larger parameter value indicates faster inter-symbol interference decrease.
item.name: atmosphericDecPowrThres

item.desc: The Switch for Interference Source Localization in Atmospheric Duct Interference.
item.name: atmosphericLocationSwch

item.desc: The Switch for Symbol Rollback in Atmospheric Duct Interference.
item.name: atmosphericSymBackSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the suppression threshold for atmospheric duct interference.
item.name: atmosphericSupresThres

item.desc: The Time Threshold T1 to Entry Interference Suppression in Atmospheric Duct Interference.
item.name: atmosphericSupresEnterPerid

item.desc: The Time Threshold T2 to Exit Interference Suppression in Atmospheric Duct Interference.
item.name: atmosphericSupresQuitPerid

item.desc: This parameter indicates the number of antennas used by the UL PHY to detect signature sequences in atmospheric ducting interference.
item.name: atmosphericSeqDemAntNum

item.desc: The Detection Threshold of Detecting Signature Sequence in Atmospheric Duct Interference.
item.name: atmosphericSeqDemParaThres

item.desc: The Switch of 1RB Allocation.
item.name: oneRBAllocateSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the function of restricting UE services based on the TA obtained based on measurement. In the case that this parameter is set to Open, if the distance between a UE and the base station is longer than the threshold specified by the taMaxThr parameter, the base station releases the UE. In the case that this parameter is set to Close, the base station does not release a UE due to its distance with the UE.
item.name: taLimitedReleaseSwch

item.desc: TM4 4*4 MIMO Switch, TM4 4*4 MIMO will be used when switch is open in TM4, 4*2 MIMO or 2*2 MIMO will be used when it's closed in TM4.
item.name: tm44T4RSwch
