If the parameter set to Filter user with high and low PRB usage based on PDCCH CCE Trigger ,the cell will filter users with high and low PRB usage.
item.name: cCEBaseBUEPRBThrdSwchDl

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge whether select user according to packet size for load balance based on PDCCH CCE Trigger. If the parameter set to Close ,the strategy is invalid. If the parameter set to Short packet based on PDCCH CCE Trigger ,the cell will select users with bearer of short packet. If the parameter set to Long packet based on PDCCH CCE Trigger ,the cell will select users with bearer of long packet.
item.name: cCEBasedLBPacketSelSwch

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge whether decide location according to MCS for load balance based on PRB Trigger. If the parameter set to Close ,the strategy is invalid. If the parameter set to Centre User based on PRB Trigger ,the cell will select centre users. If the parameter set to Edge user based on PRB Trigger ,the cell will select edge users.
item.name: cCEBaseBMCSSelectSwchDl

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to select CA UEs for load balancing based on the PDCCH CCE usage. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), CA UEs can be selected. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), CA UEs cannot be selected.
item.name: cCEBaseBCAFilterSwchDl

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge whether sort UE according to PRB for load balance based on PDCCH CCE Trigger. If the parameter set to Descending order with PRB based on PDCCH CCE Trigger,the cell selects users of the candidate in descending order. If the parameter set to Ascending order with PRB based on PDCCH CCE Trigger ,the cell selects users of the candidate in ascending order.
item.name: cCEBasedUESortOrder

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge whether the service cell offload to the cell or frequency without load information. When the Downlink scheduling PDCCH CCE usage of service cell exceeds this parameter, the cell or frequency without load information may be used as candidate target cell or frequency.
item.name: pDCCHCCEOffloadThrdDl

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge whether the service cell offload to the cell or frequency without load information. When the Uplink scheduling PDCCH CCE usage of service cell exceeds this parameter , the cell or frequency without load information may be used as candidate target cell or frequency.
item.name: pDCCHCCEOffloadThrdUl

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge relative load leveling between serving cell and Intra-LTE neighbor cells in downlink. When Downlink scheduling PDCCH CCE usage difference between serving cell and a Intra-LTE neighbor cell is below this parameter, this cell can't be used as candidate target cell in downlink for Intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: pDCCHCCENLoadRelaThrdDl

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge relative load leveling between serving cell and Intra-LTE neighbor cells in uplink. When Uplink scheduling PDCCH CCE usage difference between serving cell and a Intra-LTE neighbor cell is below this parameter, this cell can't be used as candidate target cell in uplink for Intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: pDCCHCCENLoadRelaThrdUl

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge load leveling of Intra-LTE neighbour cells in downlink.When the Downlink based scheduling PDCCH CCE usage of a Intra-LTE neighbour cell in downlink exceeds this parameter,this cell can't be used as candidate target cell in downlink for Intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: pDCCHCCEIntraNLoadThrdDl

item.desc: This parameter is used to judge load leveling of Intra-LTE neighbour cells in uplink. When the Uplink based scheduling PDCCH CCE usage of a Intra-LTE neighbour cell exceeds this parameter,this cell can't be used as candidate target cell in uplink for Intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: pDCCHCCEIntraNLoadThrdUl

item.desc: This parameter is used to execute load balancing function in downlink. When the Downlink based scheduling PDCCH CCE usage of LTE serving cell exceeds this parameter during the counter window, the cell executes load balancing in downlink.
item.name: pDCCHCCELBExeThrdZDl

item.desc: This parameter is used to execute load balancing function in uplink. When the Uplink based scheduling PDCCH CCE usage of LTE serving cell exceeds this parameter during the counter window, the cell executes load balancing in uplink.
item.name: pDCCHCCELBExeThrdZUl

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for the instantaneous proportion of the number of UEs for jointly triggering load balancing. When the period of load balancing expires and the proportion of the number of RRC-Connected UEs in the serving cell exceeds this threshold, load balancing is triggered for the serving cell if any one of the following KPIs is larger than or equal to the corresponding threshold: proportion of the number of RRC-Connected UEs, uplink PRB usage, downlink PRB usage, usage of PDCCH CCEs for downlink scheduling, and usage of PDCCH CCEs for uplink scheduling.
item.name: lBJointTriRRCRatioThrd

item.desc: It controls whether to enable the target cell/frequency sorting strategy of CA UEs for load balancing based on the number of UEs.
item.name: cULBTargetSort4CAUESwch

item.desc: This parameter controls whether to enable the target cell/frequency sorting strategy of CA UEs for load balancing based on PRBs.
item.name: pRBLBTargetSort4CAUESwch

item.desc: This parameter is used to trigger the Load Balance based on PRB. When the period of Load Balance has expired, and the CU number of LTE serving cell is larger than or equal to this parameter, it will tigger Load Balance based on PRB as if PRB ratio satisfies triggering condition.
item.name: pRBbaseBRRCNumThrdDl

item.desc: This parameter is the switch of the SPID function for load balancing.
item.name: lBSpidSwch

item.desc: This parameter is the switch of the PRB-based eMBMS filter. If the switch is turned on, the eNodeB does not select eMBMS UEs for load balancing. If the switch is turned off, the eNodeB can select eMBMS UEs for load balancing.
item.name: prbBaseBeMBMSFilterSwchDl

item.desc: This parameter is the switch of the PDCCH CCE-based eMBMS filter. If the switch is turned on, the eNodeB does not select eMBMS UEs for load balancing. If the switch is turned off, the eNodeB can select eMBMS UEs for load balancing.
item.name: cceBaseBeMBMSFilterSwchDl

item.desc: This parameter is the switch of the CU-based eMBMS filter. If the switch is turned on, the eNodeB does not select eMBMS UEs for load balancing. If the switch is turned off, the eNodeB can select eMBMS UEs for load balancing.
item.name: cuBaseBeMBMSFilterSwchDl

item.desc: This parameter controls whether to enable the target cell/frequency sorting strategy of CA UEs for load balancing based on CCEs.
item.name: cCELBTargetSort4CAUESwch

item.desc: This parameter determines whether to select MU UEs for CCE-triggered load balancing. If it is set to Close, the cell selects MU UEs. If it is set to Open, the cell does not select MU UEs.
item.name: cCEBasedMUPropotionSwch

item.desc: This parameter indicates the admission control threshold for the ratio of the number of UEs in a cell for load balancing. When the number of UEs in the cell for load balancing is larger than or equal to the threshold, the incoming handover UEs for load balancing are rejected.
item.name: lBHOCURatioACThrd

item.desc: This parameter indicates the admission control threshold of the UL PRB usage for load balancing. When the UL PRB usage in the cell for load balancing is larger than or equal to the threshold, the incoming handover UEs for load balancing are rejected.
item.name: lBHOPRBRatioACThrdUl

item.desc: This parameter indicates the admission control threshold of the DL PRB usage for load balancing. When the DL PRB usage in the cell for load balancing is larger than or equal to the threshold, the incoming handover UEs for load balancing are rejected.
item.name: lBHOPRBRatioACThrdDl

item.desc: This parameter indicates the admission control threshold of the UL PDCCH CCE usage for load balancing. When the UL PDCCH CCE usage in the cell for load balancing is larger than or equal to the threshold, the incoming handover UEs for load balancing are rejected.
item.name: lBHOCCERatioACThrdUl

item.desc: This parameter indicates the admission control threshold of the DL PDCCH CCE usage for load balancing. When the DL PDCCH CCE usage in the cell for load balancing is larger than or equal to the threshold, the incoming handover UEs for load balancing are rejected.
item.name: lBHOCCERatioACThrdDl

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the load balancing handover-based admission control strategy. If it is set to Open, the strategy is enabled. If it is set to Close, the strategy is disabled.
item.name: swch4ACBaseBHODl

item.desc: This parameter indicates the threshold of the number of real-time UEs for triggering PRB-based camping load balancing. When a UE is released by the eNodeB and the number of UEs in RRC CONNECTED status in the LTE serving cell is larger than or equal to this parameter, the serving cell triggers PRB-based camping load balancing if the PRB usage satisfies the triggering condition.
item.name: pRBbasedCLBRRCNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables load balancing frequency configuration. If it is set to Open, different execution thresholds can be configured for each frequency.
item.name: perFLBCfgSwch

item.desc: This parameter determines whether the release messages sent by the eNodeB to UEs carry the reselection IMMCI dedicated to Camping Load Balancing (CLB). When the eNodeB sends a release message to a UE, a random number between 0 and 1 is generated. If the random number is smaller than or equal to the parameter value, the release message sent by the eNodeB to the UE can carry the CLB-dedicated reselection IMMCI, so that it is easier for the UE to reselect another frequency through CLB, thus reducing the load of the serving cell. If the random number is larger than the parameter value, the release message sent by the eNodeB to the UE cannot carry the CLB-dedicated reselection IMMCI. In this case, it is more difficult for the UE to reselect another frequency through CLB.
item.name: cLBUERatioFactorwithIMMCI

item.desc: This parameter indicates the ratio of the number of UEs that are measured in centralized connected load balancing to the number of UEs with balanced load. The number of UEs that are measured in centralized connected load balancing is the number of UEs with balanced load multiplied by this parameter value.
item.name: centConLBMeasUENumRatio

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the RF fingerprinting strategy for load balancing. It is used to determine whether RF fingerprinting is used for load balancing. If measurement-based load balancing is used and this parameter is set to HO based on measurement, the system makes UEs perform measurement-based load balancing handover. If measurement-based load balancing is used and this parameter is set to HO without measurement, the system makes UEs perform load balancing handover without measurement.
item.name: rFFingerPrintLBSwch

item.desc: This parameter indicates whether the cell supports centralized load balancing or not. If it is set to Support, the cell executes centralized load balancing when the eNodeB is connected to T-Robot and centralized load balancing is enabled. If it is set to Not Support, the cell executes distributed load balancing.
item.name: supportCentLB

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to select NSA UEs for load balancing. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), NSA UEs can be selected. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), NSA UEs cannot be selected.
item.name: lBNSAUEFilterSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables special overload processing for idle SPID UEs. If it is set to Open, the special overload processing policy for idle SPID UEs is executed. If it is set to Close, the original processing policy for idle SPID UEs is executed.
item.name: cLBSpidSpecHandleSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the step for automatically adjusting the measurement threshold for load balancing in each period.
item.name: lBMeasThrdAdjStep

item.desc: This parameter sets the step for automatically adjusting the edge threshold for the MCS center in each period.
item.name: mCSThrdAdjStep

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables automatic adjustment for load balancing parameters.
item.name: lbParaAdaptSwch

item.desc: This parameter is used to filter out the UEs with too low PRB usage during load balancing. If the PRB usage of a UE is lower than this threshold, the UE is filtered out.
item.name: uePrbFilterLowThrd1

item.desc: This parameter is used to determine whether the bearer of a UE is a short-packet bearer or a long-packet bearer. If the number of RBs of a UE is greater than or equal to this threshold, the bearer of the UE is a bearer with long packets. If the number of RBs of a UE is smaller than this threshold, the bearer of the UE is a bearer with short packets.
item.name: lbPacketSelectThrd1

item.desc: This parameter is used to filter out the UEs with too high PRB usage during load balancing. If the PRB usage of a UE is higher than this threshold, the UE is filtered out.
item.name: uePrbFilterHighThrd1

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of load balancing periods for which automatic parameter adjustment must meet the requirements for measurement report proportions.
item.name: lbParaAdaptDecPeriodNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of load balancing periods for which the effect of automatic parameter adjustment needs to be observed.
item.name: lbParaAdaptObsPeriodNum

item.desc: This parameter determines the PLMN restriction policy for the neighbor cells on the target frequencies for Camping Load Balancing (CLB). If it is set to Close, the target frequencies for CLB are not restricted by PLMNs. If it is set to Only Serving PLMN, the target frequencies for CLB are those corresponding to the neighbor cells that support the serving PLMN of UEs. If it is set to Serving PLMN and Equivalent PLMNs, the target frequencies for CLB are those corresponding to the neighbor cells that support the serving PLMN and the equivalent PLMNs of UEs.
item.name: cLBRestrictPLMNSwch

item.desc: This parameter determines whether to preferentially select the UEs whose fingerprint information can be queried for load balancing based on RF fingerprint information. If it is set to Close, the UEs that meet the UE selection policy for load balancing are selected during the UE selection for fingerprint-based load balancing. If this parameter is set to Open, the UEs whose fingerprint information can be queried are selected for fingerprint-based load balancing.
item.name: lbPrioSelRffUeSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the anchoring target selection strategy for NSA UEs during load balancing. If it is set to Open and the candidate frequency is an anchor frequency, for NSA UEs, the cells that do not support EN-DC on the anchor frequency cannot be used as the target cells for load balancing. If it is set to Close, the cells that support and do not support EN-DC can all be used as the target cells for load balancing.
item.name: lbNSAAnchorSelectSwch

item.desc: This parameter determines whether to use the load information of different vendors for load balancing. If it is set to Close, no load information of different vendors is used for load balancing. If it is set to Open, the load information of different vendors is used for load balancing.
item.name: lBInterManuLoadInfoSwch

item.desc: This parameter controls whether the user-quantity-based load balancing function uses the PLMN policy for user selection. If this parameter is set to Open, the PLMN policy is used for user selection, that is, if the number of UEs in the serving cell is smaller than the load balancing execution threshold of the serving PLMN, UEs are not considered as target UEs of user-quantity-based load balancing. If this parameter is set to Close, the PLMN policies is not used for user selection.
item.name: lBCUUEPlmnSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether only the UEs that meet the PLMN policy carry Camping Load Balancing (CLB) IMMCIs when they are released if CLB based on the number of UEs is enabled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), only the UEs that meet the PLMN policy carry CLB IMMCIs, that is, if the number of UEs in the serving cell is smaller than the CLB execution threshold of the serving PLMN, the UEs carry CLB IMMCIs when they are released. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the PLMN policy is not used to determine whether UEs can carry CLB IMMCIs.
item.name: cLBCUUEPlmnSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the camping load balancing algorithm based on the number of NSA UEs. It is used to determine whether to enable camping load balancing based on the number of NSA UEs.
item.name: nsaClbSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the relative threshold number of NSA UEs in neighbor cells for camping load balancing. It is used to determine the number of NSA UEs in intra-LTE neighbor cells. If the difference between the proportions of NSA UEs in the serving cell and an intra-LTE neighbor cell separately is smaller than this threshold, this cell cannot be not selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: nsaClbNbrCuLoadRelaThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for executing camping load balancing based on the number of NSA UEs. It is used to determine whether to execute the camping load balancing based on the number of NSA UEs. If the proportion of the NSA UEs in a cell is larger than or equal to this threshold, the camping load balancing based on the number of NSA UEs is executed.
item.name: nsaClbCuExeThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of NSA UEs in neighbor cells for camping load balancing. It is used to determine the number of NSA UEs in intra-LTE neighbor cells. If the proportion of NSA UEs in an intra-LTE neighbor cell is higher than this threshold, this cell cannot be selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: nsaClbNbrCuLoadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the denominator that is used to calculate the proportion of the number of RRC-connected NSA UEs for load balancing. A larger parameter value indicates that it is more difficult to trigger the load balancing based on the number of NSA UEs.
item.name: lbNsaUeNumThrd

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables load balancing for intelligent space-division groups after intelligent cell space division is executed. If it is set to Open, the load of the cells in an intelligent space-division group can be reduced through UE migration.
item.name: muGroupLBSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for executing downlink PRB-based load balancing for the home space-division group of the serving cell. Within a measurement period, if the downlink PRB usage of the home space-division group of the serving LTE cell is higher than or equal to this threshold and the downlink PRB usage of the home neighbor coverage group is higher than or equal to the threshold for executing downlink PRB-based load balancing for the neighbor coverage groups, downlink PRB-based load balancing for space-division groups is performed in the serving cell.
item.name: dlPRBLBExeTd4MuGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for executing uplink PRB-based load balancing for the home space-division group of the serving cell. Within a measurement period, if the uplink PRB usage of the home space-division group of the serving LTE cell is higher than or equal to this threshold and the uplink PRB usage of the home neighbor coverage group is higher than or equal to the threshold for executing uplink PRB-based load balancing for the neighbor coverage groups, uplink PRB-based load balancing for space-division groups is performed in the serving cell.
item.name: ulPRBLBExeTd4MuGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink-PRB overload threshold for the space-division groups of neighbor cells in space-division group-based load balancing. It is used to check the level of the downlink PRB load of the space-division groups of neighbor cells. For an intra-LTE neighbor cell, if the downlink PRB usage of space-division groups is higher than or equal this threshold, the neighbor cell cannot be selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: dlPRBOverLdTd4MuGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for executing downlink PRB-based load balancing for the neighbor coverage groups of the serving cell. Within a measurement period, if the downlink PRB usage of the home space-division group of the serving LTE cell is higher than or equal to the threshold for executing downlink PRB-based load balancing for space-division groups and the downlink PRB usage of the home neighbor coverage group is higher than or equal to this threshold, downlink PRB-based load balancing for space-division groups is performed in the serving cell.
item.name: dlPRBLBExeTd4NbrGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for executing uplink PRB-based load balancing for the neighbor coverage groups of the serving cell. Within a measurement period, if the uplink PRB usage of the home space-division group of the serving LTE cell is higher than or equal to the threshold for executing uplink PRB-based load balancing for space-division groups and the uplink PRB usage of the home neighbor coverage group is higher than or equal to this threshold, uplink PRB-based load balancing for space-division groups is performed in the serving cell.
item.name: ulPRBLBExeTd4NbrGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink-PRB overload threshold for the space-division groups of neighbor cells in space-division group-based load balancing. It is used to check the level of the uplink PRB load of the space-division groups of neighbor cells. For an intra-LTE neighbor cell, if the uplink PRB usage of space-division groups is higher than or equal this threshold, the neighbor cell cannot be selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: ulPRBOverLdTd4MuGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink-PRB relative-threshold for the space-division groups of neighbor cells in space-division group-based load balancing. It is used to check the level of the uplink PRB load of the space-division groups of neighbor cells. If the difference between the uplink PRB usage of the home space-division group of the serving cell and that of an intra-LTE neighbor cell is less than this threshold, the neighbor cell cannot be selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: ulPRBOverLdRelaTd4MuG

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink-PRB relative-threshold for the space-division groups of neighbor cells in space-division group-based load balancing. It is used to check the level of the downlink PRB load of the space-division groups of neighbor cells. If the difference between the downlink PRB usage of the home space-division group of the serving cell and that of an intra-LTE neighbor cell is less than this threshold, the neighbor cell cannot be selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: dlPRBOverLdRelaTd4MuG

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink-PRB overload threshold for the neighbor coverage groups of neighbor cells in space-division group-based load balancing. It is used to check the level of the uplink PRB load of the neighbor coverage groups of neighbor cells. For an intra-LTE neighbor cell, if the uplink PRB usage of neighbor coverage groups is higher than or equal this threshold, the neighbor cell cannot be selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: ulPRBOverLdTd4NbrGroup

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink-PRB overload threshold for the neighbor coverage groups of neighbor cells in space-division group-based load balancing. It is used to check the level of the downlink PRB load of the neighbor coverage groups of neighbor cells. For an intra-LTE neighbor cell, if the downlink PRB usage of neighbor coverage groups is higher than or equal this threshold, the neighbor cell cannot be selected as a candidate target cell for intra-LTE load balancing.
item.name: dlPRBOverLdTd4NbrGroup

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables load balancing based on the cell traffic condition. If it is set to Open and the load balancing algorithm is not disabled (the lbSwch parameter is not set to Close), load balancing based on the traffic condition is triggered if the cell traffic is moderately or severely suppressed.
item.name: throughputStatusLBSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable user service selection during load balancing for UEs in camping state. If this parameter is set to Open, based on the value of the lbTraffTypeInd (Traffic Type Selection Indication for Load Balance) parameter, UEs in camping state that have subscribed to specified services are selected for load balancing. If this parameter is set to Close, user service selection is not performed during load balancing for UEs in camping state.
item.name: clbTraffTypeSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the cell range of intra-RAT load balancing. If this parameter is set to 1 (IntraSector), the target cells for intra-RAT load balancing are intra-RAT neighbor cells in the same sector. If this parameter is set to 2 (IntraEnb), the target cells for intra-RAT load balancing are intra-RAT neighbor cells in the same eNodeB. If this parameter is set to 3 (NotLimit), the target cells for intra-RAT load balancing are all the intra-RAT neighbor cells. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the policy for controlling the cell range of intra-RAT load balancing is invalid.
item.name: intraLBRangeCtrlStgy

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the priority-based frequency selection policy through intra-LTE Camping Load Balancing (CLB). It is used to determine whether to enable the frequency reselection priority setting policy based on CLB frequency priorities. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), a frequency with a higher intra-LTE CLB frequency selection priority has a higher CLB frequency reselection priority. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the frequency reselection priority is set based on the number of low-load neighbor cells on intra-LTE frequencies. In this case, a frequency where there are more intra-LTE low-load neighbor cells has a higher CLB frequency reselection priority.
item.name: intraCLBFreqPrioritySwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of SINR of a single RB. It is used for selecting UEs with poor uplink channel quality for load balancing. If the uplink SINR of a single RB for a UE is smaller than the parameter value, the uplink channel quality of the UE is identified to be poor. Migrating such UEs out of the serving cell can improve the indicators of the serving cell.
item.name: lBPoorSglRBSINRThrd

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables load balancing based on IP throughput. It is used to control whether to use IP throughput as a reference indicator for load balancing if connection-based load balancing and camping-based load balancing are enabled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the IP throughput of cells is used to trigger connection-based load balancing and camping-based load balancing. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the mode configured by the loadTriggerMode (Trigger Mode of Load Balance) parameter is used to trigger connection-based load balancing and camping-based load balancing.
item.name: thrpLBSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the thresholds for triggering connection-based IP throughput balancing and camping-based IP throughput balancing in the serving cell. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. Element 0 and element 1 respectively set the thresholds for triggering uplink and downlink IP throughput balancing. If the thrpLBSwch (Switch of Load Balancing Based on IP Throughput) parameter is set to 1 (Open) and the uplink IP throughput of the serving cell is smaller than the value of element 0 of this parameter, the conditions for triggering uplink connection-based IP throughput balancing and camping-based IP throughput balancing are met. If the downlink IP throughput of the serving cell is smaller than the value of element 1 of this parameter, the conditions for triggering downlink connection-based IP throughput balancing and camping-based IP throughput balancing are met. If an element is set to 65535, it indicates that the corresponding uplink or downlink IP throughput always meets the conditions for triggering connection-based IP throughput balancing and camping-based IP throughput balancing.
item.name: thrpLBSrvTrigThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the relative gain thresholds of neighbor cells for IP throughput balancing. It is used to check whether a neighbor cell can be used as a target cell for IP throughput balancing. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. Element 0 and element 1 respectively set the relative gain thresholds for uplink and downlink IP throughput balancing. Suppose that X = (uplink IP throughput of a neighbor cell - uplink IP throughput of the serving cell)/uplink IP throughput of the serving cell. If X is smaller than the value of element 0, the neighbor cell cannot be used as the target cell for uplink IP throughput balancing of the serving cell. Suppose that Y = (downlink IP throughput of a neighbor cell - downlink IP throughput of the serving cell)/downlink IP throughput of the serving cell. If Y is smaller than the value of element 1, the neighbor cell cannot be used as the target cell for downlink IP throughput balancing of the serving cell. If element 0 or element 1 is set to 65535, it indicates that all the neighbor cells always meet the uplink or downlink relative gain requirements and can be used as the target cells for uplink or downlink IP throughput balancing.
item.name: thrpLBNbrRelThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the absolute thresholds of neighbor cells for IP throughput balancing. It is used to check whether a neighbor cell can be used as a target cell for IP throughput balancing. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. Element 0 and element 1 respectively set the absolute thresholds for uplink and downlink IP throughput balancing. If the uplink IP throughput of a neighbor cell is smaller than the value of element 0, the neighbor cell cannot be used as the target cell for uplink IP throughput balancing of the serving cell. If the downlink IP throughput of a neighbor cell is smaller than the value of element 1, the neighbor cell cannot be used as the target cell for downlink IP throughput balancing of the serving cell.
item.name: thrpLBNbrAbsThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets a list of QCIs of the services that cannot be involved in load balancing. A maximum of 64 elements can be configured. If a UE uses the services that correspond to the QCIs in the list, it cannot be selected as the migration candidate for connection load balancing or camping load balancing.
item.name: lBForbidTraffQciList

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to filter large-packet UEs if load balancing is enabled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Filters uplink large-packet UEs), no uplink large-packet UE is migrated for load balancing. If this parameter is set to 2 (Filters downlink large-packet UEs), no downlink large-packet UE is migrated for load balancing. If this parameter is set to 3 (Filters uplink and downlink large-packet UEs), neither uplink large-packet UE nor downlink large-packet UE is migrated for load balancing. If this parameter is set to 0 (Large-packet users are not filtered), no large-packet UE is migrated for load balancing.
item.name: lBLargePakFilterInd

item.desc: This parameter sets the timer for waiting for a load balancing measurement report. After the measurement configuration information about load balancing is delivered, this timer is started to wait for a measurement report. When the timer expires, the measurement configuration information is deleted. Note: If this parameter is set to 65535, for a UE for which the measurement configuration information about load balancing has been delivered, the measurement configuration information is not deleted within the current measurement period. If the UE is not selected to be migrated in the next period for load balancing, the measurement configuration information is deleted.
item.name: lBMeasDelWaitTimer

item.desc: Full Distinguished Name
item.name: FDN

item.desc: Date Time
item.name: DATETIME

item.desc: Collection period of measurement task.
item.name: granularityPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.
item.name: id

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.
item.name: moId

item.desc: The parameter is used to set IMMCI based on load control.
item.name: loadCtrlSwchBasedIMMCI

item.desc: If switch of load control based on IMMCI is Open,eNodeb will trigger IMMCI when load exceed IMMCI threshold of Load Control.
item.name: loadCtrlThrdBasedIMMCI

item.desc: for the purpose of load reduction ctrl of CC board hardware or BPL, eNB config some UEs with 'IdleModeMobilityControlInfo' ,which is being included the RRCConnectionRelease message. If IMMCI trigged by CC Hardware function works, the relative parameters of CC Hardware are equivalent to Hardware trigger threshold of CC board for the adjustment of ac-barring factors,Hardware recover threshold of CC board for the adjustment of ac-barring factors,Hardware hysteresis of CC board for the adjustment of ac-barring factors,Estimation window for hardware usage of CC board for the adjustment of AC-Barring
item.name: immciMode

item.desc: Ratio increment for IMMCI users once a higher load level happens in the next load estimation period.
item.name: immciStep

item.desc: This parame indicates whether the current frequency or RAT is to be de-prioritised.
item.name: deprioritisation

item.desc: The parameter represents the idle mobility profile index.
item.name: refIdleMobilityProfileLTE

item.desc: This switch determine whether user number ratio function is valid or not.
item.name: userNumberRatioSwch

item.desc: This switch determine whether prb usage ratio function is valid or not.
item.name: prbUsgeRatioSwch

item.desc: This parameter is used to define PRB congestion threshold in PRB usage ratio procedure.
item.name: prbCongThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to define time of duration for PRB congestion threshold in PRB usage ratio procedure.
item.name: timerOfPRBCongThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to define PRB Admission control threshold in PRB usage ratio procedure.
item.name: prbAdmitThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to define time of duration for PRB Admission control threshold in PRB usage ratio procedure.
item.name: timerOfPRBAdmitThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to PRB recovery threshold in PRB usage ratio procedure.
item.name: prbRecoverThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to recovery threshold in load control procedure.
item.name: timerofRecoverThrd

item.desc: This parameter is used to limit the validity of deprioritisation.
item.name: deprioritisationTimer

item.desc: For this parameter and User ratio hysteresis for the adjustment of AC barring parameter,once the User ratio load is greater than the sum of two, the launch of the downward adjustment of ac-BarringFactor begins and contiues untill the User ratio load is less than or equal to this parameter, or the ac-BarringFactor reaches its low limit. While ,once the User ratio load is lower than their difference,the launch of the upward adjustment of ac-BarringFactor begins and contiues untill the User ratio load is greater than or equal to this parameter,or the ac-BarringFactor reaches the upper limit of 1.
item.name: acbRRCRatioThrsh

item.desc: For this parameter and Hardware trigger threshold of CC board for the adjustment of AC barring parameter,once the CC hardware load is greater than the sum of two, the launch of the downward adjustment of ac-BarringFactor begins and contiues untill the CC hardwared load is less than or equal to the later, or the ac-BarringFactor reaches its low limit. While ,once the CC hardware load is lower than their difference,the launch of the upward adjustment of ac-BarringFactor begins and contiues untill the CC hardwared load is greater than or equal to the later,or the ac-BarringFactor reaches the upper limit of 1.
item.name: acbRRCRatioHys

item.desc: User ratio load estimation window for the adjustment of AC barring parameter.
item.name: acbRRCRatioLoadWin

item.desc: This switch determine whether PRB congestion control function is valid or not. If the PRB usage rate is frequently high, consider open the function. If the PRB ratio over a threshold, eNB would release some bearer to reduce PRB usage rate.
item.name: prbUsgeRatioCongSwch

item.desc: This parameter indicates the period of release bearer for PRB congestion control. If it is configured too long, the effect of reducing PRB load is small.
item.name: prbCongRelBearPeriod

item.desc: This parameter indicates the number of release bearers in a period for PRB congestion control. If it is configured too big, the number of release bearers is too much.
item.name: prbCongRelBearNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the QCIs of the bearers that can be released in PRB usage-based congestion control. It is an array parameter consisting of nine elements. The first through ninth elements respectively indicate whether the bearers with QCI1 through QCI9 can be released. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the bearer with a QCI corresponding to the element can be released. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the bearer with a QCI corresponding to the element cannot be released.
item.name: prbCongRelBearInd

item.desc: This switch determine whether PRB admission control function is valid or not. If open, eNB can decide whether access a new bearer depend on the surplus PRB resource.
item.name: prbUsgeRatioACSwch

item.desc: This parameter indicates maximum number of low priority bearers can be preempted for high priority bearer when the high priority bearer is admitted fail.
item.name: prbACPreeMaxBearNum

item.desc: This parameter sets the QCIs of the bearers that can be preempted in PRB usage-based admission control. It is an array parameter consisting of nine elements. The first through ninth elements respectively indicate whether the bearers with QCI1 through QCI9 can be preempted. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the bearer with a QCI corresponding to the element can be preempted. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the bearer with a QCI corresponding to the element cannot be preempted.
item.name: prbACRelBearInd

item.desc: This parameter is the trigger threshold of self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. This parameter and Self-Adaptive IMMCI Trigger Hysteresis for Congestion Control Based on CC Load are used to calculate the threshold of adjust IMMCI factor.
item.name: conIMMCICCLoadThrd

item.desc: This parameter is the trigger threshold of self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. This parameter and self-adaptive IMMCI trigger hysteresis for congestion control based on ratio of user number are used to calculate the threshold of adjust IMMCI factor.
item.name: conIMMCIRRCRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter is the trigger hysteresis of self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. This parameter and self-adaptive IMMCI trigger threshold for congestion control based on ratio of user number are used to calculate the threshold of adjust IMMCI factor.
item.name: conIMMCIRRCRatioHys

item.desc: This parameter is the trigger threshold of self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. This parameter and Self-Adaptive IMMCI Trigger Threshold for Congestion Control Based on CC Load are used to calculate the threshold of adjust IMMCI factor.
item.name: conIMMCICCLoadHys

item.desc: This parameter is the adjusting step of self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. If it was configured too big, it would change the IMMCI factor faster.
item.name: conIMMCIStepLength

item.desc: This parameter is the trigger mode ofself-adaptive IMMCI for Congestion Control. If open, eNodeB would control the ratioof users carrying IMMCI. Each positionin the bitmap indicates a function entity. Rightmost bit is the first bit.First bit = Self-adaptive IMMCI basedon CC load,Second bit = Self-adaptive IMMCI basedon BPL load,Third bit = Self-adaptive IMMCI basedon ratio of user number
item.name: conIMMCITriggerMode

item.desc: This parameter is the period of self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. If it was configured too long, it would wait much time for changing the IMMCI factor.
item.name: conIMMCIPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the smart network distribution function for SPID users. If the switch is turned on, when a user is released, the user is guided to another frequency in accordance with the load condition of the serving cell.
item.name: sPIDSmartNetDistSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the smart network distribution function for Non-SPID users. If the switch is turned on, when a user is released, the user is guided to another frequency in accordance with the load condition of the serving cell.
item.name: nSPIDSmartNetDistSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the load evaluation period of the smart network distribution function for idle users. The larger the parameter value is, the longer the load evaluation period is. The smaller the parameter value is, the shorter the load evaluation period is.
item.name: smartNetDistLoadEvaPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the delayed release time of the smart network distribution function for idle SPID users. The larger the parameter value is, the longer the delayed release time is. The smaller the parameter value is, the shorter the delayed release time is.
item.name: sPIDSmtNetDistDeyRelTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the load decision thresholds for smart idle-UE distribution. It is an array parameter consisting of three elements. If the number of UEs in a cell is smaller than the value of the first element, the cell load is considered to be low. If the number of UEs in a cell is larger than or equal to the value of the first element and smaller than the value of the second element, the cell load is considered to be medium. If the number of UEs in a cell is larger than or equal to the value of the second element and smaller than the value of the third element, the cell load is considered to be high. If the number of UEs in a cell is larger than or equal to the value of the third element, the cell is considered to be overloaded. The UE camping policies that can take effect vary with the cell load levels and are used to control the distribution of idle UEs between frequencies.
item.name: smartNetDistLoadThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the IMMCI profile index for releasing SPID users and non-SPID users when the serving cell is overloaded.
item.name: ref1IdleMobilityProfileLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the probabilities that UEs carry the two IMMCI profile policies if smart idle-UE distribution is enabled and the cell is overloaded. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. The first and second elements indicate the probabilities that UEs carry the two IMMCI profile policies corresponding to the first and second elements specified by the LoadControlCellFDDLTE. Ref1IdleMobilityProfileLTE array parameter respectively. A larger element value indicates a higher probability that the UEs carry the corresponding IMMCI profile policy when they are released.
item.name: oLIMMCIProfileIndexPro

item.desc: This parameter sets a profile index of the smart network distribution function for Non-SPID users. With a profile index, you can find a configuration for IMMCI for Non-SPID users.
item.name: refSmartNetDistLTE

item.desc: This parameter sets the priorities of the dedicated-reselection and redirection functions. It is an array parameter consisting of 16 elements. The functions corresponding to elements 0 through 9 (the first ten priority values) are as follows in turn: camping load balancing, CA UE-specific reselection priority policy, self-adaptive IMMCI adjustment for congestion control, intelligent-network distribution based on redirection for idle SPID UEs, intelligent-network distribution based on IMMCI for idle SPID UEs/SPID-based idle-mode mobility control, intelligent-network distribution for idle non-SPID UEs, EN-DC carrier anchoring in IMMCI/directional reselection of SA UEs in IMMCI, customized UE-specific IMMCI, MM network coordination based on UE migration in IMMCI, and IMMCI based on special UEs. A larger element value indicates a higher priority of the corresponding function. Elements 10 through 15 are reserved.
item.name: ieUserDisFuncPriDl

item.desc: This parameter indicates the statistical time window length of each sampling point in the RRC rejection ratio-based AC barring function. It is used to calculate the RRC rejection ratio.
item.name: aCBMsg3RejLoadWin

item.desc: During the Observation Window of RRC Rejection Ratio for the Adjustment of AC Barring Parameter, if the sampling values of the cell RRC rejection ratio are always larger than or equal to RRC Rejection Ratio Trigger Threshold for the Adjustment of AC Barring Parameter+RRC Rejection Ratio Hysteresis for the Adjustment of the AC Barring Parameter and if the number of RRC requests is larger than or equal to the value of this parameter, the AC barring control function based on the RRC rejection ratio will be triggered. This parameter is used to prevent the AC barring control function from being improperly triggered due to the number of RRC requests being too small during the Observation Window of RRC Rejection Ratio for the Adjustment of AC Barring Parameter. However, the parameter value cannot be too large; otherwise, it will be hard to trigger the AC barring control function.
item.name: aCBMsg3RejUEAtmptNum

item.desc: In the observation window configured by this parameter, if the cell RRC rejection ratio of sampling points is always greater than or equal to the value of RRC Rejection Ratio Trigger Threshold for the Adjustment of AC Barring Parameter+RRC Rejection Ratio Hysteresis for the Adjustment of the AC Barring Parameter and the number of RRC requests is greater than or equal to Number of RRC Connection Attempts for AC Barring Parameter Adjustment, RRC rejection ratio-based dynamic AC barring is triggered. If the cell RRC rejection ratio of sampling points is always less than or equal to the value of RRC Rejection Ratio Trigger Threshold for the Adjustment of the AC Barring Parameter-RRC Rejection Ratio Hysteresis for the Adjustment of the AC Barring Parameter, user access barring is gradually reduced.
item.name: acbTrigMsg3RejRaGuTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the RRC rejection ratio trigger threshold for the adjustment of AC barring. It works with the RRC Rejection Ratio Hysteresis For The Adjustment Of AC Barring Parameter. The trigger threshold is equal to RRC rejection ratio trigger threshold for the adjustment of AC barring + RRC rejection ratio hysteresis for the adjustment of AC barring. The suppression threshold is equal to RRC rejection ratio trigger threshold for the adjustment of AC barring. The recovery threshold is equal to RRC rejection ratio trigger threshold for the adjustment of AC barring - RRC rejection ratio hysteresis for the adjustment of AC barring.
item.name: aCBMsg3RejRatioThrsh

item.desc: This parameter sets the RRC rejection ratio hysteresis for the adjustment of AC barring. It works with the RRC Rejection Ratio Trigger Threshold For The Adjustment Of AC Barring Parameter. The trigger threshold is equal to RRC rejection ratio trigger threshold for the adjustment of AC barring + RRC rejection ratio hysteresis for the adjustment of AC barring. The suppression threshold is equal to RRC rejection ratio trigger threshold for the adjustment of AC barring. The recovery threshold is equal to RRC rejection ratio trigger threshold for the adjustment of AC barring - RRC rejection ratio hysteresis for the adjustment of AC barring.
item.name: aCBMsg3RejRatioHys

item.desc: This parameter is the RAT priority of self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. It defines an array with seven elements that correspond to the priorities of the EUTRA-FDD, EUTRA-TDD, GERAN, UTRA-FDD, UTRA-TDD, CDMA2000-HRPD, and CDMA2000-1xRTT systems respectively. The priority of each system ranges from 0 to 255. A higher value indicates a higher priority. The value 0 indicates that the RAT is not selected as the target system for IMMCI.
item.name: conIMMCIRATPriority

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables self-adaptive IMMCI UE filtering for congestion control. If it is set to Open, high-priority UEs are filtered out and do not perform self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control.
item.name: conImmciUeFilterSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the dynamic adjustment of AC Barring parameters of eMTC UEs based on the number of eMTC UEs in a cell. When the number of eMTC UEs is large, the access of eMTC UEs is restricted through AC barring. When the number of eMTC UEs is restored to a lower level, the access restriction is gradually reduced.
item.name: eMTCACBRRCRatioSwch

item.desc: In the dynamic adjustment of AC Barring parameters, this parameter sets the length of the time window for load evaluation of the number of eMTC UEs. The load is evaluated based on the average value of the sampling points in the time window.
item.name: eMTCACBRRCRatioLoadWin

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval during which the AC barring parameters of the same type in eMTC SIB2 are not allowed to be updated since the last update.
item.name: eMTCACBUpdInterval

item.desc: This parameter is used in conjunction with the Hysteresis to Trigger the Dynamic Adjustment of AC Barring Parameters Based on the Number of eMTC UEs parameter. If the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is greater than the sum of the two parameter values, the ac-BarringFactor field in eMTC SIB2 starts to decrease until the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is smaller than or equal to this parameter value, or the ac-BarringFactor field decreases to the lower limit. If the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is smaller than the difference of the two parameter values, the ac-BarringFactor field in eMTC SIB2 starts to increase until the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is higher than or equal to this parameter value, or the ac-BarringFactor field increases to the upper limit (1).
item.name: eMTCACBRRCRatioThrsh

item.desc: This parameter is used in conjunction with the Threshold to Trigger the Dynamic Adjustment of AC Barring Parameters Based on the Number of eMTC UEs parameter. If the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is greater than the sum of the two parameter values, the ac-BarringFactor field in eMTC SIB2 starts to decrease until the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is smaller than or equal to this parameter value, or the ac-BarringFactor field decreases to the lower limit. If the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is smaller than the difference of the two parameter values, the ac-BarringFactor field in eMTC SIB2 starts to increase until the ratio of the number of eMTC UEs is higher than or equal to this parameter value, or the ac-BarringFactor field increases to the upper limit (1).
item.name: eMTCACBRRCRatioHys

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the forbidding of the access of the LTE UEs of the resource sharing party to anchor cells in a network sharing scenario. To forbid the access of the LTE UEs of the resource sharing party to anchor cells, this parameter should be set to Open; otherwise, it should be set to Close.
item.name: forbid4GSharSwch

item.desc: None. (This parameter is reserved for this version)
item.name: cellReserved

item.desc: This parameter sets the orchestration coefficient for cell orchestration. It indicates the load weight of the current cell. A larger parameter value indicates a higher cell load and a smaller parameter value indicates a lower cell load. If the orcheSwch (Orchestration Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the distribution of cells on the baseband board is calculated based on this parameter value and the cells are established based on the calculation result. If the orcheSwch parameter is set to 0 (Close), this parameter does not take effect.
item.name: orcheNumber

item.desc: This parameter sets the load adjustment period for dynamic network breathing. Within the period specified by this parameter, if the average downlink PRB usage of a cell is larger than the value specified by the NDBDlPrbThreshold (Downlink PRB Usage Threshold for CRS Power Adjustment in Dynamic Network Breathing) parameter, the eNodeB reduces the CRS power of the cell. If the average downlink PRB usage of a cell is smaller than or equal to the value specified by the NDBDlPrbThreshold parameter, the eNodeB recovers the CRS power of the cell.
item.name: nDBPrbPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink PRB usage threshold of a cell for CRS power adjustment if dynamic network breathing is enabled (dynamic network breathing is to dynamically adjust the CRS power of a cell based on the cell load). Within the period specified by the NDBPrbPeriod (Load Adjustment Period for Dynamic Network Breathing) parameter, if the average downlink PRB usage of a cell is larger than this threshold, the eNodeB reduces the CRS power of the cell. If the average downlink PRB usage of a cell is smaller than or equal to this threshold, the eNodeB recovers the CRS power of the cell.
item.name: nDBDlPrbThreshold

item.name: FDN

item.desc: Date Time
item.name: DATETIME

item.desc: Collection period of measurement task.
item.name: granularityPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the string type and can be configured as planned.
item.name: id

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the string type and can be configured as planned.
item.name: moId

item.desc: Together with the QCI and ARP Segment parameters, this parameter identifies a type of UE that does not perform self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. For example, if this parameter is set to 2, QCI is set to 8, and ARP Segment to 1, it indicates that the UEs with the SPID being 2, QCI being 8, and ARP Segment being 1 for QCI8 do not perform self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. If this parameter is set to 0, this parameter is ignored during UE identification.
item.name: sPID

item.desc: Together with the SPID and ARP Segment parameters, this parameter identifies a type of UE that does not perform self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. For example, if this parameter is set to 8, SPID is set to 2, and ARP Segment to 1, it indicates that the UEs with the SPID being 2, QCI being 8, and ARP Segment being 1 for QCI8 do not perform self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. If this parameter is set to 0, this parameter is ignored during UE identification.
item.name: qCI

item.desc: Together with the SPID and QCI parameters, this parameter identifies a type of UE that does not perform self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. For example, if this parameter is set to 1, SPID is set to 2, and QCI to 8, it indicates that the UEs with the SPID being 2, QCI being 8, and ARP Segment being 1 for QCI8 do not perform self-adaptive IMMCI for congestion control. If this parameter is set to 0, this parameter is ignored during UE identification.
item.name: aRPSegID

item.name: FDN

item.desc: Collection period of measurement task.

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.
item.name: id

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.
item.name: moId

item.desc: This parameter enables or disable self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system. If it is set to Open, the load on LTE cells and UTRAN cells is periodically detected and load balancing is executed as required. If it is set to Close, self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system is disabled.
item.name: utraLteSelfAdaptLBSwch

item.desc: This parameter indicates whether an LTE cell is highly loaded. If the ratio of the number of UEs in an LTE cell is larger than or equal to this threshold, the cell load is high. If the ratio of the number of UEs in an LTE cell is less than this threshold but larger than or equal to the value of the Threshold of the Low CU Ratio for UTRAN-LTE Self-Adaptive Load Balancing parameter, the cell load is medium.
item.name: utraLteLBCURatioHighThrd

item.desc: This parameter indicates whether the load on an LTE cell is low. If the ratio of the number of UEs in an LTE cell is less than this threshold, the cell load is low. If the ratio of the number of UEs in an LTE cell is larger than or equal to this threshold but less than the value of the Threshold of the High CU Ratio for UTRAN-LTE Self-Adaptive Load Balancing parameter, the cell load is medium.
item.name: utraLteLBCURatioLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter indicates the optimization amplitude modulation factor of the minimum receiving level RSRP in each period for self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system. The formula is as follows: Amplitude optimized by Qrxlevmin per period = 2 x Qrxlevmin optimization factor.
item.name: utraLteLBRxlevOptFactor

item.desc: This parameter indicates the optimization amplitude modulation factor of the minimum receiving quality RSRQ in each period for self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system; that is, the amplitude optimized by Qqualmin in each period is the value of this factor.
item.name: utraLteLBQualOptFactor

item.desc: This parameter indicates the rollback amplitude modulation factor of the minimum receiving level RSRP in each period for self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system. The formula is as follows: Amplitude rolled back by Qrxlevmin per period = 2 x Qrxlevmin rollback factor.
item.name: utraLteLBRxlevBackFactor

item.desc: This parameter indicates the rollback amplitude modulation factor of the minimum receiving quality RSRQ in each period for self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system; that is, the amplitude rolled back by Qqualmin in each period is the value of this factor.
item.name: utraLteLBQualBackFactor

item.desc: This parameter indicates the maximum value of the minimum receiving quality RSRQ for self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system; that is, the minimum receiving quality RSRQ cannot exceed this parameter value.
item.name: qualOptMaxValue

item.desc: This parameter indicates the maximum value of the minimum receiving level RSRP for self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system; that is, the minimum receiving level RSRP cannot exceed this parameter value.
item.name: rxlevOptMaxValue

item.desc: This parameter indicates the judgment period of self-adaptive load balancing between the UTRAN system and the LTE system. At the end of each judgment period, the related parameters are adjusted, depending on whether the optimization conditions are met.
item.name: utraLteLBJudgePeriod

item.desc: This parameter is the clearing threshold of the subframe counter of NACK. When that counter reaches this threshold, delta MCS should be decreased by delta MCS_Down.
item.name: nackThrsh

item.desc: This parameter is the clearing threshold of the subframe counter of ACK. When that counter reaches this threshold, MCS should be increased by MCS_Up.
item.name: ackThrsh

item.desc: This parameter is the clearing threshold of the schedule subframe counter of NACK. When that counter reaches this threshold, it should be cleared.
item.name: schdNACKThrsh

item.desc: This parameter is the clearing threshold of the schedule subframe counter of ACK. When that counter reaches this threshold, it should be cleared.
item.name: schdACKThrsh

item.desc: Initial DeltaMcs for normal schedule.
item.name: deltaMcsInit

item.desc: This parameter is the adjustment value of Downlink outer-loop AMC Initial value after UE handover.
item.name: deltaMcsAdjust

item.desc: The adjusting step of SINR when received NACK in uplink out loop AMC.
item.name: olAmcNAckStepUL

item.desc: The adjusting step of SINR when received ACK in uplink out loop AMC.
item.name: olAmcAckStepUL

item.desc: Initial DeltaMcs for UL AMC.
item.name: olAmcSNRInitUL

item.desc: This parameter indicates the adjustment value of the converted CQI. When the CQI reported by the UE is converted to the CQI value corresponding to nomPDSCH-RS-EPRE-Offset of 0, the converted CQI value can be fine adjusted based on this parameter value.
item.name: cqiAdjustDelta

item.desc: This parameter is used for CRS-based CQI measurement. The ratio of the PDSCH EPRE to the CRS EPRE is calculated based on PA and this parameter value.
item.name: cqiDeltaOffset

item.desc: This parameter sets the adjustment value of the target BLER for downlink 256QAM. It is used to adjust the target BLER upwards or downwards in the scenario where the downlink 256QAM table is configured.
item.name: deltaBLER4DL256Qam

item.desc: In the uplink AMC optimization of a high-speed rail scenario, this parameter sets the step for adjusting the SINR based on the received ACK messages for uplink outer-loop AMC when the UE is in a positive frequency offset area.
item.name: hstAMCUlPostiveFreqACK

item.desc: In the uplink AMC optimization of a high-speed rail scenario, this parameter sets the step for adjusting the SINR based on the received ACK messages for uplink outer-loop AMC when the UE is in a negative frequency offset area.
item.name: hstAMCUlNegtiveFreqACK

item.desc: In the uplink AMC optimization of a high-speed rail scenario, this parameter sets the step for adjusting the SINR based on the received NACK messages for uplink outer-loop AMC when the UE is in a positive frequency offset area.
item.name: hstAMCUlPostiveFreqNACK

item.desc: In the uplink AMC optimization of a high-speed rail scenario, this parameter sets the step for adjusting the SINR based on the received NACK messages for uplink outer-loop AMC when the UE is in a negative frequency offset area.
item.name: hstAMCUlNegtiveFreqNACK

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables uplink cell-specific AMC. Uplink cell-specific AMC can be enabled if the radio channel quality of all the UEs in a cell is the same.
item.name: amcCellSwch

item.desc: This parameter adjusts the outer-loop tracing speed in an atmospheric ducting scenario.
item.name: atmosDeltaSinrStepFactor

item.desc: This parameter is used to eliminate the untrusted CQI value caused by false detection. When turned on, the proportion of CQI greater than or equal to 7 can be improved.
item.name: cQIFalseDetcSwch

item.desc: This parameter is used to compensate the difference between the real CQI and the UE measured CQI value under the non-standard bandwidth. When turned on, the proportion of CQI greater than or equal to 7 can be improved.
item.name: cQIRepSwch4nonStdBW

item.desc: This parameter determines whether to configure differentiated downlink AMC parameters for UEs with the general QoS. If this parameter is set to Open, the identified UEs of general QoS type can be configured by using the downlink differentiated AMC parameters. In this way, the perception of the users with a specific type of service can be improved.
item.name: dlAmc4GeneralQoSswch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for clearing the downlink outer-loop AMC NACK counter for UEs with the general QoS. When the NACK counter reaches the threshold, the outer-loop AMC quantity is decremented by one step; that is, the outer-loop MCS is reduced by one order. If the inner-loop MCS remains unchanged, the scheduling MCS is reduced by one order.
item.name: nACKThrsh4QoS

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for clearing the downlink outer-loop AMC ACK counter for UEs with the general QoS. When the ACK counter reaches the threshold, the outer-loop AMC quantity is incremented by one step; that is, the outer-loop MCS is increased by one order. If the inner-loop MCS remains unchanged, the scheduling MCS is increased by one order.
item.name: aCKThrsh4QoS

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for clearing the counter for the number of times that downlink outer-loop AMC NACK messages are scheduled for UEs with the general QoS. When the counter value reaches the window length, the counter for the number of times that downlink outer-loop AMC NACK messages are scheduled is cleared.
item.name: schdNACKThrsh4QoS

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for clearing the counter for the number of times that downlink outer-loop AMC ACK messages are scheduled for UEs with the general QoS. When the counter value reaches the window length, the counter for the number of times that downlink outer-loop AMC ACK messages are scheduled is cleared.
item.name: schdACKThrsh4QoS

item.desc: This parameter sets the initial delta MCS value normally scheduled for UEs with the general QoS. It is used to update and maintain the initial outer-loop MCS value after a UE is handed over to a neighbor cell or the transmission mode is changed.
item.name: deltaMcsInit4QoS

item.desc: This parameter sets the adjustment quantity of the initial-value of downlink outer-loop AMC for QoS-guaranteed UEs after handover. It is used to update and maintain the initial outer-loop MCS value after a UE is handed over to a neighbor cell.
item.name: deltaMcsAdjust4QoS

item.desc: This parameter sets the step for SINR adjustment based on received NACK messages for uplink outer-loop AMC for UEs with the general QoS. It is configured to adjust the BLER for the guaranteed UEs with the general QoS. If it is set to a smaller value, the target BLER is higher. If it is set to a larger value, the target BLER is lower.
item.name: ulOlAmcNackStep4QoS

item.desc: This parameter sets the step for SINR adjustment based on received ACK messages for uplink outer-loop AMC for UEs with the general QoS. It is configured to adjust the BLER for the guaranteed UEs with the general QoS. If it is set to a larger value, the target BLER is higher. If it is set to a smaller value, the target BLER is lower.
item.name: ulOlAmcAckStep4QoS

item.desc: The rate measurement software for SA or NSA UEs can identify and optimize the ramping phase. This parameter sets the downlink target BLER in the ramping phase. For the adjustment details, refer to the adjustment rules.
item.name: lteBlerForType6

item.desc: This parameter controls whether the UL PHR is always valid for LTE split bearers. When all UL services are distributed to the NR side through split bearers, there are no UL services on the LTE side. Therefore, the PHRs of UEs cannot be reported for a long time. The UL AMC considers PHRs invalid and may perform some improper procedures, thus increasing the BLER. In this case, this parameter can be used to set the PHRs maintained by the AMC to never invalid.
item.name: pHRInfiniteSwch4Split

item.desc: The parameter sets the conservative MCS quantity for UL SR scheduling in the case of LTE splitting. When all UL services are distributed to the NR side through split bearers, there are no UL services on the LTE side. Therefore, the UL AMC becomes unstable, possibly increasing the BLER. Therefore, the MCS needs to be processed in a conservative manner during SR scheduling, and this parameter controls the specific conservative quantity.
item.name: dltaMcsSr4Split

item.desc: This parameter sets the ACK step of UL AMC outer-loop for LTE split bearers. When all UL services are distributed to the NR side through split bearers, there are no UL services on the LTE side. Therefore, the UL AMC becomes unstable, possibly increasing the BLER. In this case, the AMC BELR needs to reduced. The ratio of this parameter value to the NACK step of UL AMC outer-loop for LTE split bearers is approximately equal to the UL target BLER. You can modify these two parameters to reduce the target BLER.
item.name: ulOlAmcAckStep4Split

item.desc: This parameter sets the NACK step of UL AMC outer-loop for LTE split bearers. When all UL services are distributed to the NR side through split bearers, there are no UL services on the LTE side. Therefore, the UL AMC becomes unstable, possibly increasing the BLER. In this case, the AMC BELR needs to reduced. The ratio of the ACK step of UL AMC outer-loop for LTE split bearers to this parameter value is approximately equal to the UL target BLER. You can modify these two parameters to reduce the target BLER.
item.name: ulOlAmcNackStep4Split

item.desc: This parameter sets the interval for triggering UL AMC pre-scheduling for LTE split bearers. When all UL services are distributed to the NR side through split bearers, there are no UL services on the LTE side. Therefore, the UL AMC lacks of UL measurement values, possibly increasing the BLER. In this case, UL scheduling can be increased by pre-scheduling. The AMC can obtain more UL measurement values and thus can control the BLER more effectively.
item.name: amcPreSchdInterval4Split

item.desc: This parameter sets the target BLER corresponding to the downlink discrete scheduling for the UEs for which split bearers have been established and downlink discrete scheduling is being performed.
item.name: lteBlerForSplit

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the optimization for the initial value of the outer loop of uplink AMC. If it is set to Open, the eNodeB intelligently learns the initial value of the outer loop of uplink AMC and applies the learning result. If it is set to Close, the original default value is used.
item.name: aIDeltaSinrEnable

item.desc: This parameter sets the target BLER for mesh reinforcement learning. The modification of this parameter can adjust the target BLER that can be used after initial access to improve the uplink spectrum efficiency of the cell.
item.name: bLERTarget4Reinforce

item.desc: This parameter sets the MCS threshold for identifying downlink UEs at near points and far points. If the downlink MCS value of a UE is smaller than this threshold, the UE is identified as a far-point UE. If the downlink MCS value of a UE is larger than this threshold, the UE is identified as a near-point UE.
item.name: remoteUserJudgeMcsThr

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables aperiodic CSI reporting after the UEs with the transmission mode being TM4 are initially connected to the network. If it is set to Open, aperiodic CSI reporting is immediately triggered after the UEs with the transmission mode being TM4 are initially connected to the network. In this case, channel quality information can be obtained sooner.
item.name: initRATm4TrigAprdCSISwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the self-adaptation of downlink outer-loop initial values. If it is set to Open, UEs can be configured with different outer-loop initial values based on the channel quality to accelerate the convergence of outer-loop values of UEs. If it is set to Close, all the UEs use the same outer-loop initial value no matter whether the channel quality is good or bad. In this case, there is no guarantee that the outer-loop values of all the UEs can be fast converged.
item.name: dlInitDeltaMCSAdpSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables fast AMC optimization. In the scenarios where small-packet scheduling and continuous increase of outer-loop values of UEs occur more frequently, it is recommended that this parameter be set to Open to improve the actual SE values. If this parameter is set to Open, the outer-loop values can be increased by twice or four times when the channel quality is good, accelerating the convergence of outer-loop values.
item.name: dlFastAMCSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the NACK threshold for fast AMC in a half window. If the NACK value in a half window is larger than this threshold, the increase of outer-loop values in a half window is not allowed. If the NACK value in a half window is smaller than or equal to this threshold, the increase of outer-loop values in a half window is allowed. If fast AMC is enabled and this parameter is set to 0 by default, this threshold can be set to 1 to 10 as appropriate if the SE value is not obviously increased, the BLER is not 5% higher than the target BLER, and the configured ACK and NACK window lengths are larger than 50.
item.name: nackThr4DlFastAMC

item.desc: This parameter sets the outer-loop initial value for far-point UEs. If the self-adaptation of downlink outer-loop initial values is enabled, a higher degree of matching between this initial value and the channel quality indicates that the outer-loop values of far-point UEs converge faster.
item.name: initDeltaMCSFar

item.desc: This parameter sets the outer-loop initial value for midpoint UEs. If the self-adaptation of downlink outer-loop initial values is enabled, a higher degree of matching between this initial value and the channel quality indicates that the outer-loop values of midpoint UEs converge faster.
item.name: initDeltaMCSMiddle

item.desc: This parameter sets the outer-loop initial value for near-point UEs. If the self-adaptation of downlink outer-loop initial values is enabled, a higher degree of matching between this initial value and the channel quality indicates that the outer-loop values of near-point UEs converge faster.
item.name: initDeltaMCSNear

item.desc: This parameter sets the start Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS) value for PCCH scheduling. If it is set to a larger value, the number of RBs used for PCCH scheduling can be reduced.
item.name: pCCHMcsStart

item.desc: This parameter sets the start Modulation and Coding Scheme (MCS) value for BCCH scheduling. If it is set to a larger value, the number of RBs used for BCCH scheduling can be reduced.
item.name: bCCHMcsStart

item.desc: This parameter sets the MCS decision threshold for far-point UEs. It is a two-dimensional array. If the 64QAM table is valid for a UE and the MCS value is smaller than or equal to the first element of this array parameter, the UE is determined as a far-point UE. If the 256QAM table is valid for a UE and the MCS value is smaller than or equal to the second element of this array parameter, the UE is determined as a far-point UE.
item.name: mcsThrFar

item.desc: This parameter sets the MCS decision threshold for near-point UEs. It is a two-dimensional array. If the 64QAM table is valid for a UE and the MCS value is larger than or equal to the first element of this array parameter, the UE is determined as a near-point UE. If the 256QAM table is valid for a UE and the MCS value is larger than or equal to the second element of this array parameter, the UE is determined as a near-point UE.
item.name: mcsThrNear

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of times that a UE configured with the 256QAM or 64QAM table is scheduled before the eNodeB activates or deactivates the 256QAM table. If the number of times that the UE configured with the 64QAM table is scheduled is larger than or equal to this parameter value, the eNodeB determines whether to activate the 256QAM table. If the number of times that the UE configured with the 256QAM table is scheduled is larger than or equal to this parameter value, the eNodeB determines whether to activate the 64QAM table.
item.name: statInterval256QAM

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for the equivalent TB size ratio required to activate the 256QAM table. It is used to determine whether a UE is switched over to the 256QAM table. If the equivalent TB size ratio of the UE is larger than or equal to this threshold, the eNodeB activates the 256QAM table.
item.name: config256QAMThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for the equivalent TB size ratio required to deactivate the 256QAM table. It is used to determine whether a UE is switched over to the 64QAM table. If the equivalent TB size ratio of the UE is smaller than or equal to this threshold, the eNodeB activates the 64QAM table.
item.name: deconfig256QAMThr

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the optimization for the initial outer-loop value of downlink smart AMC. If it is set to Open, the initial outer-loop values of UEs can be dynamically adjusted to accelerate the convergence of the outer-loop values of the UEs. If it is set to Close, all the UEs use the same initial outer-loop value. In this case, the fast convergence of outer-loop values of the UE cannot be ensured.
item.name: aIInitDeltaMcsSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the uplink fast AMC function and the uplink outer-loop AMC attempt function. If it is set to 1 (FastAMC), it indicates that the uplink fast AMC function is enabled. If it is set to 2 (OlAttempt), it indicates that the uplink outer-loop AMC attempt function is enabled.
item.name: ulFastAMCSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables DCI0 loss optimization. It is used to increase the uplink rate in the scenarios where more DCI0 information is lost. If it is set to Dci0lostOlOpt and DCI0 loss occurs, the outer-ring optimization procedure is triggered on the eNodeB side. If it is set to Dci0lostIlOpt and DCI0 loss occurs, the inner-ring optimization procedure is triggered on the eNodeB side. If it is set to Dci0lostIlOlOpt and DCI0 loss occurs, the outer-ring optimization procedure and the inner-ring optimization procedure are simultaneously triggered on the eNodeB side. If it is set to 0 and DCI0 loss occurs, the outer-ring or inner-ring optimization procedure is not triggered on the eNodeB side.
item.name: dci0lostOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter set the outer-loop AMC step coefficient in the case of DCI0 loss. It is used to adjust the NACK step of outer-loop AMC on the eNodeB side when DCI0 loss occurs. If outer-ring AMC optimization in the case of DCI0 loss is enabled and DCI0 loss occurs on a UE when QPSK modulation is used, the eNodeB multiplies the outer-loop NACK step by this parameter value.
item.name: dci0lostNackCoeff

item.desc: This parameter sets the path loss threshold for outer-loop AMC optimization in the case of DCI0 loss. It is used for the eNodeB to determine whether DCI0 loss is considered in the calculation of the outer-loop AMC value. If the path loss of a UE is larger than the threshold and DCI0 loss occurs, the eNodeB updates the outer-loop AMC value. If the path loss of a UE is smaller than or equal to the threshold and DCI0 loss occurs, the eNodeB does not update the outer-loop AMC value.
item.name: dci0lostPLThrd

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the optimization for CQI statistics of sub-bands. It is used to adjust the accuracy of CQI statistics of sub-bands. If it is set to Open, the reported average CQI values of sub-bands are rounded off. If it is set to Close, the reported average CQI values of sub-bands are rounded down.
item.name: subCQIStatisticOptSwch
