item.desc: This parameter enables or disables downlink AMC attempt. If it is set to Open and the channel quality fluctuates greatly, the operator can attempt higher-order MCS scheduling, thus speeding up the convergence of downlink AMC and adaptively adjusting the downlink target BLER.
item.name: dLTrialAMCSwitch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables DTX optimization to identify the DTX information reported by the PUCCH due to burst interference. If it is set to Open, the number of retransmissions triggered by DTX can be reduced and the downlink spectrum efficiency can be improved.
item.name: dtxOptSwch4Pucch

item.desc: This parameter sets the validation type of uplink accurate MCS authorization. If uplink accurate MCS authorization is enabled (the accMCSEnableSwchUl parameter is set to Open) and this parameter is set to All, accurate MCS authorization validates all the uplink scheduling types. If this parameter is set to Pre-scheduling, accurate MCS authorization validates only uplink pre-scheduling.
item.name: ulAccMCSEnableType

item.desc: This parameter sets the difference of the thresholds for starting the outer-loop attempt procedure based on different target BLER intervals. When the consecutive number of received ACK messages reaches the threshold for outer-loop attempt, the outer-loop attempt procedure starts.
item.name: ulDelta4EnterAttemptThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the outer-loop decrease value of uplink AMC. It is an array consisting of three elements and used to adjust the outer-loop value after the outer-loop attempt procedure ends. The three elements respectively represent the corresponding outer-loop decrease values when the outer-loop increase level is 0, 1, and greater than 1 at the end of the outer-loop attempt procedure.
item.name: ulOlDown4AttemptEnd

item.desc: This parameter sets the Spectrum Efficiency (SE) threshold for adaptive switchover between single-stream mode and dual-stream mode in TM3, and controls whether to enable TM3 dual-stream. In TM3, if the SE ratio of the single-stream to the dual-stream exceeds this threshold, the downlink TM3 dual-stream transmission is enabled.
item.name: tM3IntraSEThr

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the outer-loop adjustment optimization in high-speed railway scenarios. High-interference normal mode is applicable to the high-speed railway scenarios where the intra-cell interference is greater than -115 dB and less than -105 dB. High-interference enhancement mode is applicable to the high-speed railway scenarios where the intra-cell interference is greater than -105 dB, thus improving the uplink MCS value of the cell.
item.name: hstOlAdjustOptSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the NI threshold for the outer-loop adjustment optimization in high-speed railway scenarios. In the case that the Outer-loop adjustment optimization for high-speed railway parameter is not set to Close, if the NI value of a high-speed railway cell is larger than the threshold, the eNodeB starts the outer-loop adjustment optimization procedure to increase the outer-loop MCS value of the cell.
item.name: absNiDiffThr4Hst

item.desc: This parameter is used to calculate the adjustment amount for outer-loop control for uplink AMC for a high-speed railway cell. The eNodeB uses the result obtained by multiplying the default adjustment amount that is used for outer-loop control for uplink AMC by this parameter as the new adjustment amount. The larger the adjustment amount, the faster the uplink MCS of the cell is increased.
item.name: olAdjustFactor4Hst

item.desc: This parameter sets the BLER threshold for the outer-loop adjustment optimization in high-speed railway scenarios. If the BLER of a UE in a high-speed railway cell is larger than the threshold, outer-loop adjustment optimization is enabled for the UE to increase the uplink outer-loop MCS value of the UE.
item.name: crcCntsThr4Hst

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink SINR measurement threshold for outer-loop adjustment optimization in high-speed railway scenarios. If the measured uplink SINR value of a UE is larger than the value of this parameter, the eNodeB increases the number of pre-schedulings of the UE for outer-loop control optimization, thus increasing the uplink outer-loop MCS value of the UE.
item.name: puschSinrThr4Hst

item.desc: This parameter sets the pre-scheduling period shortening factor for outer-loop adjustment optimization in high-speed railway scenarios. If the Outer-loop adjustment optimization for high-speed railway parameter is not set to Close, the eNodeB multiplies the default pre-scheduling period by this parameter and then divides the result by 64 to obtain a new pre-scheduling period and uses this period. The smaller the pre-scheduling period is, the faster the outer-loop MCS value is adjusted.
item.name: preSchdPeriodFactor4Hst

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables TM4 2T4T adaptation. It is used to control whether the adaptive switching of antenna ports between 2T and 4T in TM4 mode is supported in FDD. 2T corresponds to 2Port, indicating that only two antenna ports (Port0 and Port1) out of the four ports are used, and Port2 and Port3 are not used. 4T corresponds to 4Port, indicating that all the four antenna ports (Port0 to Port3) are used. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB periodically monitors the cell status (for example, the PRB usage, whether there are weak-field services, and whether MAC addresses are blocked) to determine whether to change the antenna ports from 4Port to 2Port or from 2Port to 4Port. If the antenna ports are changed from 4Port to 2Port, the interference to neighbor cells can be reduced. If the antenna ports are changed from 2Port to 4Port, the user experience can be improved. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the cell does not support adaptive switching of antenna ports between 2T and 4T.
item.name: adapt2T4TSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the PRB usage for antenna port switching from 4T to 2T in TM4 mode. It is used to determine whether antenna ports can be switched from 4T to 2T in TM4 mode. Within the period specified by the wTimeThr4T2T (4T-to-2T Time Window Length in TM4 Mode) parameter, if the PRB usage of a cell is lower than or equal to this parameter value, the cell meets one of the conditions for antenna port switching from 4T to 2T. 2T corresponds to 2Port, indicating that only two antenna ports (Port0 and Port1) out of the four ports are used, and Port2 and Port3 are not used. 4T corresponds to 4Port, indicating that all the four antenna ports (Port0 to Port3) are used.
item.name: prbUsageThr4T2T

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the PRB usage for antenna port switching from 2T to 4T in TM4 mode. It is used to determine whether antenna ports can be switched from 2T to 4T in TM4 mode. Within the period specified by the wTimeThr2T4T (2T-to-4T Time Window Length in TM4 Mode) parameter, if the PRB usage of a cell is higher than or equal to this parameter value, the cell meets one of the conditions for antenna port switching from 2T to 4T. 2T corresponds to 2Port, indicating that only two antenna ports (Port0 and Port1) out of the four ports are used, and Port2 and Port3 are not used. 4T corresponds to 4Port, indicating that all the four antenna ports (Port0 to Port3) are used.
item.name: prbUsageThr2T4T

item.desc: This parameter sets the MCS threshold for the UEs in weak-coverage areas when TM4 2T-4T switching adaptation is enabled. It is used to determine whether the UEs in a cell are in an area with weak coverage. This parameter is an array with two elements that correspond to the MCS thresholds for determining the UEs in an area with weak coverage in a cell when the 64QAM and 256QAM tables are used for scheduling. If the 64QAM or 256QAM table is used for scheduling of a UE and the MCS value of the channel of the UE is smaller than or equal to the first or second element of this parameter, the UE is considered to be in an area with weak coverage. If some UEs with specific services in a cell are in a weak-coverage area, the number of antenna ports configured for the cell cannot be changed from 4 to 2 in TM4 mode. If two antenna ports are used for the current cell, the number of antenna ports configured for the cell can be changed from 2 to 4.2T corresponds to 2Port, indicating that only two antenna ports (Port0 and Port1) out of the four ports are used, and Port2 and Port3 are not used.4T corresponds to 4Port, indicating that all the four antenna ports (Port0 through Port3) are used.
item.name: mcsThr4WeakField

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold (in milliseconds) of the duration for which the MAC layer is blocked. It is used to determine whether the current cell is blocked. If the downlink data cached on the MAC layer can be cleared within the period specified by this parameter, the eNodeB determines that the cell is not blocked. If the downlink data cached on the MAC layer cannot be cleared within the period specified by this parameter, the eNodeB determines that the cell is blocked. If a cell is blocked, the number of antenna ports configured for the cell cannot be changed from 4 to 2. If two antenna ports are used for the current cell, the number of antenna ports configured for the cell needs to be changed from 2 to 4.
item.name: timeThrd4MACBlock

item.desc: This parameter sets the length of the time window for 2T-to-4T antenna port switching in TM4 mode. Within the duration specified by this parameter, the eNodeB evaluates the PRB usage of a cell and weak-coverage condition of UEs, and determines whether the number of antenna ports configured for the cell needs to be changed from 2 to 4 based on the congestion condition of the MAC layer of the cell. 2T corresponds to 2Port, indicating that only two antenna ports (Port0 and Port1) out of the four ports are used, and Port2 and Port3 are not used. 4T corresponds to 4Port, indicating that all the four antenna ports (Port0 to Port3) are used.
item.name: timeThr2T4T

item.desc: This parameter sets the length of the time window for 4T-to-2T antenna port switching in TM4 mode. Within the duration specified by this parameter, the eNodeB evaluates the PRB usage of a cell and weak-coverage condition of UEs, and determines whether the number of antenna ports configured for the cell needs to be changed from 4 to 2 based on the congestion condition of the MAC layer of the cell. 2T corresponds to 2Port, indicating that only two antenna ports (Port0 and Port1) out of the four ports are used, and Port2 and Port3 are not used. 4T corresponds to 4Port, indicating that all the four antenna ports (Port0 to Port3) are used.
item.name: timeThr4T2T

item.desc: This parameter sets the indicator of a key service type. It is used to specify the type of service to be guaranteed if the adapt2T4TSwch (TM4 2T-4T Adaptation Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open). This parameter consists of 16 bits, and the lower seven bits are valid and correspond to Type1 to Type7 from low to high. If a bit is set to 0, it indicates that the service of the corresponding type is not defined as a key service. If a bit is set to 1, it indicates that the service of the corresponding type is defined as a key service.
item.name: keyServTypeSet

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables precise beamforming for TM9 UEs in smart space-division FMM cell groups. If it is set to 1 (Open), precise beamforming can be enabled for the TM9 UEs in smart space-division FMM cell groups. In this case, the traffic of the TM9 UEs in the current cell can increase.
item.name: tM9UePmiEnable

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables interference avoidance optimization for RB position allocation for TM9 UEs in a cell. If it is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB further optimizes the allocation of RB positions for UEs based on UE types to reduce the interference caused by precise beamforming of TM9 UEs to neighbor cells. If it is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB does not optimize the allocation of RB positions for UEs.
item.name: tm9UePmiRBAllocSwitch

item.desc: In the scenarios where UE-level PMIs are used for the TM9 UEs in smart space-division FMM cell groups, this parameter sets the number of beams (among the current 32 beams) that deflect clockwise or counterclockwise. A larger parameter value indicates a larger beam deflection angle for a UE, theoretically lower interference to neighbor cells, and a worse precise beamforming effect for the UE.
item.name: adjustBeamNum

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables uplink MCS optimization. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB allocates more RBs to UEs to reduce the MCS values of the UEs and improve the PUSCH demodulation performance of the UEs.
item.name: ulMcsRbReadjustSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the upper BLER threshold for outer-loop adjustment optimization in high-speed railway scenarios. If the BLER of a UE in a high-speed railway cell is larger than or equal to the threshold, outer-loop adjustment optimization is enabled for the UE to increase the uplink outer-loop MCS value of the UE.
item.name: blerMaxThr4Hst

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of outer-loop adjustment optimization for uplink AMC in high-speed railway scenarios. It consists of three elements and is valid if the hstOlAdjustOptSwitch parameter is set to a non-zero value. The first element indicates pre-scheduling optimization. If it is set to 0, pre-scheduling optimization is enabled. If it is set to 1, pre-scheduling optimization is disabled. The second element indicates whether to enable AMC optimization when a UE is handed over from a CP with lower NI to a CP with higher NI. If it is set to 0, AMC optimization is disabled. If it is set to 1, AMC optimization is enabled. The third element indicates whether to enable AMC optimization if the maximum historical NI of CPs is in the range of -110 dB to -105 dB. If it is set to 0, AMC optimization is disabled. If it is set to 1, AMC optimization is enabled.
item.name: hstOlAdjOptMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum modulation order that can be reduced for the uplink MCS. It is valid if the mcsRbReadjustSwch (Uplink MCS Optimization Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open). A larger parameter value indicates higher PUSCH transmission reliability.
item.name: ulMaxMcsDescendVal

item.desc: This parameter sets the adjustment type of the uplink MCS. It is used to determine whether the MCS is changed when the modulation order is reduced. It is valid if the mcsRbReadjustSwch (Uplink MCS Optimization Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open). If this parameter is set to 0 (MCSAdjustInQAM), the MCS is not changed when the modulation order of the MCS is reduced. If this parameter is set to 1 (MCSAdjustCrossQAM), the MCS can be changed when the modulation order of the MCS is reduced.
item.name: ulMcsRbReadjustMode

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables uplink MCS optimization for the UEs with general QoS services. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB allocates more RBs to only the UEs with general QoS services to reduce the MCS indexes of the UEs, improving the PUSCH demodulation performance of the UEs. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB allocates more RBs to all the UEs to reduce the MCS indexes of the UEs. This parameter is valid if the mcsRbReadjustSwch (Uplink MCS Optimization Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open).
item.name: genQosUeMcsOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the adaptive inter-mode TM4-TM9 handover decision mode. It indicates whether channel quality is used as one of the conditions for determining an inter-mode TM4-TM9 handover. An inter-mode TM4-TM9 handover can be performed as long as one of the conditions is met. If this parameter is set to 0, channel quality is not used as one of the conditions for inter-mode TM4-TM9 handover decision. If this parameter is set to 1, channel quality is used as one of the conditions for inter-mode TM4-TM9 handover decision.
item.name: tM49SwitchMode

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables downlink MCS optimization. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB allocates more RBs to UEs to reduce the downlink MCS indexes of the UEs, improving the PDSCH demodulation performance of the UEs.
item.name: dLMcsRbReadjustSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum MCS index reduction for downlink MCS optimization. It is used to control the maximum reduction of downlink MCS indexes. It is valid if the dLMcsRbReadjustSwch (Downlink MCS Optimization Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open).
item.name: dLMaxMcsDescendVal

item.desc: This parameter sets the adjustment type of downlink MCS. It is used to determine whether an MCS is changed when the downlink MCS index is reduced. It is valid if the dLMcsRbReadjustSwch (Downlink MCS Optimization Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open). If this parameter is set to 0 (MCSAdjustInQAM), the MCSs cannot be changed when the downlink MCS indexes are reduced. If this parameter is set to 1 (MCSAdjustCrossQAM), the MCSs can be changed when the downlink MCS indexes are reduced.
item.name: dLMcsRbReadjustMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage threshold for downlink MCS optimization of a cell. It is used to control whether downlink MCS optimization takes effect. If the PRB usage of a cell is lower than or equal to this parameter value, downlink MCS optimization takes effect. In this case, more RBs can be allocated to a UE to reduce the downlink MCS index of the UE, improving the PDSCH demodulation performance of the UE.
item.name: rbRatioThr4McsAdjust

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of UE for which downlink MCS optimization takes effect. It is valid if the dLMcsRbReadjustSwch (Downlink MCS Optimization Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open). If this parameter is set to 0 (All UEs), the eNodeB allocates more RBs to all the UEs to reduce the MCS indexes of the UEs. If this parameter is set to 1 (General QoS UEs), the eNodeB allocates more RBs to only the UEs with general-QoS services to reduce the MCS indexes of the UEs.
item.name: uEType4McsAdjust

item.desc: This parameter sets the indicators of downlink key service types. It is used to specify the types of QoS services that need to be optimized and guaranteed. It is an array parameter consisting of seven elements. The first through seventh elements respectively indicate whether the services of QoS type 1 through QoS type 7 need to be optimized and guaranteed. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the services of the corresponding type need to be optimized and guaranteed. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the services of the corresponding type do not need to be optimized or guaranteed.
item.name: dLKeyServType

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold for the equivalent TBsize ratio for the handover of UEs in a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG) from TM9 to TM4. In a scenario where CRS transmission corresponds to two antenna ports and the UEs in an SSCG support an RI of 4 at most, if the ratio of the equivalent TBsize of a UE in TM9 mode to the maximum equivalent TBsize of the UE in TM4 mode is smaller than the parameter value, the UE meets one of the conditions for handover from TM9 to TM4.
item.name: sSCGTM94TBSRatioThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the scheduling probability threshold for the handover of UEs in a Smart Space-Division Cell Group (SSCG) from TM9 to TM4. In a scenario where CRS transmission corresponds to two antenna ports and the UEs in an SSCG support an RI of 4 at most, if the ratio of the number of times that a UE in TM9 mode is scheduled with RIs smaller than or equal to 2 to the total number of times that the UE is scheduled is larger than the parameter value, the UE meets one of the conditions for handover from TM9 to TM4.
item.name: sSCGTM94SchedProbThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the low threshold of the TM9 spectrum efficiency gain of UEs for UE handover from TM9 to TM4. It is used to determine whether the UEs in an SSCG can be handed over from TM9 to TM4. If the difference between the spectrum efficiency of a UE in TM9 mode and that in TM4 mode is smaller than this parameter value, the UE can be handed over from TM9 to TM4.
item.name: sSCGTM94GainLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the high threshold of the TM9 spectrum efficiency gain of UEs for UE handover from TM4 to TM9. It is used to determine whether the UEs in an SSCG can be handed over from TM4 to TM9. If the difference between the spectrum efficiency of a UE in TM9 mode and that in TM4 mode is larger than this parameter value, the UE can be handed over from TM4 to TM9.
item.name: sSCGTM49GainHighThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the high thresholds of the TM9 spectrum efficiency gain of UEs for UE handover from TM9 to TM4. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Elements 0 and 1 set the high thresholds of the TM9 spectrum efficiency gain of UEs for UE handover from TM4 to TM9 if the cellRSPortNum (Number of Tx Antenna Port in Cell) parameter is set to 2 (indicating 2-port scenarios) and 4 (indicating 4-port scenarios) respectively and are used to determine whether the UEs in SSCGs can be handed over from TM4 to TM9 in the two scenarios. If the tM9UePmiEnable (Precise Beamforming Switch for TM9 UEs in Smart Space-Division FMM Cell Groups) parameter is set to 1 (Open) and the difference between the spectrum efficiency of a UE in TM9 mode and that in TM4 mode is smaller than the value of element 0 or 1 of this parameter, the UE can be handed over from TM4 to TM9 in the corresponding scenario.
item.name: sSCGUEPMITM49GainHighThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the low thresholds of the TM9 spectrum efficiency gain of UEs for UE handover from TM9 to TM4. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Elements 0 and 1 set the low thresholds of the TM9 spectrum efficiency gain of UEs for UE handover from TM9 to TM4 if the cellRSPortNum (Number of Tx Antenna Port in Cell) parameter is set to 2 (indicating 2-port scenarios) and 4 (indicating 4-port scenarios) respectively. They are used to determine whether the UEs in SSCGs can be handed over from TM9 to TM4 in the two scenarios. If the tM9UePmiEnable (Precise Beamforming Switch for TM9 UEs in Smart Space-Division FMM Cell Groups) parameter is set to 1 (Open) and the difference between the spectrum efficiency of a UE in TM9 mode and that in TM4 mode is smaller than the value of element 0 or 1 of this parameter, the UE can be handed over from TM9 to TM4 in the corresponding scenario.
item.name: sSCGUEPMITM94GainLowThrd

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables downlink AMC optimization in CRS muting scenarios. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the system learns the difference in demodulation performance between muting subframes and non-muting subframes and corrects the MCS indexes for downlink scheduling, improving the average downlink packet error rate and the downlink traffic of the cells.
item.name: mutingDlAmcOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of samples of UEs during initial access in CRS muting scenarios. It is used to determine whether the UEs in downlink AMC grids participate in sampling in CRS Muting scenarios. If the number of HARQ samples reported by a UE after initial access exceeds this threshold, the current number of HARQ samples reported by the UE is used in grid cluster learning.
item.name: initialSampleThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of samples of big-packet UEs in a grid in CRS muting scenarios. It is used to determine whether to collect statistics on the downlink packet error rate in CRS muting scenarios. If the number of samples of big-packet UEs in a grid exceeds this threshold, the statistics on the downlink packet error rate are collected.
item.name: bigPktUeThrdInGrid

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of samples of normal UEs in a grid in CRS muting scenarios. It is used to determine whether to collect statistics on the downlink packet error rate in CRS muting scenarios. If the number of samples of normal UEs in a grid exceeds this threshold, the statistics on the downlink packet error rate are collected.
item.name: normalUeThrdInGrid

item.desc: This parameter sets the conversion coefficient of the beamforming gain between the narrow beams for PDSCH services of TM9 UEs and the wide beams for CSI-RS measurement in precise beamforming for TM9 UEs. It is used to correct the downlink MCS values.
item.name: tM9PdschBfGainFactor

item.desc: This parameter sets the narrow-beam side-lobe suppression index of the PDSCH services of TM9 UEs. It is used to adjust the side-lobe suppression values of beams in precise beamforming for TM9 UEs. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that no side-lobe suppression is performed on beams. If this parameter is set to 1, it indicates that the power of side-lobes reduces by 15 dB. If this parameter is set to 2, it indicates that the power of side-lobes reduces by 20 dB. If this parameter is set to 3, it indicates that the power of side-lobes reduces by 25 dB.
item.name: tM9PdschBeamMaskIndex

item.desc: This parameter sets the filter coefficient of projected-power information calculated based on the channel coefficient H of TM9 UEs in FMM Smart Space-Division Cell Groups (SSCGs). It is used to increase the accuracy of inner-loop value calculation for TM9 UEs in the case that projected-power of SRS, CRS, or CSI-RS resources changes greatly. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that only the historical (instead of the current) projected-power information about the SRS, CRS, or CSI-RS resources is reported. If this parameter is set to 32, it indicates that only the current projected-power information about the SRS, CRS, or CSI-RS resources is reported and the weighted average between the current value and the historical values is not calculated. If this parameter is set to a value (X) in the range from 1 through 31, it indicates that the weighted average between the current value and the historical values is calculated based on the weight X/32.
item.name: sscgFilterFactor

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables precise inner-loop value correction for TM9 UEs in FMM SSCGs. It is an array parameter consisting of three elements.Element 0 enables or disables beamforming gain mode selection in TM4-TM9 handover. If this element is set to 1 (Open), UEs can be handed over between TM4 and TM9 based on the beamforming gain calculated by using the channel coefficient H, so that the channel information of the UEs can be more accurately matched and the TM4-TM9 handover can be more accurate.Element 1 enables or disables downlink inner-loop AMC conversion mode selection for TM9 UEs. If this element is set to 1 (Open), the downlink inner-loop AMC value can be accurately converted based on the channel coefficient H to increase the traffic of the TM9 UEs.Element 2 enables or disables inner-loop PDCCH conversion mode selection. If this element is set to 1 (Open), the inner-loop PDCCH value can be accurately converted based on the channel coefficient H to decrease the DRX proportion of TM9 UEs.
item.name: tm9InnerLoopOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the SINR jitter thresholds for inner-loop optimization. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Element 0 sets the threshold for entering inner-loop optimization. Element 1 sets the threshold for maintaining inner-loop optimization. If the difference between the measured SINR value and the AMC inner-loop value is larger than or equal to the value element 0, high-jitter counting is started in inner-loop optimization. During the counting, if the difference between the measured SINR value and the AMC inner-loop value is larger than or equal to the value of element 1, the counting continues; if the difference is smaller than the value of element 1, the counting result is cleared.
item.name: ulSinrJitterThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the filtering coefficient used to update the AMC inner-loop value in the case that the uplink AMC inner-loop optimization function takes effect, so that UEs can quickly adapt to channel condition changes. The parameter value determines the impact of the SINR value measured on the PUSCH on the update of the AMC inner-loop value.
item.name: filterCoef4UlSinrOpt

item.desc: This parameter sets the path loss threshold for enabling AMC inner-loop optimization for UEs. If the path loss of UEs are larger than this threshold, the inner-loop optimization function is enabled for such UEs, so that the UEs at middle and far points can quickly adapt to channel quality changes.
item.name: plThr4UlSinrOpt

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of consecutive SINR jitters for enabling uplink AMC inner-loop optimization. If the measurement result shows that the number of consecutive high SINR jitters is larger than the threshold, AMC inner-loop optimization can take effect.
item.name: ulSinrJitterCountThr

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables uplink AMC inner-loop optimization. If this parameter is set to Open and the measured SINR fluctuates greatly relative to the uplink AMC inner-loop value, the AMC inner-loop filtering coefficient is adjusted to quickly adapt to channel condition changes.
item.name: ulSinrOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the average beam spacing between TM9 UEs and the TM9 UEs in the neighbor cells in the same frequency domain. It is used to adjust the beams of the current UE. If the average beam spacing between the current UE and the UEs in the neighbor cells is smaller than the threshold, it is considered that the beam spacing between the current UE and the UEs in the neighbor cells is small and therefore there is interference to the neighbor cells. In this case, the beams of the current UE need to be deflected.
item.name: beamIDValueThrd

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables RI restriction during downlink scheduling. It is an array parameter consisting of five elements. It is used to set whether to schedule downlink high-priority packets of the UEs with a specific type of general-QoS service by using the RI being 1. Elements 0 through 4 set whether to enable RI restriction in downlink scheduling of the UEs with general-QoS services of type 1 through type 5. If an element is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB schedules downlink high-priority packets of the UEs with the corresponding type of general-QoS service by using the RI being 1 to reduce the packet error rate of the high-priority packets of such UEs. If an element is set to 0 (Close), the eNodeB schedules downlink high-priority packets of the UEs with the corresponding type of general-QoS service by using the RI that matches the channel quality.
item.name: dlRiRestrictSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the bitmap of general-QoS types. It is an array parameter consisting of six elements. Elements 0 through 5 respectively set whether to decrease the MCS values and increase the number of RBs for the services of general-QoS type1 through general-QoS type6. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that, for the services of the corresponding general-QoS type, the MCS value can decrease and the number of RBs can increase. In this case, the demodulation performance of the UEs with the services of this general-QoS type can improve. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that, for the services of the corresponding general-QoS type, the MCS value cannot decrease and the number of RBs cannot increase.
item.name: uETypeBitMap

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink BSR threshold of the UEs with general-QoS services. For the UEs with the general-QoS services of the type corresponding to the value of element 1 of the UETypeBitMap (Bitmap of General-QoS Types) parameter, if the BSR values of the UEs are smaller than the threshold, the MCS decrease and RB increase function takes effect for the UEs, improving the demodulation performance of them.
item.name: dlUeBsrThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink BSR threshold for making the MCS decrease and RB increase function take effect for UEs. If the BSR value of a UE is smaller than the threshold, the MCS decrease and RB increase function takes effect for the UE, improving the demodulation performance of the UE.
item.name: ulUeBsrThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum MCS values of the downlink scheduling of packets. It is an array parameter consisting of five elements. For the UEs with a type of general-QoS service, this parameter is one of the conditions for deciding whether to restrict the maximum MCS values of the downlink scheduling of the service packets. For the UEs with general-QoS services of type 1 through type 5, elements 0 through 4 respectively set the maximum MCS values of the downlink scheduling of the service packets and are used to reduce the packet error rate of the high-priority packets of the UEs with different types of general-QoS services.
item.name: dlMcsMax4PktOpt

item.desc: This parameter sets the proportions of high-priority service packets. It is an array parameter consisting of five elements. It is one of the conditions for deciding whether to make downlink RI restriction and conservative MCS scheduling take effect for the packets of the UEs with a type of general-QoS service. Elements 0 through 4 set the proportions of high-priority packets of the UEs with general-QoS services of type 1 through type 5 respectively. If the proportion of the number of high-priority packets of the UEs with general-QoS services of a type to the total number of packets in the buffer is larger than the corresponding threshold, downlink RI restriction and conservative MCS scheduling can be performed on the high-priority packets of such UEs to reduce the packet error rate of the high-priority services of them.
item.name: highPrioPktRatioThr

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables DCI0Lost optimization based on SINR measurement enhancement. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open) and the current DCI0Lost detection result is obtained through SINR measurement enhancement, the eNodeB does not apply the PUSCH measurement result corresponding to this DCI0Lost event to the maintenance of the uplink AMC and power control. In this case, in the scenarios where DCI0Lost occurs frequently, the uplink rate of the eNodeB can improve.
item.name: aftEqDci0lostOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the RB allocation policy for interference coordination among smart space-division cells. It is used to control whether interference reduction in coordinated scheduling takes effect through the adjustment of RB allocation between the cells in an SSCG. For the TM4 UEs and TM9 UEs in the overlapping areas of the cells in an SSCG, if this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the RB positions allocated by the eNodeB to TM4 UEs do not overlap those allocated to TM9 UEs to reduce the interference between the TM4 UEs and TM9 UEs.
item.name: fMMIntCoopStrategySwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the PRB usage threshold for allocating RB resources in different frequency-domain positions for the UEs at the edge of neighbor FMM cells. It is used to check whether inter-cell coordinated scheduling can take effect for cell-edge UEs. If the PRB usage of a cell exceeds the threshold, coordinated scheduling can be enabled for cell-edge UEs, so that RBs can be allocated in different frequency-domain positions for the UEs at the edge of neighbor FMM cells to reduce the interference between the FMM neighbor cells.
item.name: prbRatioThr4Overlap

item.desc: Full Distinguished Name
item.name: FDN

item.desc: Date Time
item.name: DATETIME

item.desc: Collection period of measurement task.
item.name: granularityPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.
item.name: id

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.
item.name: moId

item.desc: This parameter sets the conservative value of the CCE aggregation level and power offset of the PDCCH. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. The first and second elements indicate the conservative values of the CCE aggregation level and power offset of data and voice services respectively. During a PDCCH adaptation procedure, the CCE aggregation level and power offset of the PDCCH are obtained based on the equivalent spectrum efficiency of the UE and the first and second elements of this array parameter.
item.name: pdcchConsSwitch

item.desc: In accordance with different actual environments, different CCE aggregation levels and power offsets can be used in control channel conservative scheduling.
item.name: pdcchConsIdx

item.desc: This parameter sets the conservative value of the CCE aggregation level and power offset of the PDCCH when the CFI is 1. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. The first and second elements respectively indicate the conservative values for data and voice services on the PDCCH when the CFI is 1. If the CFI is 1, the PDCCH is likely subject to interference. This parameter can be used to adjust the PDCCH index so that the PDCCH can use a higher CCE aggregation level or larger transmit power, avoiding PDCCH false-detection caused by neighbor cell interference.
item.name: cfi1Cons

item.desc: Suppose that the current CFI is CFI_NUM. Compare the total number of CCEs in the case of CFI_NUM (CCE_TotalNum) with the total number of CCEs in the case of CFI_NUM - 1 (CCE_TotalNum_Low). If CCE_NeedNum is larger than or equal to CCE_TotalNum * ucThrCFIAdapt, CFI is incremented by one. If CCE_NeedNum is smaller than CCE_TotalNum_Low * ucThrCFIAdapt, CFI is decremented by one. Otherwise, the CFI value does not change.
item.name: cfiAdaptThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the CCE resource allocation ratio reserved for the downlink.
item.name: cceOfUltoDL

item.desc: This parameter sets the offset of control channel signaling added based on the PDCCH index in normal UE scheduling.
item.name: pdcchSigCons

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum increase of the PDCCH indexes to exceed the corresponding SE thresholds. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. The first and second elements indicate the maximum increase of the PDCCH indexes to exceed the corresponding SE thresholds of data and voice services respectively. During a PDCCH adaptation procedure, the PDCCH indexes can be obtained from the first and second elements of this array parameter separately.
item.name: pdcchIdxHighLimitdelta

item.desc: This parameter is a compulsory reserved parameter for the UL CCE demand on UL scheduling subframes.
item.name: pdcchUlProtectPara

item.desc: This parameter is the switch of adaptive adjustment of UL and DL CCE resources.
item.name: cceSelfAdpFlag

item.desc: The Maximal Value of PDCCH Adaption Level Index
item.name: pdcchIdxMaxValue

item.desc: The Minimal Value of PDCCH Adaption Level Index
item.name: pdcchConsMinIdx

item.desc: This parameter indicates the power usage offset of the maximum transmit power calculated by the cell against the power available for the PDCCH.
item.name: pdcchPwrPromdelta

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables PDCCH power sharing. If it is set to Open, PDCCH power sharing is enabled. The remaining RRU power (if any) can be used to increase the available power of the PDCCH in the cell to reduce the number of times that the power exceeds the threshold. If it is set to Close, the remaining RRU power cannot be used for power increase of the PDCCH in the cell.
item.name: pdcchPwrShareSwch

item.desc: If the PDCCH Power Sharing Switch parameter is set to Open: If this parameter is set to Open, the radio link performance can be improved by the increase of power offset and the decrease of the number of CCEs allocated on the PDCCH for UEs. If this parameter is set to Close, the radio link performance can be improved by the increase of the power offset of the CCEs allocated on the PDCCH for UEs.
item.name: pdcchDescendIndexSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the PDCCH index increase step for MSG4 scheduling.
item.name: pDCCHStep4MSG4

item.desc: This parameter indicates the initial PDCCH index for MSG4 scheduling.
item.name: pDCCHinitial4MSG4

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of scheduling attempts when the maximum PDCCH index must be used for MSG4 scheduling.
item.name: schCCETime4Msg4

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the PDCCH power priority function. If it is set to Open, the new PDCCH Index table exchanged for primary and effective secondary selection 1 (aggregation level = 1, 2, 4, and 8) is used for CCE allocation. If it is set to Close, the old PDCCH Index table is used for CCE allocation.
item.name: pDCCHPowerPriorSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables CFI adaption optimization. In a high-load scenario, this parameter is set to Open if the proportion of large CFI values is high. In this way, the proportion of large CFI values can be reduced.
item.name: cFIAdaptEnhanceSwitch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables PDCCH optimization enhancement in high-load FDD scenarios. It is set to Open in the scenario where the load is high and the proportion of large CFI values is high to reduce the proportion of large CFI values.
item.name: hiLoadPDCCHEnhanceSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the expansion factor for the number of UEs scheduled in the downlink for CFI estimation. It is used when adaptive CFI optimization is enabled. It can prevent the number of UEs involved in CFI estimation from being too small.
item.name: dlUeNumFactor4CFIAdapt

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum number of UEs that are involved in CFI estimation in the downlink. It is set to Open in high-load scenarios to ensure sufficient number of UEs involved in CFI estimation.
item.name: dlMinUeNum4CFIAdapt

item.desc: This parameter sets the fixed CFI value used when PDCCH optimization is enabled for high-load FDD scenarios. It can be flexibly configured in high-load scenarios.
item.name: hiLoadPDCCHEnhanceCFI

item.desc: This parameter sets the CFI offset of each subframe. It is used to adjust the CFI value of the corresponding subframe. It is an array parameter consisting of 10 elements. The elements in the array parameter represent the CFI offset values of subframes 0 through 9 in turn. To increase the CFI values of some subframes, the corresponding elements need to be set to larger than 0 to increase the number of PDCCH resources in the corresponding subframes.
item.name: cFIValueOffset

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the power increase for VoLTE UEs. To increase the PDCCH power for VoLTE UEs, this parameter can be set to Open; otherwise, this parameter can be set to Close.
item.name: dlPwrPdcchBoostSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum power offset that can be increased for VoLTE UEs. To increase the power of VoLTE UEs, this parameter can be set to a larger value. To decrease the power of VoLTE UEs, this parameter can be set to a smaller value.
item.name: maxPwrPdcchBoost

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables CFI compression. If it is set to Open, the demand for the CFI symbols on all the subframes is reduced to decrease the number of CFI symbols. An appropriate compression proportion of the subframes for common scheduling can be configured by adjusting the Self-Adaption Threshold Coefficient of CFI Symbols on the Subframes for Common Scheduling parameter.
item.name: cFICompressSwth

item.desc: This parameter sets the duration for uplink CCE power compensation. A smaller parameter value can decrease the number of CFI symbols.
item.name: uLCCEPwrAddTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the self-adaption threshold coefficient of CFI symbols. If CFI compression is enabled, a larger parameter value can reduce the number of CFI symbols by proportion on the subframes for common scheduling, thus reducing the number of CFI symbols and improving PDCCH usage.
item.name: cFIAdaptCoff

item.desc: This parameter sets the self-adaption threshold coefficient of the CFI symbols on the subframes for common scheduling. If CFI compression is enabled, a larger parameter value can reduce the number of CFI symbols by proportion on the subframes for common scheduling, thus reducing the number of CFI symbols and improving the PDCCH usage.
item.name: commCFIAdaptCoff

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables uplink CCE power requirement optimization. If it is set to Open when the estimated number of CFI symbols is too large, the uplink CCE power compensation value can be reduced to decrease the number of CFI symbols.
item.name: uLCCEPwrAddPromSwth

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of CFI symbols in CFI self-adaptation. A smaller parameter value can reduce the maximum number of CFI symbols in the CFI self-adaptation procedure to improve the PDCCH utilization rate.
item.name: maxCFIAdapt

item.desc: This parameter sets the self-adaption threshold coefficient of the CFI symbols on simultaneous subframes. In a TDD system, if CFI compression is enabled, a larger parameter value can reduce the number of CFI symbols on simultaneous subframes by proportion, thus improving the PDCCH usage rate.
item.name: symTxRxCFIAdaptCoff

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum number of CFI symbols on simultaneous subframes in CFI self-adaptation in a TDD system. A smaller parameter value indicates a smaller peak number of CFI symbols occupied and a higher PDCCH usage rate.
item.name: symTxRxMaxCFIAdapt

item.desc: This parameter sets the proportion of allocated uplink CCE resources in a DSS time-division scenario. A larger parameter value indicates a higher proportion of uplink CCE resources.
item.name: cceRationOnNR

item.desc: This parameter sets the power increase value for the PCFICH. It is used to increase PCFICH power and improve PCFICH performance in LTE carrier sharing scenarios.
item.name: pcfichPwrEnhanced

item.desc: This parameter sets the power increase value for the PDCCH. It is used to increase PDCCH power and improve PDCCH performance in LTE carrier sharing scenarios.
item.name: pdcchPwrEnhanced

item.desc: This parameter sets the power increase value for the PHICH. It is used to increase PHICH power and improve PHICH performance in LTE carrier sharing scenarios.
item.name: phichPwrEnhanced

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables inter-beam power sharing for the PDCCH in a smart space-division FMM group. If it is set to Open, the PDCCH performance can be improved.
item.name: sSCGPdcchPwrShareSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable PDCCH conversion optimization. If this parameter is set to Open, the eNodeB increases the PDCCH power and CCE aggregation level to improve the PDCCH demodulation performance.
item.name: pdcchConvertOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum number of available PDCCH symbols for CFI adaptation. The larger the parameter value is, the more available PDCCH resources there are.
item.name: minCFIAdapt

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the function of increasing PDCCH resources available for VoLTE UEs. If this parameter is set to Open, more PDCCH resources can be available for VoLTE UEs in the case that CFI adaptation is enabled for the VoLTE UEs.
item.name: volteCFIEnhancedSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the downlink PRB usage for CFI compression. It is used to determine whether CFI compression takes effect. If the cFICompressSwth parameter is set to 1 (Open) and the downlink PRB usage of the cell is higher than or equal to this threshold, CFI compression takes effect.
item.name: cfiComprssDlPrbRatioThr

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to count the number of CCE allocation failures based on the number of available PRBs. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), CCEs are allocated and counted in a best-effort way. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), whether to count the number of CCE allocation failures depends on the number of PRBs available in the current TTI. If there is no available PRB in the current TTI, the number of CCE allocation failures is not counted, reducing the collection of the statistics on the number of CCE allocation failures.
item.name: cCEFailStatBasedPrbSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to add CCEs when CCE allocation fails. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the number of CCEs that need to be added is estimated based on the number of UEs for which resources are successfully scheduled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the number of CCEs that need to be added is estimated when CCE allocation fails.
item.name: cceAddBasedCceFailSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the uplink PRB usage threshold in the case that CCEs are insufficient. If the uplink PRB usage is lower than this threshold and CCEs are insufficient within a period, CCEs need to be added.
item.name: ulCceLessPrbRatioThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the proportion of subframes in the case that uplink CCEs are insufficient. Within a period, if the number of subframes in which CCE allocation fails exceeds this threshold, it is considered that uplink CCEs are insufficient.
item.name: ulCceLessTtiRatio

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink PRB usage threshold in the case that CCEs are insufficient. If the downlink PRB usage is lower than this threshold and CCEs are insufficient within a period, CCEs need to be added.
item.name: dlCceLessPrbRatioThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the proportion of subframes in the case that downlink CCEs are insufficient. Within a period, if the number of subframes in which CCE allocation fails exceeds this threshold, it is considered that downlink CCEs are insufficient.
item.name: dlCceLessTtiRatio

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of RRC-connected UEs for rolling back the maximum PDCCH index of signaling. If the number of RRC-connected UEs is larger than the threshold, the maximum PDCCH index needs to be rolled back to schedule more UEs.
item.name: rRCNumThrForCCE

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum PDCCH indexes that can be rolled back. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. The first element and the second element represent the maximum PDCCH indexes that can be rolled back for non-VoLTE UEs and VoLTE UEs respectively, and are used to adjust CCEs used by the non-VoLTE UEs and VoLTE UEs.
item.name: pDCCHIdxFallBack

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to control the PDCCH demodulation performance in signaling scheduling by setting the maximum PDCCH indexes. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the maximum PDCCH index for signaling scheduling is the value of the maxPdcchIdxForDCCH (Maximum PDCCH Index for Signaling Scheduling) parameter. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the maximum PDCCH indexes for signaling scheduling of non-VoLTE UEs and VoLTE UEs are the values of the first and second elements of the pdcchIdxMaxValue array parameter separately.
item.name: dcchOwnMaxPdcchIdxSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum PDCCH index for signaling scheduling. During PDCCH self-adaptation of signaling, if the dcchOwnMaxPdcchIdxSwch (Switch for Setting the Maximum PDCCH Indexes for Signaling Scheduling) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the PDCCH index cannot exceed this parameter value. A larger parameter value indicates better PDCCH demodulation performance of signaling.
item.name: maxPdcchIdxForDCCH

item.desc: This parameter sets the period for which the eNodeB determines whether CCEs are insufficient. If the CCEs are insufficient in a period, additional CCEs are added in the next period.
item.name: cceLessStatPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the BF gain coefficient of the PDCCH inner-loop. A more-accurate inner-loop measurement value can be obtained by subtracting the BF gain value from the inner-loop value of the PDCCH. Where, the BF gain is the gain of the CSI-RS beams relative to the CRS beams.
item.name: bFgainFactorForPDCCH

item.desc: This parameter sets the period during which statistics on the muting-RBs are collected. If the CRSMutingPDCCHFBSwch (PDCCH Index Decrease Switch in CRS Muting Scenarios) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB collects statistics on the levels of muting-RBs in the period specified by this parameter to determine the values by which the PDCCH indexes decrease.
item.name: cRSMutingRBStatPeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the values by which the PDCCH indexes decrease in CRS muting scenarios. It is an array parameter consisting of twelve elements. It is valid if the CRSMutingPDCCHFBSwch (PDCCH Index Decrease Switch in CRS Muting Scenarios) parameter is set to 1 (Open). Elements 0 through 3 indicate the values by which the PDCCH indexes that correspond to the muting-RB (RBs whose CRS power needs to be muted) levels of 0%, 30%, 60%, and 100% for far-point UEs in turn decrease. Elements 4 through 7 indicate the values by which the PDCCH indexes that correspond to the muting-RB levels of 0%, 30%, 60%, and 100% for middle-point UEs in turn decrease. Elements 8 through 11 indicate the values by which the PDCCH indexes that correspond to the muting-RB levels of 0%, 30%, 60%, and 100% for near-point UEs in turn decrease.
item.name: cRSMutingFBPDCCH

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables PDCCH index decrease. It is used to determine whether to adjust the PDCCH indexes in CRS muting scenarios. If CRS muting is enabled in LTE networks, the CQIs of UEs may be smaller, the PDCCH indexes may be larger, and more CCE resources may be used. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the PDCCH indexes can be decreased by certain values to improve the CCE resource usage.
item.name: cRSMutingPDCCHFBSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to allocate uplink and downlink CCE resources based on subframes in DSS time division scenarios. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), uplink and downlink CCE resources are allocated based on subframes.
item.name: cceTimeDivisionSwitch

item.desc: This parameter sets the downlink CCE proportion in time division scheduling of uplink and downlink CCE resource allocation. It is used to control the number of available downlink CCE resources allocated to subframes. To increase the number available downlink CCE resources allocated to subframes, set this parameter to a larger value.
item.name: cceSubfrmDlRatioOnNR

item.desc: This parameter sets the steps for PDCCH index decrease. It is used to set the values of PDCCH index decrease in the case that consecutive ACK messages are received on the PDCCH. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. Element 1 sets the step for ordinary UEs and element 2 sets the step for VoLTE UEs.
item.name: pdcchDownSteplength

item.desc: This parameter sets the steps for outer-loop PDCCH index increase. It is used to set the value of outer-loop PDCCH index increase. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. Element 1 sets the step for ordinary UEs and element 2 sets the step for VoLTE UEs.
item.name: pdcchUpSteplength

item.desc: This parameter sets the window lengths for outer-loop PDCCH index increase. When the number of times that DTX occurs reaches the parameter value, the PDCCH index increases. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. Element 1 sets the window length for ordinary UEs and element 2 sets the window length for VoLTE UEs.
item.name: pdcchUpWindowlength

item.desc: This parameter sets the window lengths for outer-loop PDCCH index decrease. If no DTX occurs on the PDCCH within the window length, the PDCCH index decreases. This parameter is an array consisting of two elements. Element 1 sets the window length for ordinary UEs and element 2 sets the window length for VoLTE UEs.
item.name: pdcchDownWindowlength

item.desc: This parameter sets the lower limit of the offset for PDCCH index decrease. The total PDCCH index decrease is smaller than or equal to the parameter value.
item.name: pdcchIdxLowLimitdelta

item.desc: This parameter sets the high threshold of the proportion of subframes with insufficient CCEs. It is used to check whether the CCEs allocated to the cell are insufficient. If the number of TTIs in which CCEs are insufficient within a statistical period is larger than the threshold, the CCEs are insufficient.
item.name: cceLessTtiRatioHiThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the low threshold of the proportion of subframes with insufficient CCEs. It is used to check whether the CCEs allocated to the cell are sufficient. If the number of TTIs in which CCEs are insufficient within a statistical period is smaller than the threshold, the CCEs are sufficient.
item.name: cceLessTtiRatioLowThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the offsets to the adaptive CFI threshold for common-scheduling subframes and bidirectional subframes. It is an array parameter consisting of two elements. Element 0 sets the offset to the adaptive CFI threshold for common-scheduling subframes and element 1 sets the offset to the adaptive CFI threshold for bidirectional subframes. The adaptive CFI threshold used for common-scheduling subframes or bidirectional subframes is the difference between the CFI threshold selected for the adaptive CFI threshold and the value of element 0 or element 1 of this parameter.
item.name: cFIAdaptThrOffset

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables adaptive-CFI-threshold selection. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the adaptive CFI threshold is adaptively adjusted based on the CCE allocation failures and PRB usage in the range from cfiAdaptThrd (Threshold of CFI adaption) to cFIAdaptCoff (Self-Adaption Threshold Coefficient of CFI Symbols). If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the adaptive CFI threshold is the cfiAdaptThrd value configured on the UME.
item.name: cFIAdaptThrSelectSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold proportion of remaining RBs in each scheduling subframe. If the ratio of the number of remaining RBs in a subframe after RB estimation is completed to the total number of RBs in the bandwidth is larger than or equal to the threshold, the eNodeB determines that there are insufficient CCEs in the current subframe.
item.name: rbRestRatioThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of RRC-Connected UEs used in large-capacity PDCCH optimization. It is used to check whether a cell is in a large-capacity scenario. If the number of UEs in a cell exceeds this threshold, it is determined that the cell is in a large-capacity scenario and PDCCH resource allocation is optimized.
item.name: pdcchHiLoadRRCNumThr

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to optimize the adaptive PDCCH parameters. In large-capacity scenarios, if this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB reduces the adaptive CCE aggregation level of UEs, thus reducing the probability of CCE allocation failures caused by insufficient CCE resources and power in the cell.
item.name: pdcchAdpParaOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to optimize the PDCCH parameters related to common scheduling in large-capacity scenarios. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB restricts the number of CCE resources used for common scheduling, thus reducing the number of times that CCEs fail to be allocated due to insufficient CCE resources and power.
item.name: commonPdcchParaOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to optimize the adaptive CFI parameters in large-capacity scenarios. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the number of available PDCCH resources can increase, decreasing the number of times that CCEs fail to be allocated due to insufficient CCE resources and power.
item.name: cfiAdpParaOptSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold number of selected UEs with a low CCE aggregation level. It is used to increase the number of selected UEs at medium and near points during scheduling. If the number of currently selected UEs with a low CCE aggregation level is smaller than or equal to the threshold, the number of UEs to be scheduled needs to be increased.
item.name: smallCCENumThr

item.desc: This parameter sets the offset threshold for fuzzy DTX fed back on the PUCCH. It is used to check whether DTX occurring on the PUCCH is fuzzy DTX. If the difference between the DTX proportion fed back on the PUCCH and that fed back on the PUSCH is larger than the threshold, it is determined that the DTX fed back on the PUCCH is fuzzy DTX.
item.name: pucchFuzzyDtxDalta

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to delete fuzzy DTX for outer-loop PDCCH control. It is used to eliminate the impact of fuzzy DTX on outer-loop PDCCH control. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), outer-loop PDCCH control statistics do not include the data of fuzzy DTX fed back by the PUCCH or that fed back by the PUSCH in the case of high interference. In this case, the CCE aggregation level may reduce.
item.name: pdcchFuzzyDtxDelSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the number of selected UEs with a low CCE aggregation level. If the parameter value is larger than 0 and the number of selected UEs with a low CCE aggregation level is insufficient, the eNodeB extra selects UEs with a low CCE aggregation level to increase the number of UEs to be scheduled in the cell. The extra number is the value of this parameter. If this parameter is set to 0, it indicates that no more UE with a low CCE aggregation level is selected.
item.name: cCEAddQosUENum

item.desc: This parameter sets the threshold of the number of CCE allocation failures for the maximum PDCCH index adaptation function. It is an array parameter consisting of three elements and used to control whether to adjust the maximum PDCCH index. Elements 0 through 2 indicate the thresholds of the number of CCE allocation failures for data services, voice services, and signaling services respectively. If the number of CCE allocation failures of services of a certain type is larger than the corresponding threshold, the eNodeB decreases the maximum PDCCH index value for scheduling the services, reducing the number of CCE allocation failures due to insufficient resources.
item.name: cceAllocFailNumThr

item.desc: This parameter sets whether to enable the adaption of the maximum PDCCH index. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB reduces the adaptive CCE aggregation level of UEs, thus reducing the probability of CCE allocation failures caused by insufficient CCE resources and power in the cell.
item.name: maxPdcchIdxAdpSwch

item.desc: Collection period of measurement task.

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.

item.desc: This parameter sets the unique ID of the managed object. It is of the container type and is fixedly set to 1.

item.desc: HARQ has the retransmit mechanism. The parameter indicates the maximum transmit for HARQ and can be configurated different value for different sevice.
item.name: harqMaxTxNum

item.desc: The parameter indicates the timer of periodic buffer status report.

item.desc: The parameter indicates the timer of buffer status report retransmition.
