item.desc: This parameter sets the cell mode of a macrocell. If this parameter is set to 0 (Cell mode 0), it indicates that the current cell uses an 8-antenna mode and a maximum of eight antennas can be configured. If this parameter is set to 1 (Cell mode 1), it indicates that the current cell uses a 4-antenna mode and a maximum of four antennas can be configured.
item.name: cellMod

item.desc: Connected board
item.name: refBpPoolFunction

item.desc: This parameter sets whether the frame header configurations of all the cells on a BP board can be different from each other. If this parameter is set to 0 (Mode0), the frame header configurations of all the cells on a BP board must be the same. If this parameter is set to 1 (Mode1), the frame header configurations of all the cells on a BP board can be different from each other.
item.name: mixMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the scenario mode of a baseband board. It is used to restrict the cell specifications of the baseband board.
item.name: sceneMode

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables the cell orchestration function. If this parameter is set to Open, cells are established on the baseband board based on the configured sequence numbers. If this parameter is set to Close, cells are randomly established on the baseband board.
item.name: orcheSwch

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables CPU core group allocation. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the system can dynamically modify the value of the orcheNumber (Orchestration Coefficient) parameter based on the CPU usage. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the orcheNumber parameter remains default. If the orcheSwch (Orchestration Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the distribution of cells on the baseband board is calculated based on the orcheNumber parameter and cells are established based on the calculation result.
item.name: orcheAdaptiveSwch

item.desc: This parameter sets the period for adjusting CPU core group allocation. If the orcheAdaptiveSwch (CPU Core Group Allocation Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the eNodeB collects data related to CPU usage within the period specified by this parameter, and calculates and updates the orcheNumber (Orchestration Coefficient) parameter.
item.name: orchePeriod

item.desc: This parameter sets the relative threshold for CPU usage. During a period specified by the orchePeriodCPU (Period for Adjusting CPU Core Group Allocation) parameter, for the CPUs in the baseband board core group occupied by a cell, the orchestration coefficient (orcheNumber) is calculated and updated only if the difference between the maximum and minimum CPU usage is larger than this parameter and the maximum CPU usage is larger than or equal to the value of the cpuUsageThrd (High CPU Usage Threshold) parameter.
item.name: cPUUsageRelThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the start time at which CPU core group allocation takes effect. If the orcheAdaptiveSwch (CPU Core Group Allocation Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the system dynamically calculates and updates the orchestration coefficient (orcheNumber) based on the CPU usage of the baseband board core group occupied by the cell. The update time is a random time between the start time specified by this parameter and the end time specified by the orcheEndTime (End Time When CPU Core Group Allocation Takes Effect) parameter.
item.name: orcheStartTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the end time at which CPU core group allocation takes effect. If the orcheAdaptiveSwch (CPU Core Group Allocation Switch) parameter is set to 1 (Open), the system dynamically calculates and updates the orchestration coefficient (orcheNumber) based on the CPU usage of the baseband board core group occupied by the cell. The update time is a random time between the start time specified by the orcheStartTime (Start Time When CPU Core Group Allocation Takes Effect) parameter and the end time specified by this parameter.
item.name: orcheEndTime

item.desc: This parameter sets the upper threshold of the CPU usage. During a period specified by the orchePeriodCPU (Period for Adjusting CPU Core Group Allocation) parameter, for the CPUs in the baseband board core group occupied by a cell, the orchestration coefficient (orcheNumber) is calculated and updated only if the maximum CPU usage is larger than or equal to the parameter value and the difference between the maximum and minimum CPU usage is larger than the value of the CPUUsageRelThrdrelative (Relative CPU Usage Threshold) parameter.
item.name: cPUUsageThrd

item.desc: This parameter sets the application mode of the RFUs of the cell. It is used to configure the baseband resources. If this parameter is set to 0 (Normal mode), it indicates that a single RFU is directly connected to the BBU. If this parameter is set to 1 (Combination mode), it indicates that multiple RFUs are logically combined into one RFU and the number of antennas is accumulated. For example, two RFUs with one antenna each are logically combined into one RFU with two antennas. If this parameter is set to 2 (Mergence mode), it indicates that multiple RFUs are logically merged into one RFU and the number of antennas is not accumulated. For example, two RFUs with one antenna each are logically combined into one RFU with one antenna. If this parameter is set to 4 (Mergence Mode 2), it indicates that multiple RFUs are logically merged into one RFU, the number of downlink antennas is not accumulated, and the number of uplink antennas is accumulated. The parameter value 3 (Mergence mode(PB Networking)) or 5 (Combination mode(PB Networking)) is used in QCell networking scenarios where RFUs are connected to the BBUs through the PBridge devices.
item.name: rfAppMode

item.desc: The Baseband Device for Cable Cascading Connection.
item.name: refBpPoolFunction

item.desc: Used RRU
item.name: refSectorFunction

item.desc: This parameter sets the mapping bitmap of downlink antenna configurations. It consists of 32 elements that indicate whether antenna 1 through antenna 32 of the RFU is enabled respectively. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding antenna is disabled. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding antenna is enabled.
item.name: antMapDlSeq

item.desc: This parameter sets the mapping bitmap of uplink antenna configurations. It consists of 32 elements that indicate whether antenna 1 through antenna 32 of the RFU is enabled respectively. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding antenna is disabled. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding antenna is enabled.
item.name: antMapUlSeq

item.desc: This parameter sets the bitmap of uplink active antennas. It is an array parameter consisting of 64 elements that indicate whether uplink antenna channel 1 through uplink antenna channel 64 is activated respectively. If an element is set to 1, it indicates that the corresponding antenna channel is activated. If an element is set to 0, it indicates that the corresponding antenna channel is not activated. The number of valid elements in the bitmap is the maximum number of antennas supported by an RFU. For example, if the RRU/AAU supports eight antennas, only the first eight elements are valid.
item.name: upActAntBitmapSeq

item.desc: BPL Port
item.name: bplPort

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of 64 elements. The first element through the 64th element of the array parameter represent the mapping relations between antenna channels 1 through 64 and CRS ports separately. If the value of element m of this array parameter is n (the value range of n is from 0 to 3), it indicates that signals of CRS port n are transmitted on antenna channel m. If the value of element m of this array parameter is 15, it indicates that no CRS signal is transmitted on antenna channel m.
item.name: anttoPortMap

item.desc: Control the uplink carrier tilt of AAS, that will affect the coverage area.
item.name: aasTiltUl

item.desc: Control the downlink carrier tilt of AAS, that will affect the coverage area.
item.name: aasTiltDl

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum transmit power that can be used by a CP of a cell.
item.name: maxCPTransPwr

item.desc: The parameter indicates the transmit power of a CP in cell
item.name: cpTransPwr

item.desc: The parameter indicates the transmit power every resource element of cell-specific reference signals of servered CP. The unit is dBm.
item.name: cpSpeRefSigPwr

item.desc: This parameter sets the carrier number of an FDD RRU. It is used to identify the cells configured on the same RRU antenna and is automatically generated by the system. For the RRUs that support dynamic carrier number allocation, the parameter value is a constant (255).
item.name: rruCarrierNo

item.desc: This parameter is the delay adjustment of downlink inter-CP transmission. Only used under highway scenario.
item.name: cpTransTime

item.desc: The Indicate of downlink transmission,Default value is 1,which means the Downlink transmission is work properly.Downlink does not transmit just for special cases of SuperCell
item.name: dlTransInd

item.desc: Cell Manual Operation
item.name: adminState

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of 64 elements. The first element through the 64th element of the array parameter represents the mapping relations between antenna channels 1 through 64 and CSI-RS ports separately. If the value of element m of this array parameter is n (the value range of n is from 15 to 22), it indicates that signals of RS port n are transmitted on antenna channel m. If the value of element m of this array parameter is Not Mapped, it indicates that no CSI-RS is transmitted on antenna channel m.
item.name: anttoCSIRSPortMap

item.desc: This parameter sets whether LTE cells share baseband resources with NB-IoT cells. If the parameter is set to Open, LTE cells share baseband resources with NB-IoT cells. If the parameter is set to close, LTE cells do not share baseband resources with NB-IoT cells.
item.name: lnShareBB

item.desc: When this switch is turned on, new BC weight is generated in accordance with the new algorithm, and periodic round-robin of the BC weight is implemented to keep the balance among RSRPs received by the CPE. When this switch is turned off, BC weight configured in the OMC is used.
item.name: dynBCWeightSwitch

item.desc: Running Status
item.name: operState

item.desc: This parameter is a one-dimensional array with 64 elements corresponding to the 64 channels of the RRU. It is used to limit the maximum transmit power of each channel of the RRU. If an element is set to 1, the power of the corresponding channel cannot be higher than the value of the Maximum Actual Transmit Power of a Restricted Channel parameter.
item.name: limitPwrChannel

item.desc: This parameter sets the maximum transmit power of a restricted channel of the RRU. It is used together with the Power-Restricted Channel parameter.
item.name: maxRestrictedTransPwr

item.desc: This parameter sets the type of fronthaul channel between the RRU and the BBU. It is valid in the case that the fronthaul interface adaptation function is disabled. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), it indicates that the fronthaul channel is IF1 and the data received by the BBU is frequency domain data and DDC data. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), it indicates that the fronthaul channel is IF0 and the data received by the BBU is time domain data.
item.name: iFModeFlag

item.desc: This parameter sets the antenna arrangement type of LTE FDD base stations in 8T scenarios. It is used to set the weight used when the AAU (A9714 or A9714E)/RRU (R9248E or R9248) is connected to different types of smart antennas.
item.name: antType8T

item.desc: This parameter is an array consisting of 64 elements that correspond to the 64 channels of an RRU. It determines whether the power of each channel is involved in power sharing. If the value of an element corresponding to a channel is set to 1, it indicates that the power of the channel can be shared.
item.name: pwrShareChannel

item.desc: This parameter sets the minimum power shared by a single channel in a power-sharing cell. Only the power of the channel for which the value of the pwrShareChannel (Power-Sharing Channel) parameter is 1 can be lent during power sharing. After some power of a channel is lent, the remaining power of the channel must be higher than or equal to the parameter value.
item.name: maxRemainPwr

item.desc: This parameter sets the CPRI compression mode. It is used to determine whether to compress the IQ data of a cell. If it is set to 0 (Normal mode), IQ data is not compressed. If it is set to 1 (Compression mode), IQ data can be compressed and the optical fibers between the baseband board and the RF module can support more cells. In normal mode, the user experience of a cell is better.
item.name: cpriCompressionMode

item.desc: This parameter sets the power offset for dynamic network breathing. It is used to set the maximum increase in the carrier power if the dynamic network breathing function is enabled. If this parameter is set to 0, dynamic network breathing is disabled. If this parameter is set to a value larger than 0, dynamic network breathing is enabled and the eNodeB dynamically adjusts the CRS power of the cell based on the cell load. The maximum power increase of a carrier cannot exceed this parameter value.
item.name: nDBPwrOffset

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables static fronthaul bandwidth adaptation. If the AAU is configured with dual optical interfaces and this parameter is set to 1, a cell can be automatically switched to the optical interface that is operating properly in case that the optical interface that is originally connected to the cell is faulty. When the fault is removed, the cell can be automatically switched back to the original optical interface. In this way, the network services are not interrupted when either of the optical fiber interfaces is faulty.
item.name: fronthaulBWSelfAdaptive

item.name: nDBPwrOffset

item.desc: This parameter enables or disables fronthaul interface adaption. If this parameter is set to 0 (Close), the fronthaul interface mode flag uses the value of the iFModeFlag (Fronthaul Interface Mode Flag) parameter. If this parameter is set to 1 (Open), the fronthaul interface mode flag uses the adaptive value.

item.desc: This parameter sets the MCC in the PLMN ID of the eNB where the CP is located. In an inter-BBU super cell scenario, this parameter can be set in accordance with the network planning to associate the CP to another inter-BBU cell. In other scenarios (namely intra-BBU cell scenarios), this parameter cannot be configured by users, instead, it is set to [255, 255, 255] automatically by the system, indicating the PLMN ID of the eNB.

item.name: cpId

item.desc: This parameter indicates the application mode of the RF unit in a cell. It is set when baseband resources are configured. Normal mode refers to the single-RF unit mode. In Combination mode, two RF units are logically combined into one RF unit, and the number of transmitting and receiving antennas is doubled compared with that of a single RF unit. In Mergence mode, two or more RF units are logically merged into one RF unit, and the number of transmitting and receiving antennas is not accumulated. Mergence mode 2 means that two or more RF units are logically merged into one RF unit. After being merged, the number of receiving antennas is accumulated, and the number of transmitting antennas is not accumulated. The Mergence mode (PB networking) means that multiple Pico-RRUs are merged into one RF unit through PBridge. The number of transmitting and receiving antennas is consistent with the number of antennas supported by a single Pico-RRU. The Combination mode (PB networking mode) is to divide multiple Pico-RRU into two groups. First, the Pico-RRU in the group is merged into one RF unit through PBridge, and then logically combine the two RF units into one RF unit through combined mode. Compared with a single Pico-RRU, the number of transmitting and receiving antennas is doubled.
item.name: rfAppMode

item.name: refBpPoolFunction

item.desc: Used sector.
item.name: refSectorFunction

item.desc: The parameter is the uplink actived antenna bitmap. When this parameter is 0,it indicates that the actived bitmap is the full set of the uplink channels referenced by refSectorFunction. When this parameter is a non-zero value, it must be a subset of the uplink channel referenced by refSectorFunction. Bit0-bit31 represents channel 1-32 respectively. If bit is 1, it means the channel is valid; if bit is 0, it means the channel is invalid.
item.name: upActAntBitmap
